1

Product Description

1.1

Overview
The A733 family features high-performance platform processors targeted for mid-to-high-end
tablets and interactive display applications. It can also be applied in tablet PCs and ARM PCs.
It integrates dual-core ARM CortexTM-A76+hexa-core ARM CortexTM-A55, BXM-4-64 MC1, 3 Tops
NPU, LPDDR4/LPDDR4x/LPDDR5 to ensure rapid response and smooth operation for daily
applications like online video, web browsing, 3D games, and so on.
It supports rich peripheral interfaces including high-speed interfaces such as PCIe3.0 DM, USB3.1
GEN2 DRD, GMAC, video input interfaces such as MIPI CSI and Parallel CSI, and video output
interfaces such as HDMI, RGB, LVDS, MIPI-DSI, eDP1.4b/DP1.4, and E-ink, greatly facilitating
product expansion.
It supports independent/synchronous output on dual display, H.265/VP9/AVS2 video decoding
up to 8K@24fps, H.265/H.264 video encoding up to 4K@30fps, and ISP Allwinner SmartColor5.0
display enhancement technology to provide excellent video experience for users. Besides, the
digital audio interfaces like I2S, DMIC, and OWA enable this chip family to meet the requirements
of mainstream audio recognition solutions.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

3

System Boot

3.1

Boot ROM (BROM)

3.1.1

Overview
The BROM system is actually split up into two parts: FEL and Media Boot. The task of FEL is to
write the external data to the local NVM, and the task of the Media Boot is to load from NVM to
obtain and run an effective and legitimate BOOT0.
The BROM system includes the following features:


Supports the core0 of A55 CPU boot process



Supports Mandatory Upgrade Process through USB or SD card



Supports GPADC to select the kind of boot media to boot



Supports eFuse to select the kind of boot media to boot



Supports Normal Boot and Secure Boot



Supports loading only certified firmware in Secure Boot



Ensures that the Secure Boot is in a trusted environment



Supports cryptographic algorithms

3.1.2

-

ECDSA-256/384/521

-

RSA-2048/3072/4096

-

SHA-256/SHA-512

Security Settings
If the SoC has implemented the ARM TrustZone technology, the SoC will enable the ARM
TrustZone technology when the Secure Enable Bit is enabled. The minimal security functionality,
an ARM TrustZone technology based system, must be implemented for its Trusted Boot.
So the BROM is divided into Normal BROM and BROM Monitor. The BROM Monitor protects
against the potential threat of attackers modifying the areas of codes or data in programmable
memory.

3.1.3

Boot Medium Select
The BROM system supports the following boot media:


SD Card



eMMC



RAW NAND Flash
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

12



UFS



SPI NOR Flash (Quad Mode and Single Mode)



SPI NAND Flash

There are two ways to select the boot medium: GPADC Select and eFuse Select. The BROM will
read the state of BOOT_MODE first, and then select the boot medium to boot according to the
state of BOOT_MODE. The BOOT_MODE is the BROM_Config in the eFuse mapping.
The following table shows the BOOT_MODE setting:
Table 3-1 BOOT_MODE Setting

3.1.3.1

BOOT_MODE[0]

Boot Select type

0

GPADC boot select

1

eFuse boot select
GPADC Boot Select

If the state of the BOOT_MODE is 0, select the GPADC Boot.
If BROM fails to boot from the selected medium, it will try other media with the following priority:
EMMC_USR -> EMMC_BOOT -> SLC_NAND -> MLC_NAND -> SPI_NOR -> SPI_NAND -> UFS
And the medium selected by GPADC will be skipped.
For example, when BROM fails to boot from SPI NOR, it will try other media with the following
priority:
SPI NOR (selected by GPADC) -> EMMC_USR -> EMMC_BOOT -> SLC_NAND -> MLC_NAND ->
SPI_NAND -> UFS

4.1.1

Overview
The clock controller unit (CCU) controls the PLL configurations and most of the clock generation,
division, distribution, synchronization, and gating in CPUX domain. The input signals of the CCU
include the external clock for the reference frequency (26MHz). The outputs from the CCU are
mostly clocks to other blocks in the system.
The CCU includes the following features:

Bus source and divisions



Clock output control



Configurable module clock



Bus clock gating



4.1.3.5

PLL Spreading/Fractional Division
The fractional division is to add a fractional value to the divider N of a PLL to achieve a more
precise frequency configuration. By applying fractional division, the multiplication factor N of the
PLL can be expressed as N.x, where N represents the added fractional value.
The PLL spreading is to add a triangular wave to the N value of a PLL to let the final output
frequency exhibit a triangular wave variation. Spreading parameters consist of spread amplitude
and spread spectrum period. The spread amplitude refers to the range of variation in the output
frequency; while the spread spectrum period is the duration of one cycle of the triangular wave
modulation, whose reciprocal is spread spectrum frequency.
PLL

spreading/fractional

PLLx_PAT1_CTRL_REG;

division

is

configured

through

therefore,

the

generic/linear

PLL

PLLx_PAT0_CTRL_REG
spreading/fractional

and

division

procedures are the same. All the parameters in the two types of registers are divided into static
parameters and control parameters.
Static parameters are used to adjust the order and phase interpolation of the fractional division
loop and don’t support dynamic switching. To alter parameters, disable PLL spreading/fractional
division, configure static parameters, and then enable PLL spreading/fractional division. The
parameters are shown as below.


SPR_FREQ_MODE: SDM mode switching.



PLL_PI_EN: It is used to decide whether to enable phase interpolation (PI) mode.



PLL_PI_CFG: PI circuit current control.



SMOOTH_EN: It is used to enable frequency modulation smooth.



DITHER_EN: It is used to enable dither. When dither is enabled, a pseudo-random sequence
will be added to the frequency modulation curve.

Control parameters are used to control frequency modulation curve and support dynamic
switching. It should be reminded that if the SMOOTH_EN is set, control parameters only can be
switched in the condition that SDM_BUSY is set to 0. The control parameters are shown as
below.


WAVE_STEP: Spreading step. The formula is shown as below.
WAVE_STEP = 2^17*(x2-x1)*2/(Fclk/FREQ)
x2 is the upper limit; x2 is the lower limit; Fclk is the PLL reference clock frequency; FREQ is
the spreading slope. PLL multiplication factors range from N.x1 to N.x2.



WAVE_BOT: Spreading starting point. The formula is shown as below.
for upward frequency spreading, SDM_BOT = x1*2^17
for downward frequency spreading, SDM_BOT = x2*2^17



FREQ: Spreading slope. To dynamically switch this parameter, switch WAVE_STEP at the
same time.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

23

Confidential


SDM_DIRECTION: Spreading direction, including upward frequency spreading and
downward frequency spreading. During upward frequency spreading, the curve starts from
x1 and then adjusts to x2 before reversing; during downward frequency spreading, the curve
starts from x2 and then adjusts to x1 before reversing. To dynamically switch this parameter,
switch WAVE_BOT at the same time.



FRAC_EN: Fractional division enable.



FRAC_IN: Fractional division frequency point. The formula is shown as below.
FRAC_IN = x*2^17

The master switch of PLL spreading/fractional division is SIG_DELT_PAT_EN. It should be
enabled before PLL spreading/fractional division usage.
PLL spreading/fractional division configuration is shown as below.

Linear PLL Frequency Modulation
The linear PLL frequency modulation mode is designed to address the re-locking issue
encountered when switching N values in integer frequency duplication. In this mode, the N value
can be directly configured, and the PLL will smoothly converge the N value to the target
frequency point based on the configured frequency slope.
When configuring linear frequency modulation, static parameters in the fractional divider need
to be set, while the control parameters are automatically managed by the linear frequency
modulation.

4.1.4
4.1.4.1

Programming Guidelines
Generic PLL Frequency Modulation
All the PLLs in the CCMU subsystem are generic PLLs.
Some PLLs are configured to source from DCXO or REFPLL. The frequency of DCXO is same to
that of REFPLL, which can be 24M/19.2M/26M. The actual DCXO frequency can be obtained by
reading the XO_CTRL0_REG (bit[15:14]). The REFPLL frequency is fixed to 24M.
The jitter performance of DCXO is better than that of REFPLL. for the PLLs that have no
requirements on output clock performance, REFPLL is recommended as parameters can be
uniformly configured. for the PLLs that have requirements on output clock performance, DCXO is
recommended; the parameters can be configured based on the frequency switching, and
decimal frequency division can be used in the case that the final frequency cannot be obtained
by integer frequency multiplier.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

24

Confidential
PLL Enable
There are two configuration methods. The one is used in the startup phase, during which there is
a period of instable clock output once when PLL is enabled. The other is not recommended to be
used in the startup phase as there exists glitches when PLL_OUTPUT_GATE is enabled; after PLLs
become stable, output clock.
Method 1:
Step 1

Set PLL_LDO_EN in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 2

Set PLL_OUTPUT_GATE in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 3

Set the values of N, M1, M0, P in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG.

Step 4

Set PLL_EN in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 5

Set LOCK_ENABLE in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 6

Wait the LOCK status in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG to be 1, and perform the adjustment
for three times.

Step 7

After 20 us latency, the PLL_DDR can be used.

Method 2:
Step 1

Set PLL_LDO_EN in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 2

Set the values of N, M1, M0, P in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG.

Step 3

Set PLL_EN in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 4

Set LOCK_ENABLE in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 5

Wait the LOCK status in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG to be 1, and perform the adjustment
for three times.

Step 6

Wait 20 us latency.

Step 7

Set the PLL_OUTPUT_GATE in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG as 1. Then, PLLs can be used.

NOTE

When more than one channel output exists in PLLs, write 1 to PLL_OUTPUT_GATE for each
output clock to be used.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

25

Confidential
PLL Disable
Follow the steps below to disable PLLs. Before this, ensure that the PLL clock has been switched
to other clock source or closed.
Step 1

Set PLL_OUTPUT_GATE in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG as 0.

Step 2

Set LOCK_ENABLE in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG as 0.

Step 3

Set PLL_EN in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG as 0.

Step 4

Set PLL_LDO_EN in the PLL_DDR_CTRL_REG as 0.

NOTE

It is not suggested to enable or disable the PLLs during usage, as the PLL enable/disable will lead
to the disturbance among PLLs, which will cause system instability. When the clock is not
required, it is recommended to set the PLL_OUTPUT_GATE bit in the PLLx_CTRL_REG as 0.

PLL Spreading
Step 1

Enable PLLs.

Step 2

Configure the static parameters as below

Step 3



SPR_FREQ_MODE is recommended to be 3.



PLL_PI_EN is recommended to be 1.



PLL_PI_CFG is recommended to use the default value.



SMOOTH_EN is recommended to be 0.



DITHER is recommended to be 0.

Configure WAVE_STEP, WAVE_BOT, FREQ, SDM_DIRECTION, FRAC_IN and FRAC_EN in
conformity with PLL spreading/fractional divider formulas.

Step 4

Configure SIG_DELT_PAT_EN and other parameters to enable PLL spreading/fractional
dividers.

Step 5

To adjust static parameters, configure SIG_DELT_PAT_EN as 0. After SDM_BUSY is 0, go
back to step 1.

Step 6

To adjust control parameters when PLL spreading/fractional dividers are enabled,
configure WAVE_STEP, WAVE_BOT, FREQ, SDM_DIRECTION, and FRAC_IN.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

26

Confidential
Step 7

To disable PLL spreading, set SIG_DELT_PAT_EN as 0. To enable PLL spreading next
time, judge SDM_BUSY as 0 first.

PLL Frequency Modulation
Follow the steps below to perform PLL frequency modulation.
Step 1

Ensure the PLL is enabled. If not, enable the PLL by referring to the section PLL Enable.

Step 2

Set PLL_OUTPUT_GATE in the PLLx_CTRL_REG as 0

Step 3

Configure N, M1, M0, and P factors in the PLLx_CTRL_REG.

Step 4

Write 0 to LOCK_ENABLE in the PLLx_CTRL_REG, and then write 1.

Step 5

Wait the LOCK in the PLLx_CTRL_REG to be 1. Judge the state for three times.

Step 6

Wait 20 us latency.

Step 7

Set the PLL_OUTPUT_GATE in the PLLx_CTRL_REG as 1.

4.1.4.2

PLL Lock Status Judgement
As the output signal is unstable in the PLL initial startup phase or when the N value of FM alters,
frequency fluctuation may occur when lock status is enabled for the first time. Therefore, it is
recommended to read the lock status after 3 us. If the lock status is found to be well enabled
after reading for three times, it proves to be stable.

4.1.4.3

Bus Clock Configuration
The bus clock supports dynamic switching, but the switching process needs to obey the
following two rules.


To switch from a lower frequency to a higher frequency: configure the frequency division
factor first, and then switch the clock source.



To switch from a higher frequency to a lower frequency: switch the clock source first, and
then set the frequency division factor.

The bus frequencies are as follows.


AHB: The typical frequency is 200 MHz. The maximum frequency is no more than 200 MHz.



APB0: The typical frequency is 100 MHz. The maximum frequency is no more than 100 MHz.



APB1: The typical frequency is 100 MHz. The maximum frequency is no more than 100 MHz.



APB_UART: The frequency is configured based on UART request, which is no more than 160
MHz.



NSI: The typical frequency is 700 MHz. The maximum frequency is no more than 700 MHz.



MBUS: The typical frequency is 600 MHz. The maximum frequency is no more than 600 MHz.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

27

Confidential
Of which, the suggested NSI clock source configuration is shown as below.
When NSI_CLK runs at 700MHz, select DEPLL3X as the clock source, whose frequency is 696MHz
by default. Therefore, it is not recommended to modify the DEPLL3X frequency.
As DEPLL3X/DEPLL4X will be the clock source of DE0_CLK. If DE module runs at 4KHz, the needed
clock frequency is 696 MHz; then, DEPLL3X is selected as the clock source. If DE module runs at
2KHz, DEPLL3X is not recommended to be the clock source; other clock sources should be
considered.
NOTE

for NSI/MBUS clock configuration, write 1 to NSI_CLK_REG (bit[27]) and MBUS_CLK_REG (bit[27])
to update the NSI_DIV1and MBUS_DIV1, then the readback result will be the updated parameters.
If not, the readback result will be the initial state.

4.1.4.4

Module Clock Configuration
Generic Configuration
for the bus gating reset register of a module, the reset bit is de-asserted first, and then the gating
clock is passed to avoid potential problems caused by the asynchronous release of the reset
signal.
for all module clocks, configure the clock sources and frequency division factors first, and then
write 1 to the gating clock. for the configuration order of the clock source and frequency division
factor, follow the rules below:


To switch from a lower frequency to a higher frequency: set the frequency division factor
first, and then configure the clock source.



To switch from a higher frequency to a lower frequency: configure the clock source first, and
then set the frequency division factor.

GPU Clock Configuration
GPU working clock differs from generic working clock. for the generic working clock, clock
frequency division is realized by counting, and FACTOR_M indicates division coefficient; for the
GPU working clock, FACTOR_M indicates the designated cycles of masks every 16 cycles, through
which the clock frequency division is realized. There are two points should be noted.


The GPU_CLK frequency computing formula is GPU_CLK=CLK_SRC*((16-M)/16).



The effective clock cycle of GPU_CLK is consistent with clock frequency.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

28

Confidential
4.1.4.5

Update Clock Configuration
The configured clock parameters of NSI/MBUS/GPU0/DRAM0 should be additionally updated.
The following precautions are shown as below.
Write 1 to NSI/MBUS/GPU0/DRAM0_UPD bit in the NSI/MBUS/GPU0/DRAM0_CLK_REG to update
the configured parameters of NSI/MBUS/GPU0/DRAM0_SEL, NSI/MBUS/GPU0/DRAM0_DIV1,
NSI/MBUS/GPU0/DRAM0_CLK_GATING; then, the readback result will be the updated parameters.
If not, the readback result will be the original state.

4.1.4.6

Auto Clock Gating
Some buses and PLLs support auto clock gating. The detailed configuration methods are shown
as below.
Bus Auto Gating Configuration
Step 1

Set AHB_MAT_CLK_GATING_REG (bit[31]) as 0 to disable auto clock gating, and then
AHB BUSMATRIX clock will be always enabled; set AHB_MAT_CLK_GATING_REG (bit[31])
as 1 to enable auto gating, then the clock will be auto disabled in case of no bus
operation.

Step 2

Set AHB_MAT_CLK_GATING_REG (bit[29]) as 0 to disable auto gating, and then SD
BUSMATRIX clock will be always enabled; set AHB_MAT_CLK_GATING_REG (bit[29]) as 1
to enable auto gating, then the clock will be auto disabled in case of no bus operation.

PLL Auto Gating Configuration
The following takes DDRPLL as an example to explicate the auto clock gating of PLLs.
Step 1

Set DDRPLL_GATE_EN_REG (bit[16])as 1 and then set DDRPLL_GATE_EN_REG (bit[0])as
1 to disable auto gating.

Step 2

Set DDRPLL_GATE_EN_REG (bit[16]) as 1 and then set DDRPLL_GATE_EN_REG (bit[0])as
0 to enable auto gating.

Step 3

Read DDRPLL_GATE_STAT_REG(bit[16]) to acknowledge the current DDRPLL Clock Gate
Status.

4.2

Power Reset Clock Management (PRCM)

4.2.1

Overview
The Power Reset Clock Management (PRCM) module provides a versatile supporting multiple
power-management techniques and manages the gating and enabling of the clocks to the device
modules in CPUS domain.
The system-level reset management provides correct reset routing and sequencing when one or
more devices are stacked together in the same package. The device-level reset management
provides reset routing to relevant devices.
The PRCM has the following features:


CPUS Clock Configuration



APBS Clock Configuration



CPUS Module Clock Configuration



CPUS Module BUS Gating and Reset



RAM configure Control

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential

4.2.3

Programming Guidelines

4.2.3.1

Bus Clock Configuration

S_TIMER0, S_TIMER1, S_TIMER2, S_TIMER3, S_PWM,
S_IRRX, S_SPI

The bus clock supports dynamic switching, but the switching process needs to obey the
following two rules.


To switch from a lower frequency to a higher frequency: configure the frequency division
factor first, and then switch the clock source.



To switch from a higher frequency to a lower frequency: switch the clock source first, and
then set the frequency division factor.

The bus frequencies are as follows.


AHBS: The typical frequency is 200 MHz.



APBS0: The typical frequency is 100 MHz.



APBS1: The typical frequency is 24 MHz.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

216

Confidential
4.2.3.2

Module Clock Configuration
For the bus gating reset register of a module, the reset bit is de-asserted first, and then the gating
clock is enabled to avoid potential problems caused by the asynchronous release of the reset
signal.
For all module clocks, configure the clock sources and frequency division factors first, and then
write 1 to the gating clock. For the configuration order of the clock source and frequency division
factor, follow the rules below:


To switch from a lower frequency to a higher frequency: set the frequency division factor
first, and then configure the clock source.



To switch from a higher frequency to a lower frequency: configure the clock source first, and
then set the frequency division factor.

5

Processors

5.1

ARM Cortex A76 x2+Cortex A55 x6 Subsystem

5.1.1

Overview
The Cortex-A55 core is a mid-range, low-power core that implements the Armv8-A architecture
with support for the Armv8.1-A extension, the Armv8.2-A extension, the RAS extension, the Load
acquire (LDAPR) instructions introduced in the Armv8.3-A extension, and the dot product
instructions introduced in the Armv8.4-A extension.
The Cortex-A76 core is a high-performance and low-power Arm product that implements the
Armv8-A architecture.
The Cortex-A55 core includes the following features


Core Features
-

Full implementation of the Armv8.2-AA64, A32, and T32 instruction sets.

-

Both the AArch32 and AArch64 execution states at all Exception levels (EL0 to EL3).

-

In-order pipeline with direct and indirect branch prediction.

-

Separate L1 data and instruction side memory systems with a Memory Management
Unit (MMU).

-

Supports for Arm TrustZone® technology.

-

Optional Data Engine unit that implements the Advanced SIMD and floating-point
architecture support.

-

Optional Cryptographic Extension. This architectural extension is only available if the
Data Engine is present.



-

Generic Interrupt Controller (GIC) CPU interface to connect to an external distributor.

-

Generic Timers interface supporting 64-bit count input from an external system counter.

Cache features
-

Optional unified private L2 cache.

-

L1 and L2 cache protection in the form of Error Correction Code (ECC) or parity on all
RAM instances.

The Cortex-A76 core includes the following features:


Core features
-

40-bit Physical Address (PA).

-

A Memory Management Unit (MMU).
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

239

Confidential
-

Optional Cryptographic Extension.

-

Armv8.4 Dot Product instruction support.

-

Superscalar, variable-length, out-of-order pipeline.

-

Supports for Arm TrustZone® technology.

-

Supports for Page-Based Hardware Attributes (PBHA).

-

Reliability, Availability, and Serviceability (RAS) Extension.

-

Full implementation of the Armv8.2-A A64, A32, and T32 instruction sets.

-

Generic Interrupt Controller (GICv4) CPU interface to connect to an external distributor.

-

Generic Timers interface supporting 64-bit count input from an external system counter.

-

An integrated execution unit that implements the Advanced SIMD and floating-point
architecture support.

-

AArch32 Execution state at Exception level EL0 only. AArch64 Execution state at all
Exception levels (EL0 to EL3).



Cache features
-

Separate L1 data and instruction caches.

-

Private, unified data and instruction L2 cache.

-

Optional L1 and L2 memory protection in the form of Error Correcting Code (ECC) or
parity on RAM instances which affect functionality.

The DSU includes the following features:


AMBA ACE5 or AMBA 5 CHI main bus interface.



Optional 128-bit wide I/O-coherent Accelerator Coherency Port (ACP).



Optional 64-bit wide device peripheral port.



Supports for cores with 40-bit, 44-bit, or 48-bit physical addresses.



Armv8.2-A debug logic or (for compatible cores) Armv8.4-A debug logic.



Supports Reliability, Availability, and Serviceability (RAS).



Optional unified 16-way set-associative L3 cache.



64-byte cache lines throughout.



Supports cache partitioning.



Partial L3 cache power down support.



Optional cache protection in the form of Error Correcting Code (ECC) on L3 cache RAM
instances.



Snoop Control Unit (SCU).

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

240

Confidential


L3 memory system can be clocked at a rate synchronous to the external system interconnect
or at integer multiples.

5.1.2



Armv8.2-A or Armv8.4-A architecture cores supported.



Supports three types of cores.



Cores can be clocked at different frequencies.

PMU

The DynamIQ Shared Unit includes performance monitors that enable you to gather various
statistics on the operation of the memory of the cluster during runtime. These provide useful
information about the behavior of the cluster that you can use when debugging or profiling code.
The PMU provides six counters. Each counter can count any of the events available in the cluster.
The absolute counts that are recorded might vary because of pipeline effects. This has negligible
effect except in cases where the counters are enabled for a very short time.
The PMU includes the following interfaces and counters:
Event interface
Events from all other units across the design are provided to the PMU.
System register and APB interface
You can program the PMU registers using the system registers or external APB interface.
Counters
The PMU has 32-bit counters that increment when they are enabled based on events and a 64-bit
cycle counter.
PMU register interface
DSU support access to the performance monitor registers from the internal system register
interface.

5.1.4
5.1.4.1

Programming Guidelines
PLL Distribution
The whole CPU_SYS includes four PLLs, consisting of CPU_BACK_PLL, CPU_L_PLL, CPU_B_PLL,
and CPU_DSU_PLL. The CPU_BACK_PLL is generated by the generic PLL, and the other three
PLLs are generated by the linear PLLs.
The primary clock source of core0/core1/core2/core3/core4/core5 is CPU_L_PLL; and their
backup clock source is 26MHz, CPU_BACK_PLL, and 1.2 GHz.
The primary clock source of core6/core7 is CPU_B_PLL; and their backup clock source is 26MHz,
CPU_BACK_PLL, and 1.2 GHz.
The primary clock source of cluster is CPU_DSU_PLL; and their backup clock source is 26MHz,
CPU_BACK_PLL, and 600 MHz.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

243

Confidential
The clocks of core and cluster supports dynamic adjustment. The clock ratio of cluster directly
influences the latency of access to L3. To meet a great performance, it is recommended that the
frequency of cluster should be at least 75% of that of the fastest core.
The ratio between the frequency of cluster master clock and that of output clock of cluster
accessing external devices is 1:1 or 2:1. For the specific configuration, refer to
CPU_DSU_PLL_CLK_REG (bit[1:0]).
5.1.4.2

Linear PLL Frequency Modulation
There are two kinds of parameters for linear PLL frequency modulation, including the immediate
effect type and the manual update type.
The immediate effect type is that the configured values immediately take effect after being
written to registers, and the readback value is same to the configured one.
The manual update type is that the configured values need to be updated by additionally writing
1 to update bit in PLLx_CTRL_REG; then the readback value are the updated parameter; or, the
readback value will be the original one.
The manual update type of parameters depends on PLLs’ output clocks. Therefore, when
PLL_EN is not enabled, the update operation is invalid when PLLs don’t output clocks.
The PLL parameters influenced by UPDATE operation are PLL_LFM_REG and N in the
PLL_CTRL_REG. The interval of two update operations should be no less than 1 us.
Enable PLLs
Follow the steps below to enable PLLs.
Step 1

Set the PLL_LDO_EN in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 2

Set the PLL_OUTPUT_GATE in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 3

Configure N, M1, M0, and P in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG.

Step 4

Set the PLL_EN in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 5

Set the LOCK_ENABLE in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 6

Set the PLL_UPDATE in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 7

Wait the PLL_UPDATE in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG to be cleared.

Step 8

Wait the LOCK status in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG to be 1, and perform the
adjustment for three times.

Step 9

After 20 us latency, the PLL is enabled.

Disable PLLs
Follow the steps below to disable PLLs.
Step 1

Set the PLL_OUTPUT_GATE in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG as 0.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

244

Confidential
Step 2

Set the LOCK_ENABLE in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG as 0.

Step 3

Set the PLL_PLL_EN in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG as 0.

Step 4

Set the PLL_LDO_EN in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG as 0.

NOTE

It is not suggested to enable or disable the PLLs during usage, as the PLL enable/disable will lead
to the disturbance among PLLs, which will cause system instability. When the clock is not
required, it is recommended to set the PLL_OUTPUT_GATE bit in the PLL_CTRL as 0.

PLL Pre-divider Frequency Modulation
The PLL linear frequency modulation supports smooth transition to target N value at a certain
modulation rate value without re-locking. However, only the linear frequency modulation of N
value is supported. When the pre-divider factor alters, PLL should be re-locked.
When not enabling linear frequency modulation, or when the pre-divider should be adjusted in
the condition that liner frequency modulation is enabled. Follow the steps below to perform PLL
pre-divider frequency modulation.
Step 1

Set the PLL_OUTPUT_GATE in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG as 0.

Step 2

Set the LOCK_ENABLE in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG as 0.

Step 3

Configure N, M1, M0, and P in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG.

Step 4

Set the LOCK_ENABLE in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 5

Set the PLL_UPDATE in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 6

Set the PLL_UPDATE in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 7

Wait the LOCK_STATUS in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG to be cleared.

Step 8

Wait 20 us latency.

Step 9

Set the PLL_OUTPUT_GATE in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

PLL Linear Frequency Modulation
The following steps take CPU_L_PLL as an example to perform PLL linear frequency modulation.
Step 1

Set PLL_PLL_EN in the CPU_L_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1, and wait CPU_L_PLL lock state is
stable.

Step 2

Set SPR_FREQ_MODE in the CPU_L_PLL_PAT0_CTRL_REG as 10 or 11. Set PLL_PI_EN as
1 and SMOOTH_EN as 0 in the CPU_L_PLL_PAT1_CTRL_REG.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

245

Confidential
Step 3

Set PLL_LFM_STEP in the CPU_L_PLL_LFM_REG. STEP is 12 bit. The formula is as below:
FREQ = FCLK*FCLK*STEP/2^17

In the above formula. FREQ is the target modulation rate at the unit of MHz/us. The FCLK is
reference clock frequency at the unit of MHz. Thus, the step can be gotten by the formula as
below:
STEP = FREQ*2^17/FCLK/FCLK
Step 1

Set the PLL_LFM_EN in the CPU_L_PLL_LFM_REG as 1.

Step 2

Set the PLL_UPDATE in the CPU_L_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 3

Wait the PLL_UPDATE in the CPU_L_PLL_CTRL_REG to be 0.

Step 4

Set the PLL_N in the CPU_L_PLL_CTRL_REG and then write 1 to the PLL_UPDATE.

Step 5

Wait the PLL_UPDATE to be 0, indicating the linear frequency modulation completes.

Step 6

To re-configure N value, go back to the step 7.

Step 7

To disable linear frequency modulation, set PLL_LFM_EN in the CPU_L_PLL_LFM_REG
as 0, and set PLL_UPDATE in the CPU_L_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

5.1.4.3

Generic PLL Frequency Modulation
Enable PLLs
There are two configuration methods. The one is used in the startup phase, during which there is
a period of instable clock output once when PLL is enabled. The other is not recommended to be
used in the startup phase as there exists glitches when PLL_OUTPUT_GATE is enabled; after PLLs
become stable, output clock.
Method 1:
Step 1

Set PLL_LDO_EN in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 2

Set PLL_OUTPUT_GATE in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 3

Set the values of N, M1, M0, P in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG.

Step 4

Set PLL_EN in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 5

Set LOCK_ENABLE in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 6

Wait the LOCK status in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG to be 1, and perform the
adjustment for three times.

Step 7

After 20 us latency, PLLs can be used.

Method 2:
Step 1

Set PLL_LDO_EN in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 2

Set the values of N, M1, M0, P in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

246

Confidential
Step 3

Set PLL_EN in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 4

Set LOCK_ENABLE in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

Step 5

Wait the LOCK status in the CPU_L/B/DSU_PLL_CTRL_REG to be 1, and perform the
adjustment for three times.

Step 6

After 20 us latency.

Step 7

Set the PLL_OUTPUT_GATE in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1. Then, PLLs can be
used.

NOTE

When more than one channel output exists in PLLs, write 1 to PLL_OUTPUT_GATE for each
output clock to be used.

Disable PLLs
Follow the steps below to disable PLLs. Before this, ensure that the PLL clock has been switched
to other clock source or closed.
Step 1

Set PLL_OUTPUT_GATE in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG as 0.

Step 2

Set LOCK_ENABLE in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG as 0.

Step 3

Set PLL_EN in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG as 0.

Step 4

Set PLL_LDO_EN in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG as 0.

NOTE

It is not suggested to enable or disable the PLLs during usage, as the PLL enable/disable will lead
to the disturbance among PLLs, which will cause system instability. When the clock is not
required, it is recommended to set the PLL_OUTPUT_GATE bit in the PLL_CTRL as 0.

PLL Spreading
Step 1

Enable PLLs.

Step 2

Configure the static parameters as below


SPR_FREQ_MODE is recommended to be 3.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

247

Confidential

Step 3



PLL_PI_EN is recommended to be 1.



PLL_PI_CFG is recommended to use the default value.



SMOOTH_EN is recommended to be 0.



DITHER is recommended to be 0.

Configure WAVE_STEP, WAVE_BOT, FREQ, SDM_DIRECTION, FRAC_IN and FRAC_EN in
conformity with PLL spreading/fractional divider formulas.

Step 4

Configure SIG_DELT_PAT_EN and other parameters to enable PLL spreading/fractional
dividers.

Step 5

To adjust static parameters, configure SIG_DELT_PAT_EN as 0. After SDM_BUSY is 0, go
back to step 1.

Step 6

To adjust control parameters when PLL spreading/fractional dividers are enabled,
configure WAVE_STEP, WAVE_BOT, FREQ, SDM_DIRECTION, and FRAC_IN.

Step 7

To disable PLL spreading, set SIG_DELT_PAT_EN as 0. To enable PLL spreading next
time, judge SDM_BUSY as 0 first.

PLL Frequency Modulation

CAUTION
Before PLL frequency modulation, ensure the PLLs are enabled. It is not recommended to
enable/disable during the PLL usage. When the clock is not used, set PLL_OUTPUT_GATE in the
CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG as 0.
The generic PLLs cannot be used during the frequency modulation. Therefore, set
PLL_OUTPUT_GATE in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG as 0.

Follow the steps below to perform PLL frequency modulation.

5.1.5

Step 1

Configure N and M factors.

Step 2

Write 0 to LOCK_ENABLE in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG, and then write 1.

Step 3

Wait the LOCK in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG to be 1.

Step 4

Set the PLL_OUTPUT_GATE in the CPU_BACK_PLL_CTRL_REG as 1.

6

Interprocessor Communication

6.1

Message Box (MSGBOX)

6.1.1

Overview
The Message Box (MSGBOX) provides interrupt communication mechanism for microprocessors.
The MSGBOX has the following features:


Supports two CPUs to transmit information through one-way channels. Each CPU has a
MSGBOX and can only read or write in one communication



6.1.2

-

CPUX_MSGBOX: CPUS write, CPUX read

-

CPUS_MSGBOX: CPUX write, CPUS read

The channel between two CPUs has 4 channels, and the FIFO depth of each is 8x32 bits.

Block Diagram
The following figure shows the block diagram of the message box.
Figure 6-1 Message Box Block Diagram
CPUX_MSGBOX

CPUS_MSGBOX
8x32bits

8x32bits

8x32bits

8x32bits
CPUS

CPUX

CPUX

CPUS

8x32bits

8x32bits

8x32bits

8x32bits

Each CPU has 4 channels. The two channels can be configured to be secure by software, the
other two channels can be configured to be non-secure by software. The two secure channels or
two non-secure channels can be configured as one synchronous box (Sending a message
requires a response) or one asynchronous box (Sending a message requires no response).

6.1.3

Clock Sources
The MSGBOX is mounted on AHB. Before accessing the MSGBOX registers, you need to de-assert
the MSGBOX reset signal on AHB bus and then open the MSGBOX gating signal on AHB bus.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

320

Confidential

6.1.4
6.1.4.1

Functional Description
Interrupt
Each channel can independently configure the interrupt enable bit. A read interrupt will be
generated when the channel is not empty, while a write interrupt will be generated when the
channel is not full. For each CPU, all channels can generate read interrupts, that is, if only a
channel is non-full, the read interrupt will be generated. The channel that generates interrupts
can be queried by the interrupt status register.

6.1.4.2

FIFO Status
When channel FIFO is non-full, the MSGBOX_FIFO_STATUS_REG [0]is 0. At the moment, the FIFO
can be written.
When channel FIFO is full, the MSGBOX_FIFO_STATUS_REG [0] is 1. At the moment, if FIFO is
written again, the previous data will be covered.

6.1.4.3

Transmitter/Receiver Mode
At the same channel, user1 is fixed as transmitter, user0 is fixed as receiver.

6.1.5
6.1.5.1

Programming Guidelines
Check the Transfer Status via the Interrupt
Follow the steps below to check the transfer status:
Step 1

Enable the interrupts: Configure the interrupt enable bits of transmitter/receiver
through MSGBOX_RD_IRQ_EN_REG/MSGBOX_WR_IRQ_EN_REG.

Step 2

Check

the

IRQ

status

of

the

corresponding

queue

through

MSGBOX_RD_IRQ_STATUS_REG/MSGBOX_WR_IRQ_STATUS_REG.


If the FIFO is not full, the channel will generate a transmission interrupt to remind
the transmitter to transmit data. Write data to the FIFO in the interrupt handler,
then clear the pending bit of the transmitter in MSGBOX_WR_IRQ_STATUS_REG and
the enable bit of the transmitter in MSGBOX_WR_IRQ_EN_REG.



If the FIFO is filled with new data, the channel generates a reception interrupt to
remind the receiver to receive data. Read data from the FIFO in interrupt handler,
then clear the pending bit of the receiver in MSGBOX_RD_IRQ_STATUS_REG and the
enable bit of the receiver in MSGBOX_RD_IRQ_EN_REG.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

321

Confidential
6.1.5.2

Check the Transfer Status via the FIFO
Follow the steps below to check the FIFO status of the corresponding queue:


If the FIFO is not full, the transmitter fills the FIFO with 8*32 bits.



If the FIFO is full, the receiver reads the FIFO data, and reads MSGBOX_FIFO_STATUS_REG to
acquire the current FIFO data amount and the FIFO data amount before reading to ensure
that no data is dropped.

6.1.5.3

Transmit/Receive Message

message transmitting and receiving of CPUs.
CPUX_MSGBOX: Receiving message

6.2

Spinlock

6.2.1

Overview
The spinlock provides hardware synchronization mechanism in multi-core systems. With the lock
operation, the spinlock prevents multiple processors from handling the sharing data
simultaneously and thus ensure the coherence of data.
The spinlock has the following features:

6.2.2



Supports 32 lock units



Two kinds of lock status: locked and unlocked



Lock time of the processor is predictable (less than 200 cycles)

Clock Sources
The spinlock is mounted on AHB. Before accessing the spinlock registers, you need to de-assert
the reset signal on AHB bus and then open the corresponding gating signal on AHB bus.

6.2.3

Functional Description

6.2.3.1

Typical Application
The following figure shows how to take and release spinlock. A processor locks spinlock0 before
executing specific codes, and then unlocks the codes. After the lock is free, other processors can
read or write the data.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

331

Confidential

Free a Lock
SPINLOCK_LOCK_REG_i[0]=0

Free the Lock
End

6.2.3.2

Spinlock State Machine
When a processor uses spinlock, it needs to acquire the spinlock status through
SPINLOCK_STATUS_REG.
Reading operation: When the return value is 0, it indicates that the spinlock enters the locked
status; reading this status bit again can return 1, it indicates that the spinlock is the locked
status.
Writing operation: When the spinlock is in the locked status, writing 0 can convert the spinlock to
the unlocked status, the writing operation for other status is invalid.
The following figure shows the spinlock state machine.
Figure 6-4 Spinlock State Machine

(e)

1

Unlocked State
(TAKEN_bit=0)
(f)

a)

(d)

Locked State
(TAKEN_bit=1)
0
(c)
Write 1

When the spinlock is in the unlocked state, writing 0/1 has no effect;
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

332

Confidential
b)

When the spinlock is in the locked state, writing 0 can convert the corresponding spinlock to

the unlocked state;
c)

When the spinlock is in the locked state, writing 1 has no effect;

d)

When the spinlock is in the unlocked state, reading the bit can return 0 (it indicates spinlock

enters into the locked state);
e)

When the spinlock is in the locked state, reading the bit can return 1 (it indicates spinlock is

in the locked state);
f)

After reset, the spinlock is in the unlock state by default.

6.2.4

Programming Guidelines

6.2.4.1

Switching Spinlock Status
Follow the steps below to switch the lock status of a spinlock between the locked and unlocked
statuses.
Step 1

When the read value from SPINLOCKN_LOCK_REG (N=0–31) is 0, the spinlock comes into
the locked status.

Step 2

Execute the application codes, and the status of SPINLOCK_STATUS_REG is 1.

Step 3

Write 0 to SPINLOCKN_LOCK_REG (N=0–31), the spinlock converts into the unlocked
status, and the corresponding spinlock is released.

CPUX:
a)

The CPUX initializes Spinlock.

b)

spinlock0 and then request to take spinlock0. Otherwise, retry until the lock register0 is
taken.

c)

Execute CPUX critical code.

d)

After executing CPUX critical code, the CPUX frees spinlock0.

e)

Enable spinlock0 irq.

f)

Clear spinlock0 irq pending.

g)

While CPUS acquired spinlock0’ authorization, CPUX waits for CPUS’ freeing spinlock0.

CPUS:
a)

If the CPUX has taken spinlock0, the CPUS waits for CPUX to free spinlock0.

b)

The CPUS requests to take spinlock0. If it fails, retry until the lock register0 is taken.

c)

Execute CPUS critical code.

d)

After executing CPUS critical code, the CPUS frees spinlock0.

e)

Enable spinlock0 irq.

f)

Clear spinlock0 irq pending.

7

Thermal Sensor

7.1

Thermal Sensor Controller (THS)

7.1.1

Overview
The thermal sensors are common elements in wide range of modern system on chips (SoCs)
platform. The thermal sensors are used to constantly monitor the temperature on the chip.
The SoC embeds five thermal sensors in possible hot spots on the die. Sensor0 is located in the
CPUB; sensor1 is located in the DDR; sensor2 is located in the NPU; sensor3 is located in the
CPUL;

sensor4 is located in the GPU. These thermal sensors generate interrupt to lower

temperature via DVFS, on reaching a certain thermal threshold.
The THS has the following features:

7.1.2



Averaging filter for thermal sensor reading



Supports over-temperature protection interrupt and over-temperature alarm interrupt



Supports ±3℃ error limit from 60 to 125℃ and ±5℃ from -40 to 60℃

Environment Diagram
The following figures show the environment diagram of the THS.

Write 0x3A to the bit [31:12] of THS_PER to set the THS work period.

Step 6

Write 0x1 to the bit2 of THS_FILTER to enable the temperature convert filter.

Step 7

Write 0x1 to the bit [1:0] of THS_FILTER to select the filter type.

Step 8

Read THS eFuse value from SID, and then write the eFuse value to TSENSORn_CDATA to
calibrate THS.

Step 9

Write 0x1 to the bit [0] of THS_DATA_INTC to enable the interrupt of THS.

Step 10 Set GIC interface based on IRQ 71.
Step 11 Put the interrupt handler address into the interrupt vector table.
Step 12 Write 0x1 to the bit [0] 0f THS_EN to enable THS.
Step 13 Read the bit [0] of THS_DATA_INTS. If it is 1, the temperature conversion is complete.
Step 14 Read the bit [11:0] of THS0_DATA, and calculate the THS temperature based on section

8

Timers

8.1

Timer0

8.1.1

Overview
The Timer0 supports timing, counting, and interrupt output.
The Timer module has the following features:


Supports configuring timer registers through AHB interface



Count clock can be switched between RTC_32K, DCXO, SYS_CLK24M, PERI0_200M, and
RC16M through PRCM/CCU

8.1.2



Programmable 56-bit down timer



Supports two count modes: continuous mode and single mode



Generates an interrupt when the count value is decreased to 0

Block Diagram
The following figure shows the block diagram of timer1.

8.1.4

Functional Descriptions

8.1.4.1

Count Time Calculation

T

Description

It is generated by the multiplexer between DCXO and
PLL_REF. Its frequency is fixed at 24 MHz.

{TIMER_IVH, TIMER_IVL} - {TIMER_CVH, TIMER_CVL}
f clk_timer

Where,
TIMER_IVH is the higher 24 bits of the interval value that is configured by the lower 24 bits of the
TIMER_IVH_REG.
TIMER_IVL is the lower 32 bits of the interval value that is configured by the TIMER_IVL_REG.
TIMER_CVH is the higher 24 bits of the current value that is configured by the lower 24 bits of the
TIMER_CVH_REG.
TIMER_CVL is the lower 32bits of the current value that is configured by the TIMER_CVL_REG.
fclk_timer is the frequency of timer clock source.
8.1.4.2

Count Modes
The timer is a 56-bit down counter. The counter value is decremented by 1 on each rising edge of
the timer clock. The timer has two count modes: the single count mode and the periodic mode.
You can configure the count modes via the TIMER_CTRL_REG(bit[7]).


Continuous Mode

In the continuous mode, the timer will reload data from the Timer Interval Value and generate an
interrupt when the counter is decreased to 0. Then, it restarts another round of counting.


Single Mode

In the single mode, the timer will stop counting and generate an interrupt after the counter
decreases to 0. It restarts counting only when the interval value is reloaded.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

356

Confidential

8.1.5
8.1.5.1

Programming Guidelines
Initialization
Refer to the following steps to initialize the timer.
Step 1

Configure the timer parameters including the clock sources and timing modes by
writing to TIMER_CTRL_REG. There is no sequence requirement for these parameter
configurations.

Step 2

Write the interval value.
a)

Write to TIMER_IVL_REG and TIMER_IVH_REG to configure the interval values of the
timer.

b)

Write to TIMER_CTRL_REG (bit[1]) to load the interval value to the timer. If the bit is
1, no write operation is permitted; if the bit is 0, reload succeeds.

Step 3

Write to TIMER_CTRL_REG(bit[0]) to start the timer. Read TIMER_CVL_REG and
TIMER_CVH_REG to get the current value of the timer.
NOTE

When performing read or write operations on the current value registers, operate
TIMER_CVL_REG register before TIMER_CVH_REG register.
8.1.5.2

Interrupt Processing
Refer to the following steps to process the interrupt:
Step 1

Write to the corresponding interrupt in TIMER_IRQ_REG. The timer will generate an
interrupt once the count value reaches 0.

Step 2

After the software program enters the interrupt process, write to the pending bit of the
corresponding interrupts in TIMER_STA_REG to clear the interrupt pending.

Step 3

8.1.6

Resume the interrupt and continue to execute the interrupted process.

8.2

Timer1

8.2.1

Overview
The Timer1 supports the timing, counting, and interrupt output.
The Timer module has the following features:

8.2.2



Count clock can be switched between RTC_32K and SYS_CLK24M



Configurable eight pre-scaler coefficients



Programmable 32-bit down timer



Supports two count modes: continuous mode and single mode



Generates an interrupt when the count is decreased to 0

8.2.4

Functional Descriptions

8.2.4.1

Count Time Calculation

Description
It is generated by the multiplexer between DCXO and
PLL_REF. Its frequency is fixed at 24 MHz.
Its frequency is 32.768 KHz by default.

TMR0_INTV_VALUE_REG - TMR0_CUR_VALUE_REG
TMR0_CLK_SRC

× TMR0_CLK_PRES

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

362

Confidential
Where,
TMR0_INTV_VALUE_REG is the timer interval value.
TMR0_CUR_VALUE_REG is the timer current count value.
TMR0_CLK_SRC is the timer clock source.
TMR0_CLK_PRES is the timer clock frequency division.
8.2.4.2

Count Modes
The timer is a 32-bit down counter. The counter value is decremented by 1 on each rising edge of
the timer clock. The timer has two count modes: the single mode and the continuous mode. You
can configure the count modes via the TMRn_CTRL_REG (bit[7]).


Continuous Mode

In the continuous mode, the timer will reload data from the Timer Interval Value and generate an
interrupt when the counter is decreased to 0. Then, it restarts another round of counting.


Single Mode

In the single mode, the timer will stop counting and generate an interrupt after the counter
decreases to 0. It restarts counting only when the interval value is reloaded.

8.2.5
8.2.5.1

Programming Guidelines
Initialization
Refer to the following steps to initialize the timer:
Step 1

Configure the timer parameters including the clock sources and timing modes by
writing to TMRn_CTRL_REG. There is no sequence requirement for these parameter
configurations.

Step 2

Write the interval value.
a)

Write to TMRn_INTV_VALUE_REG to configure the interval values of the timer.

b)

Write to TMRn_CTRL_REG to load the interval value to the timer. If the bit is 1, no
write operation is permitted; if the bit is 0, reload succeeds.

Step 3

Write to TMRn_CTRL_REG to start the timer. Read TMRn_CUR_VALUE_REG to get the
current value of the timer.

8.2.5.2

Interrupt Processing
Refer to the following steps to process the interrupt:
Step 1

Write to the corresponding interrupt in TMR_IRQ_EN_REG. The timer will generate an
interrupt once the count value reaches 0.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

363

Confidential
Step 2

After the software program enters the interrupt process, write to the pending bit of the
corresponding interrupts in TMR_IRQ_STA_REG to clear the interrupt pending.

Step 3

8.2.6

Resume the interrupt and continue to execute the interrupted process.

8.3

Watchdog Timer (WDT)

8.3.1

Overview
Watchdog Timer is used to transmit a reset signal to reset the entire system after an exception
occurs.
The It has the following features:


Two clock sources selectable: RTC_32K and DCXO/750



Includes a 32-bit up counter and a 12-bit down counter



Configurable 12 initial values



Supports generating timeout interrupts



Supports generating reset signals



Supports timer restart

8.3.2

Block Diagram
The following figure shows the functional block diagram of the watchdog module.
Figure 8-3 Watchdog Block Diagram

8.3.3

Functional Descriptions
The watchdog timer includes a 32-bit up counter and a 12-bit down counter. The counter value is
increased or decreased by 1 on each rising edge of the count clock. For the down counter, it only
works in the reset mode.
The watchdog timer has two operating modes: interrupt mode and reset mode.


Interrupt mode

Write 2’b10 to WDT_CFG_REG (bit[1:0]). When the up counter value reaches the
WDT_INTERVAL_VALUE set by the WDT_MODE_REG, an interrupt will be generated if
WDT_IRQ_EN_REG (bit[0]) is set to 1.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

374

Confidential


Reset mode

Write 2’b01 to WDT_CFG_REG (bit[1:0]). When the up counter value reaches the
WDT_INTERVAL_VALUE set by the WDT_MODE_REG, a reset signal will be generated to reset the
entire system. The period of pulling the reset signal to low is controlled by a down counter value,
which is congifured by WDT_OCFG_REG (bit[11:0]).
The clock sources of WDT can be selected from CLK_32K and DCXO/750(26MHz/750) by
configuring WDT_CFG_REG (bit[8]).
The WDT will restart counting by setting 1 to WDT_CTRL_REG (bit[0]) and setting 0xA57 to
WDT_CTRL_REG (bit[12:1]).

8.3.4
8.3.4.1

Programming Guidelines
Initialization
Follow the steps below to initialize the watchdog timer:
Step 1

Configure the WDT_CFG_REG (bit[1:0]) to set the generation of the interrupts or the
output of reset signal.

8.3.4.2

Step 2

Configure the WDT_MODE_REG (bit [7:4]) to configure the initial count value.

Step 3

Write 1 to WDT_MODE_REG (bit [0]) to enable the watchdog timer.

Interrupt Processing
Follow the steps below to process the interrupt:
Step 1

Write 1 to the WDT_IRQ_EN_REG (bit[0]) to enable the interrupt.

Step 2

After entering the interrupt process, write 1 to the WDT_IRQ_STAT (bit[0]) to clear the
interrupt pending, and then process the interrupt.

Step 3
8.3.4.3

Resume the interrupt and continue to execute the interrupted process.

Watchdog Timer Reset
In the following instance making configurations for Watchdog: Configure clock source as

DCXO/750, configure Interval Value as 1s and configure Watchdog Configuration as to whole
system. This instance indicates that reset system after 1s.
writel (0x16AA_003F, WDT_OCFG_REG)

//Set reset pulse width to 2ms

writel (0x16AA0001, WDT_CFG_REG)

//To whole system

writel (0x16AA0010, WDT_MODE_REG)

//Interval Value set 1s

writel ((readl(WDT_MODE_REG)|(1<<0), WDT_MODE_REG)

//Enable Watchdog

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

375

Confidential
8.3.4.4

Watchdog Timer Restart
In the following instance making configurations for Watchdog:
Configure Interval Value as 1s and Configure Watchdog to reset whole system. If the time of other
codes is larger than 1s, watchdog will reset the whole system. In the sentence of time of other
codes inside 1s, watchdog will be restarted if the configuration of restart watchdog is
implemented (normal feed dog process), and watchdog should be configured as restart after
changing the interval value. Below are the procedures for Normally feed dog and Change the
interval value.
1. Normally feed dog process
//Configure reset pulse width 2ms
writel(readl(WDT_OCFG_REG) & (~(0xFF << 0)) | (0x3F << 0) | (0x16AA << 16), WDT_OCFG_REG);
writel(readl(WDT_CFG_REG) & (~(0x1 << 0)) | (0x1 << 0), WDT_CFG_REG)

//To whole system

writel(readl(WDT_MODE_REG) & (~(0xF << 4)) | (0x1 << 4), WDT_MODE_REG) //Interval Value set
1s
writel(readl(WDT_MODE_REG) & (~(0x1 << 0)) | (0x1 << 0), WDT_MODE_REG) //Enable Watchdog
----other codes--//Writel 0xA57 at Key Field and Restart Watchdog
writel(readl(WDT_CTRL_REG) | (0xA57 << 1) & (~(0x1 << 0)) | (0x1 << 0), WDT_CTRL_REG);

2. Change WDT Interval value
//Configure reset pulse width 2ms
writel(readl(WDT_OCFG_REG) & (~(0xFF << 0)) | (0x3F << 0) | (0x16AA << 16), WDT_OCFG_REG );
writel(readl(WDT_CFG_REG) & (~(0x1 << 0)) | (0x1 << 0), WDT_CFG_REG)

//To whole system

writel(readl(WDT_MODE_REG) & (~(0xF << 4)) | (0x1 << 4), WDT_MODE_REG) //Interval Value set
1s
writel(readl(WDT_MODE_REG) & (~(0x1 << 0)) | (0x1 << 0), WDOG_MODE_REG) //Enable Watchdog
----other codes--writel(readl(WDT_MODE_REG) & (~(0xF << 4)), WDT_MODE_REG)

//Interval Value set 1s

//Writel 0xA57 at Key Field and Restart Watchdog
writel(readl(WDT_CTRL_REG) | (0xA57 << 1) & (~(0x1 << 0)) | (0x1 << 0), WDT_CTRL_REG)

9

RTC

9.1

RTC

9.1.1

Overview
The Real Time Clock (RTC) is used to implement the time counter and the timing wakeup
functions. The RTC can display the year, month, day, week, hour, minute, second in real time.
With the independent power, the RTC can still work when system powers off.
The RTC has the following features:


Embedded with a 16-bit day counter, a 5-bit hour counter, a 6-bit minute counter, and a
6-bit second counter



Externally connect to 32.768 kHz low-frequency oscillator for counting clock



1 kHz counting frequency



Configurable initial value by software anytime



Supports generating interrupt and waking up the external devices with the timing alarms
function



Supports fanout function of internal 32K clock



8 general-purpose registers for storing the power-off information in the VDD_RTC power
domain



Multiple special registers for recording the BROM information in the VDD_CPUS power
domain

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential

9.1.4.3

Alarm 0
The ALARM0_CUR_VLU_REG is a 32bit number which adds 1 each second. When Alarm0irq is
enabled, read the value of the ALARM0_CUR_VLU_REG, add n seconds, and write to the
ALARM0_DAY_SET_REG. N seconds later, the value of ALARM0_CUR_VLU_REG is the same to that
of ALARM0_DAY_SET_REG. Then, the Alarm0irq will be triggered.

9.1.4.4

Power-off Information Storage
The RTC provides eight 32-bit general purpose register to store power-off information.
Because VCC-RTC always holds non-power-off state after VCC-RTC cold starts, when the system
is in shutdown or standby scene, the CPU can judge software process by the storing information.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

384

Confidential
9.1.4.5

VDD-RTC
The RTC module has a LDO, the input source of the LDO is VCC_RTC, the output of the LDO is
RTC_VIO, the value of RTC_VIO is adjustable, the RTC_VIO is mainly used for internal digital logic.

9.1.4.6

RC Calibration
RC calibration circuit is shown as below. Whether to output the calibrated RC clock is decided by

Figure 9-5 RC Calibration Circuit

The following figure shows the principle of RC calibration. The DCXO is taken as the reference
clock to compute the counter number M in the RC clock within 1 ms, 16 ms, or 128 ms. As a result,
the accurate frequency of the internal RC can be obtained; then, it will be divided by 32.768KHz
to get the division ratio K of 32.768 KHz divided from RC clock; at last, the RC16M is divided by
ratio K to get the frequency of 32.768 KHz. It should be reminded that the principle of RC
calibration is to let output frequency is 32.768 KHz but not let input frequency is 16MHz.

9.1.4.7

DCXO Scheduled Wake-up
The DCXO scheduled wakeup circuit includes two controls, which are the scheduled wakeup
hardware automatic enable and the scheduled wakeup time length configured by software.
The scheduled wakeup means that DCXO circuit is waked up every 1s-60s in the scene of super
standby or shutdown to output clock for 32K calibration; generally, the ambient temperature
alters slightly within several seconds. Afterwards, DCXO circuit is switched off for a period, which
is the scheduled wakeup time length configured by software. The period from DCXO wakeup to
DCXO stable clock output is 3ms-4ms. If the scheduled wakeup function is disabled, DCXO circuit
will keep working. The DCXO schedule wake-up diagram is shown as below.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

385

Confidential
Figure 9-7 DCXO Scheduled wake-up diagram
Time axis

Shut-down/Enter

The scheduled
wakeup time
configured by
software

The period
from DCXO
wakeup to
DCXO stable
clock output

Start-up/Exit

The time of a
calibration

In the scene of shutdown or super standby, the time of a calibration consists of the scheduled
wakeup time configured by software plus the period from DCXO wakeup to DCXO stable clock
output and the time of a calibration. In the above figure, the scheduled wakeup time is 1s; the
actual value can be configured by software. The period from DCXO wakeup to DCXO stable clock
output is theoretically 4ms; the actual value is based on the IC verifications. Among the three
periods, startup or super standby exit will not lead to DCXO anomalies.
The DCXO enable signal and DCXO scheduled wakeup signal are in an OR relationship, and they
do not conflict.
The intervals of operations on DCXO enable and disable should be at least 4ms.

9.1.5

Programming Guidelines

9.1.5.1

RTC Clock Source Select
To select from RTC clock sources, follow the steps as below.
a)

Set LOSC_CTRL_REG [bit1] as 1 to select the divided clock whose RTC internal clock source
is DCXO.

b)

Set LOSC_CTRL_REG [bit1] as 0 to select the divided clock whose RTC internal clock source
is External 32K or RC16M.

c)

Use clock source auto switch when External 32K is lost.

Step 1

Set LOSC_CTRL_REG [bit14] as 1. When External 32K is lost, 32k clk source will be auto
changed to RC.

Step 2

Set LOSC_CTRL_REG [bit4] as 1 to enable external 32768Hz crystal.

Step 3

Set LOSC_CTRL_REG [bit15] as 0 enable External 32K auto switch function.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

386

Confidential
Step 4

Read LOSC_AUTO_SWT_STA_REG [bit2] for three times. It is 0, indicating External 32K
startup succeeds.

Step 5

Set LOSC_CTRL_REG [bit1] as 1.

Step 6

Read LOSC_AUTO_SWT_STA_REG [bit0]. If it is 1, indicating the RTC clock source has
been switched to External 32K.

Step 7

Set LOSC_CTRL_REG [bit0] as 0 to select the divided clock whose RTC internal clock
source is RC16M.

NOTE
When External 32K is disabled, the divided clock of RC16M will be selected whether
LOSC_CTRL_REG [bit0] is written to 0 or 1.

d)

Do not use clock source auto switch when External 32K is lost.

Step 1

Set LOSC_CTRL_REG [bit15] as 1 to disable External 32K auto switch function.

Step 2

Set LOSC_CTRL_REG [bit14] as 0. When External 32K is lost, 32k clk source won’t be auto
changed to RC.

Step 3

Set LOSC_CTRL_REG [bit0] as 0 to select the divided clock whose RTC internal clock
source is RC16M.

Step 4

Set LOSC_CTRL_REG [bit0] as 1 to select the divided clock whose RTC internal clock
source is External 32K.

NOTE
After External 32K auto switch function is disabled, both RC16M and External 32K should be
enabled as whether 32K clock exists cannot be guaranteed in this scene.
9.1.5.2

Real Time Setting
Write the current time to RTC_DAY_REG and RTC_HH_MM_SS_REG.

NOTE
The bit [8:7] of LOSC_CTRL_REG is should be set to 0 before the next time configuration.
Here are the basic code samples.
For example, set time to 21st, 07:08:09 and read it.

9.1.5.3

Alarm0 Setting
Step 1

Enable alram0 interrupt by writing 1 to ALARM0_IRQ_EN.

Step 2

Write the count-down day, hour, minute, second number to ALARM0_DAY_SET_REG,
ALARM0_CUR_VLU_REG, and ALARM0_CONFIG_REG.

Step 3

Enable alarm0 function by writing 1 to ALARM0_ENABLE_REG, then the software can
query

alarm

count

value

in

real

time

by

ALARM0_DAY_SET_REG

and

ALARM0_CUR_VLU_REG. When the setting time is reached, ALARM0_IRQ_STA_REG is set
to 1 to generate an interrupt.
Step 4

After entering the interrupt process, write 0 to the ALARM0_IRQ_STA_REG to clear the
interrupt pending, and execute the interrupt process.

Step 5

Resume the interrupt and continue to execute the interrupted process.

Step 6

The power-off wakeup is generated via SoC hardware and PMU, the software only needs
to set the pending condition of alarm0, and set ALARM0_CONFIG_REG to 1.

9.1.5.4

DCXO Frequency
The SoC supports three kinds of high-frequency oscillator, whose pull up/down status are input
by two external PADs, DCXO_ST0 and DCXO_ST1. The two PADs status are weak pull-up by
default. When external pins float or connect to power, the PAD input signal is 1. When external
pins are grounded, the PAD input signal is 0. When the two PADs are combined, the oscillator
status are as follows.
2’b00: 24M oscillator (UFS uses external 26M oscillator)
2’b01: 19.2M oscillator
2’b10: 26M oscillator
2’b11: 24M oscillator (UFS uses external 19.2M oscillator)
The status of DCXO_ST PAD can be read by the XO_CTRL0_REG (bit[15:14]). To avoid external
interference, perform read operation for three times and ensure the read values are consistent.
As DCXO PAD status are weak pull up by default. When external pins are grounded, a leakage
path will be formed. Therefore, if DCXO_ST0 and DCXO_ST1 status is 00 when the power-up
completes, it indicates the external pins are grounded. In this condition, the DCXO PAD will be
configured as 0 in the XO_CTRL1_REG(bit[11:8]) to avoid power leakage.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

388

Confidential
9.1.5.5

PHY Reference Clock
On the SoC, DCXO outputs two independent reference clocks. One is for UFS and the other is for
COMBO PHY0, COMBO PHY1, and HDMI. The clock gating is put on each analog PHY reference
clock entrance. Therefore, the reference clock can be closed.
These PHY reference clock gating is controlled by XO_CTRL1_REG (bit[5:4]) and XO_CTRL1_REG
(bit[1:0]) and default to be closed. Write 1 to corresponding bits to enable reference clock. The
configuration principles are shown as below.
If the PHY reference clock is supplied by external PADs, the internal reference clock gating is



configured as 0 to disable clock.
If the PHY reference clock is supplied by DCXO, the internal reference clock gating is 1 to



enable clock.
The reference clocks of UFS, COMBO PHY0, COMBO PHY1 are controlled by both RTC gating and
clock request of each module. For details, see the section of each module.

10 I/O Memory Management Unit
The I/O Memory management unit (IOMMU) is designed for the specific memory requirements of
products. It maps the virtual address of peripherals accessing memory to the physical address.
The IOMMU allows multiple ways to manage the location of physical address, and it can map the
physical address which has potentially conflict to allocate memory space for different processes,
and also allow the application of non-continuous address to map to continuous virtual address
space.
MMU-600 contains the following key components:


Two IOMMUs
-

iommu0 supports master0-3: USB0_USB1, CSI, ISP, VE_ENC

-

iommu1 supports master0-5: VE_MBUS0, VE_MBUS1, DE0, DI, G2D, EINK



Supports mapping virtual address to physical address by hardware



Each IOMMU supports concurrent address mapping in host modules



Each IOMMU supports 16G space address mapping



Each IOMMU supports maximum 15 masters



Supports independent bypass, prefetch, and interrupt handling for masters



Supports two-level TLBs. Each master has its own L1 TLB, while the masters in one IOMMU
share a L2 TLB.



Supports complete flush and local invalidation for TLB



Supports triggering PTW behaviors in case of a cache miss



Supports authorization check



Supports 4K protection of MBUS protocol; not support that of AXI host port

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

405

Confidential

11 Memory Controllers
11.1

SDRAM controller (DRAMC)
The DRAMC has the following features:


32-bit LPDDR4/LPDDR4x/LPDDR5 SDRAM



Clock frequency up to 2133 MHz for LPDDR4 and LPDDR4x



Clock frequency up to 2400 MHz for LPDDR5



Supports Dynamic Frequency Setting(DFS) via hardware



Supports multiple Low Power Modes



Supports the read-modify-write function



Supports flip chip package



Supports VPR/VPW command processing



Supports DBYTE mapping and CA mapping



Supports DVFSC only for LPDDR5



Supports PPR only for LPDDR4 and LPDDR5

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

406

Confidential

11.2

Universal Flash Storage Host Controller (UFSHC)
The Universal Flash Storage protocol developed by JEDEC is aimed to define UFS electrical
interface and UFS device. UFS electrical interface is a general-purpose serial communication bus;
and UFS device is a general-purpose data storage and communication medium. UFSHC is the
UFS host controller compatible with UFS protocol. In the chip, the UFSHC is composed of
Synopsys UFS3.0, UniPro1.8, and MPHY4.1.
The UFSHC has the following features:


Supports Scatter/Gather DMA



Preconfigures up to 32 task requests and 8 task management requests



Supports various UPIU data packets (32B~65535B)



Supports system host to program and access the 32-bit AHB slave interface



Supports DMA data transmission through the 128-bit AXI master interface.



Supports the following UFS2.0 features:



-

Supports HS-G3, up to 5.8Gbps theoretically in the high-speed mode.

-

Symmetrical 2RX-2TX lanes

Supports the following UFS3.0 features:
-

Supports HS-G4, up to 11.6Gbps theoretically in the high-speed mode.

-

Supports PA_INIT error codes in UECDL register

-

Supports QOS indication of TX, RX and PA_INIT in the UECDL register



Supports 40-bit RMMI data interface



Supports MPHY rate mode
-

High speed: Gear 1/2/3/4 (Rate A or B)

-

Low speed: PWM Gear 1/2/3/4

11.3

SD/MMC Host Controller (SMHC)

11.3.1

Overview
The SMHC (SD-MMC Host controller) can be configured to support Secure Digital memory (SD
Memory), UHS-I Card, Secure Digital I/O (SDIO), Multimedia Cards (MMC), and eMMC.
The SMHC has the following features:






Four SD/MMC host controller (SMHC) interfaces
-

SMHC0, compliant with the protocol Secure Digital Memory (SD3.0)

-

SMHC1, compliant with the protocol Secure Digital I/O (SDIO3.0)

-

SMHC2 and SMHC3, compliant with the protocol Multimedia Card (eMMC5.1)

-

Supports one SD (Verson1.0 to 3.0) or MMC (Verson3.3 to 5.1)

The SMHC0 and the SMHC1 support the following:
-

1-bit or 4-bit data width

-

Maximum performance:


SDR mode 200 MHz@1.8 V IO pad



DDR mode 50 MHz@1.8 V IO pad



SDR mode 50 MHz@3.3 V IO pad

The SMHC2 and the SMHC3 supports the following:
-

1-bit, 4-bit, or 8-bit data width

-

Maximum performance


SDR mode 200 MHz@1.8V IO pad



DDR mode 200 MHz@1.8V IO pad



DDR mode 50 MHz@3.3V IO pad



SDR mode 50 MHz@3.3V IO pad



Supports block size of 1 to 65535 bytes



Supports hardware CRC generation and error detection



Supports eMMC boot operation and alternative boot operation



Supports command queue for eMMC V5.1 device



Supports host pull-up control



Supports Command Completion signals and interrupts to host processor, and Command
Completion signal disable



Programmable baud rate



Supports descriptor-based internal DMA controller
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

11.3.5

Functional Description

11.3.5.1

Data Path
The SMHC and SD/SDIO/eMMC contains the following interface buses: CLK, CMD, and DATA 1/4.
During one clock cycle, the SMHC can transmit 1-bit command with one or two bits’ data in
1-ch DATA mode, or four or eight bits’ data in 4-ch DATA mode. The CMD is a bidirectional
channel for initializing the SD/SDIO/eMMC and transmitting commands, and it can work in the
open-drain mode and push-pull mode. The DATA is also a bidirectional channel, and it works in
the push-pull mode.


Reading Data from the SD/SDIO/eMMC

The register configures the signals for the read operation, and synchronizes the signals to the
SMHC clock domain. Then the Data RX reads data from the SD/SDIO/eMMC via the
CLK/CMD/DATA interface buses and writes the data in the FIFO. After that, the DMAC transfers the
data from the FIFO to the memory.


Writing Data to the SD/SDIO/eMMC

The register configures the signals for the write operation, and synchronize the signals to the
SMHC clock domain. Then the DMAC reads data from the memory and writes the data to the FIFO.
After that, the Data TX reads the data from the FIFO and writes the data to the SD/SDIO/eMMC via
the CLK/CMD/DATA interface buses.
11.3.5.2

Package Format
Data transfer over the SD/eMMC bus is based on command and data bit streams that are
initiated by a start bit and terminated by a stop bit. There are three types of SD/eMMC packets:
command token, response token, and data packet.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

411

Confidential
Command Tokens
The command token starts an operation. A command is sent from the host to a device. It is
transferred serially on the CMD line. Command tokens have the following coding scheme:
Figure 11-3 Command Token Format

parameter, protected by 7-bit CRC checksum

Always‘0’

Each command token has 48 bits, preceded by a start bit (‘0’) and succeeded by an end bit
(‘1‘). To detect transmission errors, each token is protected by CRC bits.
Response Tokens
After receiving a command, the card returns a 48-bit or 136-bit response based on the command
type.
A response token is sent from the device to the host as an answer to a previously received
command. It is transferred serially on the CMD line.

11.3.5.4

Internal DMA Controller
The SMHC has an internal DMA controller (IDMAC) to transfer data between the host memory and
SMHC port. With a descriptor, the IDMAC can efficiently move data from the source to destination
by automatically loading the next DMA transfer arguments, which needs less CPU intervention.
Before transferring data in the IDMAC, the host driver should construct a descriptor list, configure
arguments of every DMA transfer, and then launch the descriptor and start the DMA.
The IDMAC has an interrupt controller. When enabled, it generates an interrupt to the HOST CPU
in situations such as data transmission is completed or some error happens.
IDMAC Descriptor Structure
The IDMAC uses a descriptor with a chain structure, and each descriptor points to a unique buffer
and the next descriptor.

Phase Offset of the Command and Data

To obtain the command phase or data phase in output timing, follow the steps blow:
Step 1

Configure the MODE_SEL (bit [31]) and HS400_NEW_SAM_EN (bit [0]) of SMHC_NTSR
(offset: 0x005C) to choose the timing mode.

Step 2

Configure the DAT_DRV_PH_SEL (bit [17]) to select data drive phase offset and configure
CMD_DRV_PH_SEL (bit [16]) to select command drive phase offset in SMHC_DRV_DL
(offset: 0x0140)
