Programming Guidelines
Initialization
Before data and commands are exchanged between a card and the SMHC, the SMHC needs to be
initialized. The following takes SMHC0-2 as an example to initialize the SMHC:
Step 1

Configure the corresponding GPIO register as an SMHC in the section GPIO to reset clock
by writing 1 to SMHCx_BGR_REG [SMHCx_RST](x=0, 1, 2, 3), and open clock gating by
writing 1 to SMHCx_BGR_REG[SMHCx_GATING] (x=0, 1, 2, 3); select clock sources and set
the division factor by configuring the SMHCx_CLK_REG (x=0, 1, 2, 3) register.

Step 2

Configure SMHC_CTRL to reset the FIFO and controller, and enable the global interrupt;
configure SMHC_INTMASK to 0xFFCE to enable the common interrupts and the
interrupts caused by error/anomaly, and then register the interrupt function.

Step 3

Configure SMHC_CLKDIV to open clock for devices. Configure SMHC_CMD as the change
clock command (for example 0x80202000). Send the update clock command to deliver
clock to devices.

Step 4

Configure SMHC_CMD as a normal command. Configure SMHC_CMDARG to set
command parameters. Configure SMHC_CMD to set parameters like the command
sequence, the response receive, the response type, the response length, the response
types to send the commands. According to the initialization process in the protocol, you
can finish SMHC initialization by sending the corresponding command one by one.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

422

Confidential
11.3.6.2

Single-block Write
To write a single block of data, follow the steps below:
Step 1

Write 0x1 to SMHC_CTRL[DMA_RST] to reset the internal DMA controller; write 0x82 to
SMHC_IDMAC to enable the IDMAC interrupt and configure AHB master burst transfers;
configure SMHC_IDIE to enable the transfer interrupt, receive interrupt, and abnormal
interrupt.

Step 2

Configure SMHC_FIFOTH to determine the burst size and TX/RX trigger level. For
example, if SMHC_FIFOTH is configured as 0x300F00F0, it indicates the burst size is 16,
TX_TL is 15, and RX_TL is 240. Configure SMHC_DLBA to determine the start address of
the DMA descriptor.

Step 3

To write one block data to sector1, configure SMHC_BYTCNT[BYTE_CNT] to 0x200 and
configure the descriptor according to the data size; set the data sector address of
CMD24 (Single Data Block Write) to 0x1, write 0x80002758 to SMHC_CMD, and send
CMD24 command to write data to the device.

Step 4

Check whether SMHC_RINTSTS[CC] is 1. If yes, the command is sent successfully;
otherwise, continue to wait until timeout, and then exit the process.

Step 5

Check whether SMHC_IDST[TX_INT] is 1. If yes, the data transfer for writing DMA is
completed. Write 0x337 to SMHC_IDST to clear the interrupt flag. Otherwise, continue to
wait until timeout, and then exit the process.

Step 6

Check whether SMHC_RINTSTS[DTC] is 1. If yes, the data transfer and CMD24 writing
operations are completed. Otherwise, anomaly occurs. Read SMHC_RINTSTS and
SMHC_STATUS to query the existing anomaly.

Step 7

Send CMD13 command to query whether the device writing operation is completed and
returns to the idle status. For example, device RCA is 0x1234, first set SMHC_CMDARG to
0x12340000, write 0x8000014D to SMHC_CMD, go to step4 to ensure command transfer
is completed, and then check whether the highest bit of SMHC_RESP0 (CMD13 response)
is 1. If yes, the device is in the idle status, and the next command can be sent. Otherwise,
the device is in the busy status. Continue to send CMD13 to wait for the device to enter
the idle status until timeout.

11.3.6.3

Single-block Read
To read a single block of data, follow the steps below:
Step 1

Write 0x1 to SMHC_CTRL[DMA_RST] to reset the internal DMA controller; write 0x82 to
SMHC_IDMAC to enable the IDMAC interrupt and configure AHB master burst transfers;
configure SMHC_IDIE to enable the transfer interrupt, receive interrupt, and abnormal
interrupt.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

423

Confidential
Step 2

Configure SMHC_FIFOTH to determine the burst size and TX/RX trigger level. For
example, if SMHC_FIFOTH is configured as 0x300F00F0, it indicates the burst size is 16,
TX_TL is 15, and RX_TL is 240. Configure SMHC_DLBA to determine the start address of
the DMA descriptor.

Step 3

To read one block data from sector1, configure SMHC_BYTCNT[BYTE_CNT] to 0x200 and
configure the descriptor according to the data size; set the data sector address of
CMD17 command (Single Data Block Read) to 0x1, write 0x80002351 to SMHC_CMD, and
send CMD17 command to read data from the device to DRAM/SRAM.

Step 4

Check whether SMHC_RINTSTS[CC] is 1. If yes, the command is sent successfully;
otherwise, continue to wait until timeout, and then exit the process.

Step 5

Check whether SMHC_IDST[RX_INT] is 1. If yes, the data transfer for writing DMA is
completed. Write 0x337 to SMHC_IDST to clear the interrupt flag. Otherwise, continue to
wait until timeout, and then exit the process.

Step 6

Check whether SMHC_RINTSTS[DTC] is 1. If yes, data transfer and CMD17 reading
operation are completed. Otherwise, anomaly occurs. Read SMHC_RINTSTS and
SMHC_STATUS to query the existing abnormity.

11.3.6.4

Open-ended Multiple-Block Write
To write open-ended multiple data blocks, follow the steps below:
Step 1

Write 0x1 to SMHC_CTRL[DMA_RST] to reset the internal DMA controller; write 0x82 to
SMHC_IDMAC to enable the IDMAC interrupt and configure AHB master burst transfers;
configure SMHC_IDIE to enable the transfer interrupt, receive interrupt, and abnormal
interrupt.

Step 2

Configure SMHC_FIFOTH to determine the burst size and TX/RX trigger level. For
example, if SMHC_FIFOTH is configured as 0x300F00F0, it indicates the burst size is 16,
TX_TL is 15, and RX_TL is 240. Configure SMHC_DLBA to determine the start address of
the DMA descriptor.

Step 3

To

write

three

blocks

of

data

to

sectors

begin

with

sector0,

configure

SMHC_BYTCNT[BYTE_CNT] to 0x600 and configure the descriptor according to the data
size; set the data sector address of CMD25 command (Multiple Data Blocks Write) to 0x0,
write 0x80003759 to SMHC_CMD, and send CMD25 command to read data from the
device to DRAM/SRAM.
Step 4

Check whether SMHC_RINTSTS[CC] is 1. If yes, the command is sent successfully;
otherwise, continue to wait until timeout, and then exit the process.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

424

Confidential
Step 5

Check whether SMHC_IDST[TX_INT] is 1. If yes, the data transfer for writing DMA is
completed. Write 0x337 to SMHC_IDST to clear the interrupt flag. Otherwise, continue to
wait until timeout, and then exit the process.

Step 6

Check whether SMHC_RINTSTS[ACD] and SMHC_RINTSTS[DTC] are both 1. If yes, the
data transfer, CMD12 transfer, and CMD25 writing operations are completed. Otherwise,
abnormity exists. Read SMHC_RINTSTS and SMHC_STATUS to query the existing
abnormity.

Step 7

Send CMD13 command to query whether the device writing operation is completed and
returns to the idle status. For example, device RCA is 0x1234, first set SMHC_CMDARG to
0x12340000, write 0x8000014D to SMHC_CMD, go to step4 to ensure command transfer
completed, and then check whether the highest bit of SMHC_RESP0 (CMD13 response)
is 1. If yes, the device is in the idle status, and the next command can be sent. Otherwise,
the device is in the busy status. Continue to send CMD13 to wait for the device to enter
the idle status until timeout.

11.3.6.5

Open-ended Multiple-block Read
To read open-ended multiple data blocks, follow the steps below:
Step 1

Write 0x1 to SMHC_CTRL[DMA_RST] to reset the internal DMA controller; write 0x82 to
SMHC_IDMAC to enable the IDMAC interrupt and configure AHB master burst transfers;
configure SMHC_IDIE to enable the transfer interrupt, receive interrupt, and abnormal
interrupt.

Step 2

Configure SMHC_FIFOTH to determine the burst size and TX/RX trigger level. For
example, if SMHC_FIFOTH is configured as 0x300F00F0, it indicates the burst size is 16,
TX_TL is 15, and RX_TL is 240. Configure SMHC_DLBA to determine the start address of
the DMA descriptor.

Step 3

To read three blocks of data from sectors begin with sector0, configure
SMHC_BYTCNT[BYTE_CNT] to 0x600 and configure the descriptor according to the data
size; set the data sector address of CMD18 command (Multiple Data Blocks Read) to 0x0,
write 0x80003352 to SMHC_CMD, and send CMD18 command to read data to the device.
When the data transfer is completed, CMD12 will be sent automatically.

Step 4

Check whether SMHC_RINTSTS[CC] is 1. If yes, the command is sent successfully;
otherwise, continue to wait until timeout, and then exit the process.

Step 5

Check whether SMHC_IDST[RX_INT] is 1. If yes, the data transfer for writing DMA is
completed. Write 0x337 to SMHC_IDST to clear the interrupt flag. Otherwise, continue to
wait until timeout, and then exit the process.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

425

Confidential
Step 6

Check whether SMHC_RINTSTS[ACD] and SMHC_RINTSTS[DTC] are both 1. If yes, data
transfer, CMD12 transfer, and CMD18 reading operation are completed. Otherwise,
abnormity exists. Read SMHC_RINTSTS and SMHC_STATUS to query the existing
abnormity.

11.3.6.6

Pre-Defined Multiple-Block Write
To write pre-defined multiple data blocks, follow the steps below:
Step 1

Write 0x1 to SMHC_CTRL[DMA_RST] to reset the internal DMA controller; write 0x82 to
SMHC_IDMAC to enable the IDMAC interrupt and configure AHB master burst transfers;
configure SMHC_IDIE to enable the transfer interrupt, receive interrupt, and abnormal
interrupt.

Step 2

Configure SMHC_FIFOTH to determine the burst size and TX/RX trigger level. For
example, if SMHC_FIFOTH is configured as 0x300F00F0, it indicates the burst size is 16,
TX_TL is 15, and RX_TL is 240. Configure SMHC_DLBA to determine the start address of
the DMA descriptor.

Step 3

To write three blocks of data, configure SMHC_CMDARG to 0x3 to specify the number of
data blocks as three. Then write 0x80000157 to SMHC_CMD to send the CMD23
command. Check whether SMHC_RINTSTS[CC] is 1. If yes, the command is sent
successful; otherwise, continue to wait until timeout, and then exit the process.

Step 4

Configure SMHC_BYTCNT[BYTE_CNT] to 0x600 and configure the descriptor according
to the data size; set the data sector address of CMD25 command (Multiple Data Blocks
Write) to 0x0, write 0x80002759 to SMHC_CMD, and send CMD25 command to write data
to the device.

Step 5

Check whether SMHC_RINTSTS[CC] is 1. If yes, the command is sent successful;
otherwise, continue to wait until timeout, and then exit the process.

Step 6

Check whether SMHC_IDST[TX_INT] is 1. If yes, the data transfer for writing DMA is
completed. Write 0x337 to SMHC_IDST to clear the interrupt flag. Otherwise, continue to
wait until timeout, and then exit the process.

Step 7

Check whether SMHC_RINTSTS[DTC] is 1. If yes, the data transfer and CMD25 writing
operations are completed. Otherwise, abnormity exists. Read SMHC_RINTSTS and
SMHC_STATUS to query the existing abnormity.

Step 8

Send CMD13 command to query whether the device writing operation is completed and
returns to the idle status. For example, device RCA is 0x1234, first set SMHC_CMDARG to
0x12340000, write 0x8000014D to SMHC_CMD, go to step5 to ensure command transfer
completed, and then check whether the highest bit of SMHC_RESP0 (CMD13 response)
is 1. If yes, the device is in the idle status, and the next command can be sent. Otherwise,
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Follow the steps below to initialize the command queue:
Step 1

Initialize the eMMC. For detailed initialization steps, refer to section 11.3.6.1
Initialization.

Step 2

Send CMD6 to configure the timing mode and bus width. Send CMD16 to configure the

NOTE

be able to modified.

Step 4

Configure CQTDLBA register and CQTDLBAU register to set the base address of the task

Configure CQSSC1 register to set how to query the status of the device's task queue.

Step 6

Configure CQIC register to enable/disable interrupt, set interrupt count and timer
protection.

Step 7

Configure CQRMEM register to set which errors may trigger a RED interrupt.

Step 8

Configure CQCFG register to enable CQE activity.

eMMC CMDQ supports multiple operation modes, which could be selected by configuring the
CMDQ_MODE bit (bit [5:4]) of CQCFG register.
11.3.6.9

CMDP Mode

NOTE
a.

SMHC1 doesn’t support CMDP mode.

To enable the CMDP mode, write 1 to the CQE_EN bit (bit [0]) and configure the field value of
CMDQ_MODE bit (bit [5:4]) as 2’b00 in CQCFG register.
The CMDP mode only supports block data transfers for the following transfer modes and
commands:


Data transfer- single data block reading: CMD17



Data transfer- single data block writing: CMD24



Data transfer- pre-defined multiple data blocks reading: CMD23 --> CMD18



Data transfer- pre-defined multiple data blocks writing: CMD23 --> CMD25



Data transfer - open-ended multiple data blocks reading: CMD18 --> CMD12



Data transfer - open-ended multiple data blocks writing: CMD25 --> CMD12

In CMDP mode, the transfer descriptor and DCMD descriptor are the same as these in CMDQ
mode. The differences of task descriptor between CMDP mode and CMDQ mode are as follows.

Confidential
Offset: 0x0008
Bit

Read/Write

Register Name: SMHC_TMOUT
Default/Hex

Description
DTO_LMT
Data Timeout Limit
This field can set time of the Host wait for the data
from the Device.
Ensure to communicate with the Device,this field
must be set to maximum that greater than the time
N AC

.

About the N AC , the explanation is as follows:
When Host read data, data transmission from the
Device starts after the access time delay N AC
beginning from the end bit of the read
command(ACMD51,CMD8,CMD17,CMD18).
31:8

R/W

0xffffff

When Host read multiple block(CMD18),the next
block’s data transmission from the Device starts

after the access time delay N AC beginning from the
end bit of the previous block.
When Host write data, this value is no effect.
Note: Under the following 3 conditions, the timeout
limit is half of the set time.
1> DDR8 mode
2> DDR4 and SMHC_NTSR[MODE_SELEC](0x5C[31])
high
3> HS400 and
SMHC_NTSR[HS400_NEW_SAMPLE_EN](0x5C[0])
high
7:0

RTO_LMT

Interrupt Coalescing Timeout Value
Software uses this field to configure the maximum time

0x0428 Command Queuing Task Doorbell Register (Default Value: 0x0000_0000)

Using this register, software triggers CQE to process a new task.
Offset: 0x0428

Read/Write

Register Name: CQTDBR
Default/Hex

Description

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

472

Confidential
Offset: 0x0428
Bit

Read/Write

Register Name: CQTDBR
Default/Hex

Description
CQE_TDBR
Command Queuing Task Doorbell
Software shall configure TDLBA and TDLBAU, and
enable CQE in CQCFG before using this register.
Writing 1 to bit n of this register triggers CQE to
start processing the task encoded in slot
n of the TDL.
CQE always processes tasks in-order according to
the order submitted to the list by CQTDBR write
transactions.
CQE processes Data Transfer tasks by reading the
Task Descriptor and sending
QUEUED_TASK_PARAMS (CMD44) and
QUEUED_TASK_ADDRESS (CMD45)
commands to the device.
CQE processes DCMD tasks (in slot #31, when
enabled) by reading the Task Descriptor, and
generating the command encoded by its index and

31:0

R/W1S

0x0

argument.
The corresponding bit is cleared to ‘0’ by CQE in
one of the following events:
When a task execution is completed (with success
or error)
The task is cleared using CQTCLR register
All tasks are cleared using CQCTL register
CQE is disabled using CQCFG register
Software may initiate multiple tasks at the same
time (batch submission) by writing 1 to multiple
bits of this register in the same transaction.
In the case of batch submission:
CQE shall process the tasks in order of the task
index, starting with the lowest index.
If one or more tasks in the batch are marked with
QBR, the ordering of execution will be based on
said processing order.
Writing 0 by software shall have no impact on the
hardware, and will not change the value of the
register bit.

Default/Hex

Description
DTO_LMT
Data Timeout Limit
This field can set time of the Host wait for the data
from the Device.
Ensure to communicate with the Device,this field
must be set to maximum that greater than the time
N AC

.

About the N AC , the explanation is as follows:
When Host read data, data transmission from the
Device starts after the access time delay N AC
beginning from the end bit of the read
command(ACMD51,CMD8,CMD17,CMD18).
31:8

R/W

0xffffff

When Host read multiple block(CMD18),the next
block’s data transmission from the Device starts

after the access time delay N AC beginning from the
end bit of the previous block.
When Host write data, this value is no effect.
Note: Under the following 3 conditions, the timeout
limit is half of the set time.
1> DDR8 mode
2> DDR4 and SMHC_NTSR[MODE_SELEC](0x5C[31])
high
3> HS400 and
SMHC_NTSR[HS400_NEW_SAMPLE_EN](0x5C[0])
high

0x0428 Command Queuing Task Doorbell Register (Default Value: 0x0000_0000)

Confidential

Default/Hex

Description
CQE_TDBR
Command Queuing Task Doorbell
Software shall configure TDLBA and TDLBAU, and
enable CQE in CQCFG before using this register.
Writing 1 to bit n of this register triggers CQE to start
processing the task encoded in slot
n of the TDL.
CQE always processes tasks in-order according to the
order submitted to the list by CQTDBR write
transactions.
CQE processes Data Transfer tasks by reading the Task
Descriptor and sending QUEUED_TASK_PARAMS
(CMD44) and QUEUED_TASK_ADDRESS (CMD45)

command encoded by its index and argument.

31:0

R/W1S

0x0

The corresponding bit is cleared to ‘0’ by CQE in one
of the following events:
When a task execution is completed (with success or
error)
The task is cleared using CQTCLR register
All tasks are cleared using CQCTL register
CQE is disabled using CQCFG register
Software may initiate multiple tasks at the same time
(batch submission) by writing 1 to multiple bits of this
register in the same transaction.
In the case of batch submission:
CQE shall process the tasks in order of the task index,
starting with the lowest index.
If one or more tasks in the batch are marked with QBR,
the ordering of execution will be based on said
processing order.
Writing 0 by software shall have no impact on the
hardware, and will not change the value of the register
bit.

11.4

NAND Flash Controller (NDFC)
The NDFC is the NAND Flash Controller which supports all NAND flash memory available in the
market. New type flash can be supported by software re-configuration.
The On-the-fly error correction code (ECC) is built-in NDFC for enhancing reliability. BCH is
implemented and it can detect and correct up to 80 bits’ error per 1024 bytes’ data. The
on-chip ECC and parity checking circuitry of NDFC frees CPU for other tasks. The ECC function
can be disabled by software.
The data can be transferred by DMA or by CPU memory-mapped IO method. The NDFC provides
automatic timing control for reading or writing external Flash. The NDFC maintains the proper
relativity for CLE, CE# and ALE control signal lines. There are three different kinds of modes for
serial read access, mode0 is for conventional serial access, mode1 is for EDO type and the mode2
is for extension EDO type. NDFC can monitor the status of R/B# signal line. Block management
and wear leveling management are implemented in software.
The NDFC has the following features:


Supports all SLC/MLC flash and EF-NAND memory available in the market



Software configure seed for randomize engine



Software configure method for adaptability to a variety of system and memory types



Supports 2CE/2RB



Supports 8-bit Data Bus Width



Supports 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768 bytes’ size per page



Supports Conventional and EDO serial access method for serial reading Flash



On-the-fly BCH error correction code which correcting up to 80 bits per 1024 bytes



Corrected Error bits’ number information report



ECC automatic disable function for all 0xff data



NDFC status information is reported by its’ registers and interrupt is supported



One Command FIFO



Supports internal DMA controller based on chain-structured descriptor list



Two 256x32-bit RAM for Pipeline Procession



Supports SDR, ONFI DDR1.0, Toggle DDR1.0, ONFI DDR2.0 and Toggle DDR2.0 RAW NAND
FLASH



Supports the Maximum IO Rate of Mass Production 50MHz in SDR mode, the Mass
Production 100MHz in DDR1.0 mode, and the Mass Production 150MHz in DDR2.0 mode



Supports self ‒debug for NDFC debug

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

530

Confidential

11.5

SPI Flash Controller (SPIF)

11.5.1

Overview
The SPI is a synchronous, serial communication interface which allows rapid data
communication with fewer software interrupts. Different from SPI, this SPIF is typically designed
for higher speed Flash devices and it only works at Master mode.
The SPI_Flash has the following features:




Supports multiple SPI mode
-

Standard SPI (3-Wire/4-Wire SPI)

-

Dual-Output/Dual-Input SPI and Dual I/O SPI

-

Quad-Output/Quad-Input SPI, Quad I/O SPI, and QPI

-

Octal-Input/Octal-Output SPI, Octal I/O SPI, and OPI

-

Programmable serial data frame length: 1 bit to 32 bits

Supports Prefetch mode of operation for executing code from FLASH memory, which
significantly reduces read time



Supports Single Transfer Rate (STR) mode and Dual Transfer Rate (DTR) mode, and DTR
mode supports DQS signal





High Speed Clock Frequency
-

150MHz for STR Mode

-

100MHz for DTR Mode

Software Write Protection
-

Write protection for all/portion of memory via software

-

Top/Bottom Block protection



Programmable delay between transactions



Supports Mode0, Mode1, Mode2 and Mode3



Supports control signal configuration
-

Up to one chip select to support multiple peripherals

-

Polarity and phase of the Chip Select (SPIF_CS) and SPI Clock (SPIF_CLK) are
configurable

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

SPI Clock Mode
The SPI Flash supports 4 different modes for data transfer. Software can select one of the four
modes in which the SPI works by setting the bit5(SPI_CPOL) and bit4(SPI_CPHA) of SPI Global
Control Register[0x0004].
The SPI_CPOL defines the signal polarity when SPIF_CLK is in the idle state. The SPIF_CLK is high
level when POL is '1 'and it is low level when POL is '0'. The SPI_CPHA decides whether the
leading edge of SPIF_CLK is used for setup or sample data. The leading edge is used for setup
data when PHA is '1' and for sample data when PHA is '0'. The four kind of modes are listed
Table:
Table 11-14 SPI Flash Modes with Clock Polarity and Phase

During Phase 0, Polarity 0 and Phase 1, Polarity 1 operations, output data changes on the falling
edge and input data is shifted in on the rising edge.
During Phase 1, Polarity 0 and Phase 0, Polarity 1 operations, output data changes on the rising
edges and is shifted in on falling edges.
The Bit Mode only supports Phase 0, Polarity 0 operation; the most significant bit (MSB) of data is
transmitted first which is not configurable.

STR & DTR
In the SPI mode 0 and mode 3, the input data of devices will be latched at the rising edge of SCK,
and the output data can be used at the falling edge of SCK.
Figure 11-15 SPI STR Transfer

As with the STR command, the instruction bit is latched at the rising edge of the clock in the DTR
command. However, after that, the address and input data are latched at the dual edge. After the
instruction bit is latched at the falling edge of SCK, the first address bit will be latched at the next
rising edge of SCK. The first output data bit will be sent at the falling edge of the last access
latency period.
As with the STR command, the SCK period is obtained by measuring the cycle between two
adjacent SCK falling edges. In the mode 0, the SCK is already at a low level when some command
starts to be executed, thus the first SCK period during the command execution indicates the
cycle from the falling edge of CS# to the first falling edge of SCK.
Figure 11-16 SPI DTR Transfer Example, 1-4-4

DQS
DQS signal indicates input/output data valid for DTR modes and is required to support
high-speed data. When data strobe function is enabled, DQS signal will be driven to ground once
CS# goes LOW till the device is driving output data, in which case DQS toggles to synchronize
data output. When data strobe function is not enabled, DQS signal will not be driven.
Figure 11-18 SPI DTR Transfer with DQS Input Clock Signal

11.5.5.4

SPI Chip Select Signal
The SPIF supports one chip select signal, which can be activated by the SPI_CS_SEL (bit[7:6]) of
SPI_GLOBAL_CTRL. The polarities of CS signals can be configured by the SPI_CS_POL (bit[5]) of
SPI_GLOBAL_CTRL.
The various intervals of CS signals can be configured by SPI_CS_DELAY. The specific
configuration steps are as follows.
Step 1

Delay CSSOT and output the effective data after CS is enabled.

Step 2

Delay CSEOT at the rising edge of last valid data, and disable CS.

Step 3

After the CS is disabled, the interval between enabling CS and disabling CS is CSDA.

Figure 11-19 SPI CS Select Timing Relation

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

538

Confidential
11.5.5.5

SPI Transfer Mode
SPI supports multiple transfer modes such as SPI Bit Mode, SPI Standard Mode, SPI Dual Mode,
SPI Quad Mode, and SPI Octal Mode. Their main differences lie in the number of wires. Even in
the same transfer mode, the subdivision modes will be further derived based on the number of
wires used to data transfer. The number of data lines used by Command-Address-Data is
specified on the subdivision pattern heading in the manner of X-X-X. For example, one Data line
for Commend, two for Address, and two for data, are identified as (1-2-2).
SPI Bit Mode (3-Wire/4-Wire)
For some specific scenarios, the devices such as the sensor take the SPI interfaces as the
communication protocol. Generally, their data volume is relatively small, and some devices
support three wires, so the SPI Bit Mode is added, and 3-wire mode and 4-wire mode are
subdivided, which includes SPIF_CS, SPIF_CLK, and 1/2 data line. The transmission length
ranges from 1-32bit.
The 4-Wire Mode is selected when the Work Mode Select(bit[1:0]) is equal to 0x3 in the SPI
Bit-Aligned Transfer Configure Register. In SPI 4-Wire Mode, the input data and output data use
the independent two data lines. The MISO is used for inputting data, and the MOSI is used for
outputting data.
The SPI 3-Wire Mode is only valid when the SPI controller works as Master Device, and selected
when the Work Mode Select(bit[1:0]) is equal to 0x2 in the SPI Bit-Aligned Transfer Configure
Register. In the 3-Wire mode, the input data and the output data use the same single data line.
The following figure describe this mode.

SPI Dual Mode
Using the dual mode allows data to be transferred to or from the device at two times the rate of
standard single mode SPI devices. Data can be read at a faster speed using two data bits (MOSI
and MISO) at a time. The following describe the Dual Input/Dual Output SPI (1-1-2), the Dual IO
SPI (1-2-2), and the (2-2-2) SPI Mode.


SPI Dual Input/dual Output Mode (1-1-2)

In the dual Input/dual Output SPI, the command, address, and the dummy bytes are output in
the unit of a single bit in serial mode through SPIF_MOSI line. Only the data bytes are output
(write) and input (read) in unit of dual bits through the SPIF_MOSI and SPIF_MISO.
Figure 11-25 SPI Dual Input/Dual Output Mode（1-1-2）

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

541

Confidential


SPI Dual IO Mode (1-2-2)

In the Dual IO SPI, only the command bytes are output in the unit of a single bit in serial mode
through SPIF_MOSI line. The address bytes and the dummy bytes are output in the unit of dual
bits through the SPIF_MOSI and SPIF_MISO. And the data bytes are output (write) and input
(read) in the unit of dual bits through the SPIF_MOSI and SPIF_MISO.
Figure 11-26 SPI Dual Input/Dual Output Mode (1-2-2)

SPI Quad Mode
Using the quad mode allows data to be transferred to or from the device at 4 times the rate of
standard single mode SPI devices, data can be read at fast speed using four data bits (MOSI,
MISO, IO2(WP#) and IO3(HOLD#)) at the same time. The following describe the Quad Input/Quad
Output SPI (1-1-4), 1-4-4 mode, and 4-4-4 mode.


Quad Input/Quad Output SPI (1-1-4)

In the Quad Input/Quad Output SPI, the command, address, and the dummy bytes are output in
unit of a single bit in serial mode through SPIF_MOSI line. Only the data bytes are output (write)
and input(read) in unit of quad bits through the SPIF_MOSI, SPIF_MISO, SPIF_WP# and
SPIF_HOLD#.
Figure 11-27 SPI Quad Input/Quad Output Mode (1-1-4)

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1-4-4 Mode



4-4-4 Mode

SPI Octal Mode
The Octal SPI Mode allow data to be transferred to or from the device at eight times the rate of
the standard SPI. When using the Octal SPI, there are 8 data wires.

11.5.5.6

Prefetch Mode
If the CPU wants to directly access Flash, the prefetch mode is needed to improve efficiency. In
the prefetch mode, the CPU continues fetching instructions from flash and cache them (The
maximum cache size is 128 Bytes.). Then HREADY_I should be controlled by handshake to send
back the instructions to CPU through AHB.

11.5.5.7

SPI Flash Private DMA
The private DMA adopts the chained descriptor structure. The address and size of the first
descriptor are configured by registers. After getting the first descriptor, the hardware will obtain
the data from the address recorded in the descriptors. When the current transfer finishes, the
hardware will continue to obtain descriptors based on the address of the next descriptor given
by the previous descriptor until the terminal character is found. Then, a DMA transfer ends.

System Setup
Configure SPI Pin
Program the GPIO to configure the SPI PIN.
Configure SPI Clock and Reset
Configure SPI ref clock, AHB Clock, De-assert SPI ref Reset, and AHB reset in the section CCU.
Configure SPI Internal Clock
Step 1

Configure clock source (SPI_TIMING_CFG[0x000C])


STR Mode
Write 0 to the CLK_SPI_SRC_SEL bit (bit [24]), the CLK_SCK_SRC_SEL bit (bit [25])
bit, and the CLK_SCKOUT_SRC_SEL bit (bit [26]) bit.



DTR Mode
Write 0 to the CLK_SPI_SRC_SEL bit (bit [24]) and the CLK_SCK_SRC_SEL bit (bit
[25]) bit.
Write 1 to the CLK_SCKOUT_SRC_SEL bit (bit [26]) bit.

NOTE
When the value of the CLK_SCKOUT_SRC_SEL (bit [26]) bit is 1, the real output clock frequency of
SPIF-CLK signal is the SPIFC clock frequency divided by 2.
Step 2

Generate the sckr of SPI data receiving


Configure SCKR delay mode (SPI_TIMING_CFG[0x000C]).
SCKR_DLY_MODE_SEL (bit [20]): Select delay mode. Writing 0 is the digital delay,
and writing 1 is the digital and analog delay.



Configure the digital delay of SCKR
SPI_TIMING_CFG[0x000C], DIGITAL_SCKR_DELAY_CFG (bit[18:16]): digital delay
volume. The step length is 0.5 clock.



Configure the analog delay of SCKR
SPI_TIMING_CFG[0x000C], ANALOG_SAMP_DL_SW_VALUE (bit[5:0])

Step 3

Generate SPI output clock


Select SPI working mode (SPI_MODE). Refer to the section SPI Clock Mode for more
details.



Configure SPI_GLOBAL_CTRL[0x0004]:
SPI_CPOL (bit [5]): Clock Polarity

Confidential



DTR switch（SPI_GLOBAL_CTRL[0x0004]）
DTR_EN (bit [16]): It is closed by default. When it is closed, the output clock
frequency is same to that of SCKR and SCKT; when it is open, the output clock
frequency is half that of SCKR and SCKT.

SPI Interface Public Configuration
Step 1

CS Delay Configuration: SPI_CS_DELAY[0x001C]


CSDA (bit [23:16]): The intervals of two adjacent CS enable is recommended to be
no less than 6sclk. The actual value is CSDA+1.



CSEOT (bit [15:8]): After the SCLK_OUT is invalid, the CS signal will be de-asserted
after CSEOT SCLK. The minimum interval is 1sclk. The actual value is CSEOT+1.



CSSOT (bit [7:0]): After the SCLK_OUT is valid, the CS signal will be asserted after
CSSOT SCLK. The minimum interval is 1sclk. The actual value is CSSOT+1.

Step 1

Configure the length and the starting address of storage location for the first descriptor.
Then, finish the following operations to complete DMA Configuration.


Descriptor0


AHB Master Burst Type Configuration
HBURST_TYPE (bit [6:4]): Supports SINGLE/INCR4/INCR8/INCR16 mode.



DMA Transfer Direction Configuration
DMA_DIR (bit [1]): DMA read or DMA write.



DMA Finish Flag
DMA_FINISH_FLAG (bit [0]): Currently the memory space allocated by the CPU
to DMA may be a part of the total data volume to be transferred. For instance,
the 256 Byte memory space is allocated to transfer 1 MB data. In this situation,
a DMA descriptor merely points to the allocated 256 Byte data location, and it
will also point to the next descriptor to fetch data. When the data of the last
descriptor is fetched, the stop bit should be pulled up to terminate a DMA
handling.



Descriptor1


DMA_BLK_LEN ([31:16])
DMA BLK length. It indicates the size of each DMA packet, with multiples of 8
Byte aligned to achieve the optimized rate when accessing storage.



DMA_DATA_LEN (bit [15:0])

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

553

Confidential
It indicates the data volume indicated by the current descriptor of DMA.


Descriptor2
It indicates the data storage location of current descriptor.



Descriptor3
It indicates the storage location of the next descriptor.



Descriptor4-7
The SPI configuration parameters. In the course of setting parameters with DMA for
SPI, the content of descriptors is configured to SPI.

Enable SPI
Write 1 to the SPI_NMODE_EN in the SPI_GLOBAL_CTRL, then it will be auto pulled down.
11.5.6.2

CPU Transfer
The software operation of CPU transfer is almost the same as DMA transfer. However, there are
still two main differences.
One difference is that when the CPU transfers, channel parameter cannot come from DMA
descriptors. SPI_GLOBAL_CTRL[0x0004], SPI_CFG_MODE(bit[0]) must be set to 0. All parameters
should come from REGISTER FILE. SPI_GLOBAL_CTRL[0x0004], SPI_CPU_MODE_EN(bit[20]) is
used to start CPU transfer (Different from descriptor and SPI_GLOBAL_CTRL[0x0004],
SPI_NMODE_EN(bit[2])).
The other difference is that when reading data from Register [0x0210], it is recommended to read
SPI_CDC_FIFO_STA[0x0050], RF_CNT([bit5-0]), especially when total read number is not integer
multiple of trigger level. When writing data to Register [0x0220], it is always ready as long as
trigger level is not reached.
NOTE
Register [0x0040] and [0x0044] are not used in CPU transfer.

11.5.6.3

Auto Status Reading
The software operation of status reading is almost the same as CPU transfer. CMD_TRANS_EN
and RX_DATA_EN must be set high because RX data path is used for status reading.
MODE_BIT_TRANS_EN and DUMMY_BIT_TRANS_EN should be set accordingly. But STATUS
OPCODE will not go through READ_FIFO and READ_BUFFER. Meanwhile, I/O Pins used should be
set accordingly. SPI_STATUS_READ[0x0068] and SPI_STATUS_READ_2[0x006C] are used for
STATUS READING. And to avoid endless reading and dead lock, the CPU should tell the maximum
reading times. Then, to start STATUS READING, SPI_READ_STATUS_MODE_EN should be set. In
this mode, DATA_TRANS_NUM (002C, [15:0]) is suggested to be 1 and DTR_EN [0x0004, bit 16] is
suggested to be 0.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

554

Confidential
11.5.6.4

Prefetch
The software operation of PREFETCH is almost the same as CPU transfer.
The System Setup part, SPI Initialization part and Channel Setup part is the same as DMA
transfer.
After the basic initialization and setup, enable SPI_GLOBAL_CTRL[0x0004], SPI_PMODE_EN(bit 3)
to enter PREFETCH mode. Then directly read in prefetch area to get data; for details, see the
section Memory Map.

CAUTION
a)

DQS function is not supported in the prefetch mode. As in this mode, if the DQS of external
devices goes wrong, it may lead to hang.

b)

11.5.7

LSB first operation is supported in the prefetch mode.

12 Interrupts
12.1

Interrupt Controller

12.1.1

Overview
The Interrupt Control module is used to handle interrupt coalescing and provide interrupt
recording in multi-core systems. This module provides an independent interrupt processing
mechanism for each core to adapt to the limitations of different cores on the number of
interrupts.
This module has the following features:

12.1.2



Interrupt coalescing



Interrupt recording

Block Diagram
The following figure shows the block diagram of the interrupt controller.
Figure 12-1 Interrupt Controller Block Diagram

INTERRUPT_CTRL

IRQ

12.1.3

INT_REG
RV_INT_CTRL

E902

CPUS_INT_CTRL

OR100

Functional Description
Interrupt Coalescing
Different cores will use independent interrupt coalescing schemes and interrupt mask registers.
Software can allocate interrupts according to respective scheme. After the chip is powered up,
software can mask the interrupts that need responding resources and do not belong to its own
core.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

582

Confidential
Interrupt Recording
When the coalesced interrupt is triggered, this module provides interrupt recording registers,
namely, system interrupt state registers. Software can query the flag bit to get the interrupt
number of the specific module that initiated the interrupt.

12.2 Generic Interrupt Controller (GIC)
12.2.1 Overview
The GIC is a generic interrupt controller that handles the interrupts from peripherals to the cores
and between cores. The GIC supports a distributed microarchitecture containing several
individual blocks that are used to provide a flexible GIC implementation.
All the GIC blocks communicate through fully credited AXI4-Stream interface channels. This
means that the interface exerts transient backpressure only on their ic<xy>tready signals,
enabling packets to be routed over any free-flowing interconnect. Channels can be routed over
dedicated AXI4-Stream buses, or over any available free-flowing transport layer in the system. A
channel is described as free-flowing if all transactions on that channel complete without a
non-transient dependency on any other transaction.
The GIC includes build scripts that can create appropriate levels of hierarchy for any particular
configuration. In small configurations, the distribution can be hidden and internally optimized.
the GIC has the following features:


Interrupt services and masking:
-

Supports the following interrupt types:


Up to 56000 LPIs. A peripheral generates these interrupts by writing to a
memory-mapped register in the GIC-600.



Up to 960 SPIs in groups of 32.



Up to 16 PPIs that are independent for each core and can be programmed to
support either edge triggered or level-sensitive interrupts.


-

Up to 16 SGIs that are generated through the GIC CPU interface of a core.

Up to 16 ITS modules that provide device isolation and ID translation for message-based
interrupts and enable virtual machines to program devices directly.



Interrupt masking and prioritization with 32 priority levels, five bits per interrupt.

Registers and programming
-

Flexible affinity routing, using the Multiprocessor Identification Register (MPIDR)
addresses, including support for all four affinity levels.

-

Single ACE-Lite slave port on each chip for programming of all GIC Distributor (GICD)
registers, GIC Interrupt Translation Service (GITS) registers, and GIC Redistributor (GICR)
registers. Each ITS has an optional ACE-Lite slave port for programming the
GITS_TRANSLATER register.



Coherent view of SPI register data across multiple chips.

Security
-

A global Disable Security (DS) bit. This bit enables support for systems without security.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

589

Confidential
-

The following interrupt groups allow interrupts to target different exception levels:


Group 0.



Non-secure Group 1.



Secure Group 1.



Performance Monitoring Unit (PMU) counters with snapshot functionality.



Error correction: ARMv8.2 Reliability Accessibility Serviceability (RAS) architecture-compliant
error reporting for the following:
-

Software access errors

-

ITS command and translation errors

-

Error Correcting Code (ECC) errors

12.3 Core-Local Interrupt Controller (CLIC)
12.3.1 Overview
The Core-Local Interrupt Controller (CLIC) is only used for sampling, priority arbitration and
distribution for external interrupt sources.


Supports RISC-V Core-Local Interrupt Controller Version 0.8 specification



Up to 64 configurable external interrupt sources that support level interrupts and pulse
interrupts; compatible with up to 16 interrupts of CLINT



8 levels of interrupt priority



4 memory-mapped control registers for each interrupt



Supports registers like MSCRATCHCSW and MSCRATCHCSWL for the purpose of exchanging
stack pointers in the interrupt handler function.

13 DMA
13.1

DMA Controller (DMAC)

13.1.1

Overview
The direct memory access (DMA) is a method of transferring data between peripherals and
memories (including the SRAM and DRAM) without using the CPU. The data can be transferred
between a peripheral and a memory, between peripherals, or between memories through DMA.
It is an efficient way to offload data transfer duties from the CPU.
The DMAC has the following features:


Two 16-channel DMAs. One is in CPUX domain and the other is in CPUS domain.



Supports DMA channel number configuration through parameters



Supports reading or writing up to 64 peripheral DMA requests



Supports chained transfer



Supports programmable 8-/16-/32-/64-bit data width



Supports programmable DMA burst length



DRQ response includes waiting mode and handshake mode



Supports non-aligned transfer for memory devices



DMA channels support pausing, bmode, timeout, and IO speed mode

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

607

Confidential

The DMAC integrates 16 independent DMA channels and each channel has an independent FIFO
controller. When the DMA channel starts, the DMAC gets a DMA descriptor from the
DMA_DESC_ADDR_REG and uses it as the configuration information for the data transfer of the
current DMA package. Then the DMAC can transfer data between the specified devices. After
transferring a DMA package, the DMAC judges whether the current channel transfer is finished via
the linked address in the descriptor. If the linked address shows all the packages are transferred,
the DMAC will end the chain transmission and close the channel.

13.1.3

Clock Sources
The DMAC is mounted on AHB and MBUS. Their clock frequencies influence the transfer
efficiency of the DMAC.

13.1.4.2

SMHC3

SMHC3

DMAC Descriptor
The DMAC descriptor is the configuration information of DMA transfer and decides the DMA
working mode. Each descriptor includes 6 words: Configuration, Source Address, Destination
Address, Byte Counter, Parameter, and Link.


Configuration: It is mainly used for configuring the following information by DMA_CFG_REG.
-

DRQ type: DRQ type of the source and destination devices.

-

Address counting mode: For both the source and destination devices, there are two
address counting modes: the IO mode and linear mode. The IO mode is for IO devices
whose address is fixed during the data transfer and the linear mode is for the memory
whose address is increasing during the data transfer.

-

Transferred block length: The amount of data that non-memory peripherals can transfer
in a valid DRQ. The block length supports 1 beat, 4 beats, 8 beats, and 16 beats.

-

Transferred data width: The data width of operating the non-memory peripherals. The
data width supports 8 bits, 16 bits, 32 bits, and 64 bits.

-

BMODE mode: It is used in the following scenario: the source is an IO device, and the
destination is a memory device. In this mode, the data amount of DMA block
transmission can be limited to that when the DRQ threshold of source IO device is 1.



Source Address: It configures the address of the source device.



Destination Address: It configures the address of the destination device. DMA reads data
from the source address and then writes data to the destination address.



Byte counter: It configures the data amount of a package. The maximum value is (2^25-1)
bytes. If the data amount of the package reaches the maximum value, even if DRQ is valid,
the DMA will stop the current transfer.



Parameter: It configures the interval of each data block and is only valid for non-memory
devices. When detecting that the DRQ holds high, the DMA will start block transmission
regardless of the DRQ change. When transmission ends, DMA will wait the set period and
continue to the next DRQ detection.
In addition, the Parameter is responsible for enabling and configuring TIMEOUT. In the case
that the source device is an I/O device and the destination device is a memory device, the
waiting time of a DRQ signal triggered by the source device can be set when TIMEOUT is
enabled. When time is out, an interrupt signal of TIMEOUT will be generated by DMA. There
are three sub-functions of TIMEOUT to be enabled (TIMEOUT will only generate interrupts if
they are disabled): suspend the transmission of the current channel after an interrupt is
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

611

Confidential
generated; end the transmission of the current channel after an interrupt is generated; skip
to the next descriptor for transmission after an interrupt is generated. (TIMEOUT only can be
enabled in BMODE.)
The Parameter also configures whether the IOspeed is enabled or not. If IOspeed is enabled,
DMA will transmit the data of the I/O device from the source device or the destination device,
or both of them at a faster speed. The larger block indicates a faster speed. However, when
the block is 1, the speed won’t change even if the IO speed is enabled.
If the address bit of the link and parameter is 0xFFFFF800, the DMAC will stop the data
transfer after transferring the package; if the address bit of the link and parameter is not
0xFFFFF800, the address bit will be considered as the address of the next package
configuration, which is called the chained multi-package transfer.
Figure 13-2 DMA Chained Transfer

13.1.4.3

Interrupts
There are four kinds of DMA interrupts: the half package interrupt, package end interrupt, queue
end interrupt, and timeout interrupt.


Half package interrupt

When enabled, the DMAC sends out a half package interrupt after transferring half of a package.


Package end interrupt

When enabled, the DMAC sends out a package end interrupt after transferring a complete
package.


Queue end interrupt

When enabled, the DMAC sends out a queue end interrupt after transferring a complete queue.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

613

Confidential


Timeout interrupt

If TIMEOUT is enabled, DMA will generate a timeout interrupt after timeout.
Notice that when CPU does not respond to the interrupts timely, or two DMA interrupts are
generated very closely, the later interrupt may override the former one. As for CPU, the DMAC has
only a system interrupt source.
13.1.4.4

Security
The DMAC supports system TrustZone and the security mode configuration of the DMA channel.
Each DMA channel is secure by default. When the TrustZone is enabled, the DMAC is secure, only
the secure devices can access the DMAC.
When a DMA channel is configured to the non-secure mode, this channel can only access the
non-secure area of the memory, that is, the DMAC cannot write data to the secure area of the
memory, and the read-back data from the secure area of the memory is 0.

13.1.4.5

Clock Gating
The DMA_CLK_GATE module can auto control clock gating by hardware, which is mainly used for
generating clocks for DMAC sub-modules and some of their circuits.
The DMA_CLK_GATE module consists of two parts: the channel clock gate and the common clock
gate.
Channel Clock Gate: When the system accesses the registers of the enabled DMA channels, the
channel clock gate will be automatically open. When the system finishes accessing or the DMA
data transfer is completed, the channel clock gate will be automatically closed after a
16-HCLK-cycle delay; also, the related circuit clocks, such as channel control and FIFO control,
will be closed.
Common Clock Gate: When all the DMA channels are closed, the clock gates of common circuits
will be automatically closed. The common circuits include the common circuits of FIFO control
modules, MPORT modules, and MBUS.
Whether DMA clock gating can support all the functions stated above or not is decided by
software.

13.1.4.6

Transfer Mode
The peripherals initiate data transfer by transmitting DMA request signals to the DMAC. After
receiving the request signal, the DMAC converts it to the internal DRQ signal and controls the
DMA data transfer.
The DMAC supports two data transfer modes: the waiting mode and handshake mode.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

614

Confidential
Waiting Mode
a)

When the DMAC detects a valid external request signal, the DMAC starts to operate the
peripheral device. The internal DRQ always holds high before the transferred data amount
reaches the transferred block length.

b)

When the transferred data amount reaches the transferred block length, the internal DRQ
will pull low automatically.

c)

The internal DRQ holds low for certain clock cycles (WAIT_CYC), and then the DMAC restarts
to detect the external requests. If the external request signal is valid, then the next transfer
starts.

Handshake Mode
a)

When the DMAC detects a valid external request signal, the DMAC starts to operate the
peripheral device. The internal DRQ always holds high before the transferred data amount
reaches the transferred block length.

b)

When the transferred data amount reaches the transferred block length, the internal DRQ
will be pulled down automatically. For the last data transfer of the block, the DMAC sends a
DMA Last signal with the DMA commands to the peripheral device. The DMA Last signal will
be packed as part of the DMA commands and transmitted on the bus. It is used to inform the
peripheral device that it is the end of the data transfer for the current DRQ.

c)

When the peripheral device receives the DMA Last signal, it can judge that the data transfer
for the current DRQ is finished. To continue the data transfer, it sends a DMA Active signal to
the DMAC.
NOTE

A DMA Active signal will be converted to one DRQ signal in the DMA module. To generate multiple
DRQs, the peripheral devices need to send out multiple DMA Active signals via the bus protocol.
d)

When the DMAC receives the DMA Active signal, it will send back a DMA ACK signal to the
peripheral device.

e)

When the peripheral device receives the DMA ACK signal, it will wait for all the operations on
the local device to be completed, and both the FIFO and DRQ status are refreshed. Then it
invalidates the DMA Active signal.

f)

When the DMAC detects the falling edge of the DMA Active signal, it invalidates the
corresponding DMA ACK signal, and restarts to detect the external request signals. If a valid
request signal is detected, the next data transfer starts.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential

13.1.4.7

DEVICE

Address Auto-Alignment
For the non-IO devices whose start address is not 32-byte-aligned, the DMAC will align the
address to the 32-byte through the burst transfer within 32 bytes, which will improve the DRAM
access efficiency.
The following example shows how the DMAC adjusts the address: when the peripheral device of
a DMA channel is a non-IO device whose start address is 0x86 (not 32-byte-aligned), the DMAC
firstly uses a 26-byte burst transfer to align the address to 0xA0 (32-byte-aligned), and then
transfers data by 64-byte burst (the maximum transfer amount that MBUS allows).
The IO devices do not support address alignment, so the bit width of IO devices must match the
address offset; otherwise, the DMAC will ignore the inconsistency and directly transmit data of
the corresponding bit width to the address.
The address of the DMA descriptor does not support the address auto-alignment. Make sure the
address is word-aligned; otherwise the DMAC cannot identify the descriptor.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential

13.1.5

Programming Guidelines

13.1.5.1

DMAC Clock Control
a)

If the DMAC clock is synchronous with the AHB clock, enable the DMAC gating bit of AHB
clock before accessing the DMAC register.

b)

If the reset input signal of the DMAC is asynchronous with AHB0 and is low valid by default,
de-assert the reset signal of the DMAC before accessing the DMA register.

c)

To avoid the indefinite state within registers, de-assert the reset signal first, and then enable
the gating bit of AHB.

d)

As the DMAC supports Clock Auto Gating function, it will automatically disable the DMAC
clock in the idle state to reduce power consumption. The Clock Auto Gating is enabled by
default.

13.1.5.2

DMAC Transfer Procedure
The DMAC transfer procedure is as follows.
Step 1

Configure DMA_IRQ_CPU_EN_REG and DMA_IRQ_CPUS_EN_REG register to select an
channel interrupt to transmit to CPU field or CPUS field. If no configuration, the
interrupt will transmit to both CPU field and CPUS field.

Step 2

Request DMA channel, and check if the DMA channel is idle by checking if it is enabled. A
disabled channel indicates it is idle, while an enabled channel indicates it is busy.

Step 3

Write the descriptor with 6 words into the memory. The descriptor must be
word-aligned. For more details, refer to the section DMA Descriptor.

Step 4

Write

the

start

address

of

the

descriptor

to

DMA_DESC_ADDR_REG

and

DMA_DESC_HIG_ADDR_REG.
Step 5

Enable the DMA channel, and write the corresponding channel to DMA_EN_REG.

Step 6

The DMA obtains the descriptor information.

Step 7

Start to transmit a package. When half of the package is completed, the DMA sends a
Half Package Transfer Interrupt; when a total package is completed, the DMA sends a
Package

End

Transfer

Interrupt.

This

interrupt

status

can

be

read

by

DMA_IRQ_PEND_REG.
Step 8

Set DMA_PAU_REG to pause or resume the data transfer.

Step 9

After completing a total package transfer, the DMA decides to start the next package
transfer or end the transfer by the link of the descriptor. If the link is 0xFFFFF800, the
transfer ends; otherwise, the next package starts to transmit. When the transfer ends,
the DMA sends a Queue End Transfer Interrupt.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

617

Confidential
Step 10 Disable the DMA channel.

13.1.5.3

Interrupt Processing
Follow the steps below to process the DMAC interrupt:
Step 1

Write the corresponding interrupt enable bit of DMA_IRQ_EN_REG. The system
generates an interrupt when the corresponding condition is satisfied.

Step 2

After entering the interrupt process, write to clear the interrupt pending and execute the
process of waiting for the interrupt.

Step 3

Resume the interrupt and continue to execute the interrupted process.

14 Video & Graphics Engine
14.1

Video Encoder
The Video Encoding consists of the video encoding unit(VE) and JPEG encoder(JPEG). The VE
supports H.264 and H.265 encoding, JPEG supports JPEG/MJPEG encoding.

14.1.1

VE
The VE is a CODEC that supports H.264 and H.265 protocol based on ASIC. It is custom-made for
the IPC usage and features high compressing rate, low CPU usage, short delay and low power
consumption.
The VE has the following features:


Supports ITU-T H.264 High profile /Main profile /Baseline profile @Level 4.2 encoding, up to
4K@30fps
-

Supports the output picture format of semi-planar YCbCr4:2:0

-

Motion compensation with 1/2- or 1/4- pixel precision

-

Search Range [H:+/-128, V: +/-24]

-

Four prediction unit (PU) types of 16x16, 16x8, 8x16 and 8x8 for inter-prediction

-

Three PU types of 16x16, 8x8 and 4x4 for intra-prediction

-

Transform 4x4 and transform 8x8

-

CABAC and CAVLC entropy encoding

-

In-loop deblocking filter

-

Multi-slice encoding

-

Supports

normal

functions:

Macro-block

rate

control,

intra-refresh,

inter-only-in-P-frame
-

Supports special functions: dynamic search window range

-

Supports region of interest(ROI) encoding with custom QP map

-

Supports three-bit rate control modes: constant bit rate(CBR), variable bit rate(VBR),
and FIXEDQP.



-

Supports lossless compression for reference frame.

-

Supports OSD front-end overlaying

Supports ITU-T H.265 Main Profile @Level 5.0 Main-Tier encoding, up to 4K@30fps
-

-

embedded hardware Video Engine(VE). VCF gets the bitstream from topper software, parses
bitstream, invokes the Video Engine, and generates the decoding image sequence. The decoder
image sequence is transmitted by the video output controller to the display device under the
control of the topper software.

14.3

Display Engine (DE)
The Display Engine (DE) is a hardware composer to transfer image layers from a local bus or a
video buffer to the LCD interface. The DE supports many overlay windows to blend, and supports
video post-processing in the video channel.
The DE has the following features:


Supports output size up to 4096x2048.



Supports up to 7 alpha blending channels and 2 display out.



Supports four overlay layers in each channel, and has an independent scaler.



Supports potter-duff compatible blending operation.



VCH0 supports AFBD & TFBD, VCH1/UCH0~1 support TFBD, VCH2 support restricted 2K AFBD.
When VCH2 AFBD is on, all PQ modules in VCH2(SNR/FCM) and DEP1(GAMMA/DRC/DITHER)
except scaler are not available.



Supports input format semi-planar of YUV422/YUV420/YUV411/P010/P210 and planar of
YUV422/YUV420/ YUV411, ARGB8888/XRGB8888/RGB888/ARGB4444/ ARGB1555/RGB565.



Supports Frame Packing/Top-and-Bottom/Side-by-Side Full/Side-by-Side Half 3D format
data.



Supports 10-bit processing path for HDR video.



Supports SDR/HDR10/Hybrid-log gamma EOTF and color space conversion.



Supports AWonder1.1 for excellent display experience.
-

Adaptive de-noising for compression noise or mosquito noise for yuv420/422 input.

-

Adaptive edge-directive scaler.

-

Adaptive local dynamic contrast enhancement.

-

Adaptive detail/edge enhancement.

-

Adaptive color enhancement (Blue-stretch, Green-stretch and fresh tone correction) and
skin-tone protection.



-

17x17x17 programmable LUT for display0.

-

Adaptive de-banding for color banding removal.

-

Hue gain, Saturation gain, and Value gain controlled.

-

Fully programmable color matrix.

-

Dynamic gamma.

-

Color temperature tuning / Auto white balance

-

Global dimming (Up to 2560x2048 for display0, 2048x2048 for display1)

Supports write back for high efficient dual display and miracast.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

640

Confidential


Supports output format YUV444/YUV422/YUV420/RGB444 for 10/8bit.



Supports Register Configuration Queue for register update function.



Supports 1/2/4 ppc (pix per cycle) output.



Supports offline composition mode to increase bandwidth utilization.



Supports online rotation for AFBC1.3 YUV420 format, clockwise 0/90/180/270 degress
horizontal/vertical flip, up to 4K resolution.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

14.4

De-interlacer (DI)
The De-interlacer is a module which provides de-interlacing functions. It is an off-line processing
module which reading input frame buffer and writing output frame buffer by memory bus. In this
version of DI, it also provides Temporal Noise Reduction function to reduce the random noise.
And the new-add Film Mode Detection function can detect the pull-down content from video and
recover the film with maximum details. The DI has the following features:


Supports off-line processing mode only



Supports 8bit NV12/NV21/YV12 and planar YUV422/planar YUV422 UV-combined input data
format



Supports 8bit NV12/NV21/YV12 and planar YUV422/planar YUV422 UV-combined output data
format for DIT, and YV12/planar YUV422 output data format for TNR.



Supports video resolution from 32x32 to 2048x1280 pixel



Supports weave/pixel-motion-adaptive de-interlace method



Supports Field-Based Motion Detection with horizontal trailing width reduction



Supports Temporal Noise Reduction function



Supports Film Mode Detection with Video-On-Film Detection



Performance:
-

Module clock 500MHz for 1080P@60Hz YUV420, 550MHz for 1080P@60Hz YUV422 with
all functions enable

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential

Graphic 2D (G2D)
The Graphic 2D (G2D) engine is hardware accelerator for 2D graphic.
The G2D has the following features:


Supports mixer input layer size up to 7680x7680 pixels and output layer size up to 2048x2048



Supports rotate input/output layer size up to 4096x4096 pixels

Supports pre-multiply alpha image data



Supports color key



Supports two pipes Porter-Duff alpha blending



Supports multiple video formats 4:2:0, 4:2:2, 4:1:1 and multiple pixel formats (8/16/24/32 bits’
graphics layer)



Supports memory scan order option



Supports any format convert function above



Supports 1/16× to 32× resize ratio



Supports 32-phase 8-tap horizontal anti-alias filter and 32-phase 4-tap vertical anti-alias
filter.



Supports window clip



Supports FillRectangle, BitBlit, StretchBlit, and MaskBlit.



14.6

E-ink
The E-ink Engine(EE) is a hardware accelerator for E-ink LCD, It can rapidly update 64 Region LUT
Pipeline.
The E-ink has the following features:


Supports output size up to 2560x1650@106Hz.



Supports 8/16 bits data interface.



Supports 64 pipeline(4-bit) or 31 pipeline(5-bit) region update



Supports dither(support Floyd-Steinberg，Atkinson and Ordered dither)



Supports auto mode selection



Supports overlap and collision handling



Supports dual scan display

15 Video Output
15.1

TCON_LCD

15.1.1

Overview
The Timing Controller_LCD (TCON_LCD) is a module that processes video signals received from
system through a complicated arithmetic and then generates control signals and transmits them
to the LCD panel driver IC.
The TCON_LCD includes the following features:


15.1.2

Two TCON LCD controllers: TCON_LCD0 and TCON_LCD1
-

TCON_LCD0 supports 4K@45fps, and TCON_LCD1 supports 1080P@60fps

-

TCON_LCD0 controls one dual-link LVDS, one dual-link MIPI DSI, or one RGB interface

-

TCON_LCD1 controls one MIPI DSI interface



Supports RGB interface with DE/SYNC mode, up to 1920 x 1080@60fps



Supports serial RGB/dummy RGB interface, up to 800 x 480@60fps



Supports LVDS interface with dual link, up to 1920 x 1080@60fps



Supports LVDS interface with single link, up to 1366 x 768@60fps



Supports i8080 interface, up to 800 x 480@60fps



Supports BT.656 interface for NTSC and PAL



Dither function for RGB888, RGB666, and RGB565 with dither function

15.1.6.4

BT656 Interface
The BT656 transmission protocol is needed when outputting the data in YUV format in the HV
interface. Compared with the standard CSI interface, BT.656 has no SYNC signals like Field, VSYN,
and HSYN. Instead, it embeds the field synchronization information of image transmission in the
data stream transmitted by Date Bus. The Data Bus bit width of BT.656 is 8bit. And the
transmitting image data type is the interlaced YUV422. The encoding format for each row is as
follows:
Row=End of Active Video (EAV) + horizontal blanking data (80H/10H) + Start of Active Video (SAV)
+ valid data (UYVY)
Both of the embedded EAV and SAV are four bytes in the format of FF 00 00 XY. The first three
types are fixed to 8’hFF 8’h00 in hexadecimal. The last bytes XY are used as the control word.
The specific image row and field synchronization information is as follows.
Table 15-6 Analysis of XY Signal

Protection Bits.

The following figure shows the relationship between basic timing and CPU timing. WR is fixed to
1 when reading. And it is the reverse phase of dclk1 when writing, in which it is low active and
only has 1 period of low level. CS is active when pixel data is valid. RD is always set to 1 when
writing. And it is the reverse phase of dclk1 when writing, in which it is low active and only has 1
period of low level. 1 is set by “LCD_CPUI/F”. Set to 0 or 1 when reading, and set to 1 when
reading.

When CPU I/F is in the idle state, it can generate WR/RD timing by setting “LCD_CPUI/F”. The
CS strobe is one DCLK width, and the WR/RD strobe is half DCLK width.
There are two kinds of transmission modes for CPU interface: auto transmission and flush
transmission. In the auto transmission mode, the image data is transmitted in the active area,
whose transmission timing is controlled by HV timing; in the flush transmission mode, the image
data is transmitted only when LCD_FIFO is non empty without taking into consideration of HV
timing.

Step 1

Select HV interface type

Configure LCD_CTL_REG[LCD_IF] to 0 to select HV (Sync+DE) mode, and configure
LCD_HV_IF_REG [HV_MODE] to 0 to select 24bit/1cycle parallel mode.
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_ctl.lcd_if = HV(Sync+DE);
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_ctl.src_sel = src;

//src = DE/color/grayscale/...

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

659

Confidential
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_hv_ctl.
Step 2

hv_mode = 24bit/1cycle parallel mode;

Clock configuration
NOTE



In parallel RGB mode, the displayed pixel clock (pixel_CLK) is required to be consistent with
the DCLK, the pixel_clk (pixel_clk=Ht*Vt*frame rate) is decided by external LCD.



When using phase adjustment function, the LCD_IO_POL_REG.DCLK_SEL (reg0x88) selects
dclk0‒2 of different phase, and LCD_IO_POL_REG.IO2_INV can achieve 180°phase delay.

Configure corresponding frequency by setting PLL_VIDEO0/1 register, and configure TCON LCD0
Clock register.
Configure internal frequency division of TCON_LCD. Based on clock source of TCON and DCLK
clock ratio, configure LCD_DCLK_REG[LCD_DCLK_DIV]. If using phase adjustment function,
LCD_DCLK_REG[LCD_DCLK_EN] needs to be set, usually is 0xf. When the dclk1 and dclk2 in
LCD_DCLK_REG[LCD_DCLK_EN] are used, the value of LCD_DCLK_REG[LCD_DCLK_DIV] needs no
less than 6.
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_dclk. dclk_en = en;
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_dclk. dclk_div = div;
Step 3

Set sequence parameters

The sequence parameters include x, ht, hbp, hspw, y, vt, vbp, vspw, and correspond to
LCD_BASE_REG from reg0x48 to reg 0x54. Note that hbp includes hspw, and vbp includes vspw.
And LCD_BASIC2_REG.VT needs be set to the twice of the actual value.
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_basic0.x = x-1;
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_basic0.y = y-1;
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_basic1.ht = ht-1;
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_basic1.hbp = hbp-1;
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_basic2.vt = vt*2;
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_basic2.vbp = vbp-1;
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_basic3.hspw = hspw-1;
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_basic3.vspw = vspw-1;
Step 4

Enable IO output

Set the corresponding data IO enable and control signal IO enable of LCD_IO_TRI_REG (reg0x8C)
to 0 to start enable. Note that except the internal IO of TCON_LCD, the external GPIO mapping
needs to be set to LCD mode.
When some control signals require polarity reversal, it can realize by setting LCD_IO_POL_REG.
IO 0-3_INV.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

660

Confidential
Step 5

Set and open interrupt function

The LCD_GINT0_REG controls interrupt mode and flag, and the LCD_GINT1_REG sets the
interrupt line position of Line interrupt mode.
V interrupt:
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_gint0.vb_en = 1;
Line interrupt:
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_gint1.lcd_line_int_num = line;
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_gint0.line_en = 1;
Step 6

Turn on module enable

Enable LCD_CTL_REG[LCD_EN] and LCD_GCTL_REG[LCD_EN].
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_ctl.lcd_en = 1;
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_gctl.lcd_en = 1;
The following table is an example of typical parameter configuration.
Serial RGB
The serial RGB mode is consistent with parallel RGB mode, the main difference is the definition
of clock and the sequence of serial data. The difference is as follows.
Step 1

Select HV interface type

Set LCD_CTL_REG [LCD_IF] to 0 to select HV(Sync+DE) mode; set LCD_HV_IF_REG [HV_MODE] to
select 8bit/3cycle RGB serial mode (RGB888), 8bit/4cycle Dummy RGB mode (DRGB) or
8bit/4cycle RGB Dummy mode (RGBD).
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_ctl.lcd_if = HV(Sync+DE);
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_ctl.src_sel = src; //src = DE/color/grayscale/...
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_hv_ctl. hv_mode = Serial mode;
Step 2&3 Set clock and sequence parameters
In serial RGB mode, DCLK is the transfer clock of each byte data. In the same resolution, pixel_clk
of serial RGB is three times of its clock in parallel RGB, and ht, hbp, hspw own the same
conversion relation. When display is split into odd field and even field, LCD_BASIC2_REG [VT]
needs not to be set to the twice of the actual value.
lcd_dev[sel]->lcd_basic2.vt = vt;
Set LCD_HV_IF_REG[RGB888_ODD_ORDER/LCD_HV_IF_REG.RGB888_ODD_EVEN] to select RGB
output sequence of the selected odd and even lines.
lcd_dev[lcd_sel]->lcd_hv_ctl. srgb_seq_even = seq_even;
lcd_dev[lcd_sel]->lcd_hv_ctl. srgb_seq_odd = seq_odd;

TRI Mode

Step 1

Select i8080 interface type.

Step 2

The step is the same as HV interface, but pulse adjustment function is invalid.

Step 3

The step is the same as HV interface.

Step 4

The step is the same as HV interface.

Step 5

Select type and operating mode of i8080, the operating mode includes TRI mode and
AUTO mode, and the two operating modes are different in the following steps.

------------------------------------------------------- For TRI mode-----------------------------------------------------Step 6

Open TRI FIFO switch to enable TRI mode function.

Step 7

Set parameters of TRI mode, including block size, block space and block number.
NOTE



When output interface is parallel mode, the setting value of block space parameter is not
less than 20.



When output interface is 2 cycle serial mode, the setting value of block space parameter is
not less than 40.



When output interface is 3 cycle serial mode, the setting value of block space parameter is
not less than 60.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

666

Confidential


When output interface is 4 cycle serial mode, the setting value of block space parameter is
not less than 80.

Step 8

Set the tri interrupt or counter interrupt. When using the two interrupts, the tri start
operation need be operated (the bit1 of LCD_CPU_IF_REG is set to"1") mainly in the
interrupt service function. If using TE trigger interrupt, you can select the external input
pin as a trigger signal, and then set the 0x8C register (bit[24]) to "1" to open up input of
pad.

Step 9

Open the total switch of interrupt.

Step 10 Open the total enable of interrupt.
Step 11 Operate “tri start” operation (LCD_CPU_IF_REG (bit[1]) is set to "1").
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- For Auto mode---------------------------------------------------Step 6

Set and open V interrupt or Line interrupt. The step is the same as HV interface.

Step 7

Open module total enable.

15.2

TCON_TV

15.2.1

Overview
TCON_TV is a bridge module between DE and HDMI_TX/EDP_TX to generate video timing.
The TCON_TV includes the following features:


Two TCON_TV controllers: TCON_TV0 and TCON_TV1
-

TCON_TV0 controls HDMI interface

-

TCON_TV1 controls eDP interface



Supports configuring TCON_TV registers through AHB bus



Supports

outputting

the

video

timing

of

HDMI2.0b

and

the

video

format

of

4096×2160@60fps

15.2.2



Supports 1/2/4 pixel interface mode.



Supports 6/8/10 color depth.



Supports RGB444, YCbCr444, YCbCr422, and YCbCr420 input.



Supports generating interlaced-scanning odd and even field video timing, including VIC39.



Supports 3D framepacking active space insert.



Supports the colorbar testing of four kinds of patterns.



Supports outputting DDR dynamic frequency modulation indication.



Supports outputting the line-triggered and field-triggered maskable interrupts.



Supports outputting the configurable polarity of the signals of HSYNC, VSYNC, DE, and data.

Block Diagram
Figure 15-16 TCON_TV Block Diagram

Figure 15-17 TCON_TV Sub-blocks
Sub-blocks

Description
It is the testing module. When the colorbar is enabled, it will generate
the four testing patterns, including colorbar, lattice, grayscale, and

ColorBar

grid. It can be configured as the output mode of 1/2/4 pixels. During the
normal working, the colorbar should be disabled.
It is the interface processing module. According to the indication signal
generated by ctrl_gen and the filling state of TVFIFO, it interacts with

DE_INF

the previous stage DE and vdbist to obtain valid pixel data, so as to
complete the pixel sampling, and generate the write and clear control
of tvfifo.
It is the synchronized data caching module. It completes data writing

FIFO_wrapper

according to the write control signal generated by ed_inf, and generate
a filling status indication. Then, it completes data reading according to
the read control signal generated by the ctrl_gen module.
It is the timing generation module. It generates the video timing
according to the video format parameters configured by registers,

ctrl_gen

including non-interlaced, interlaced, 3D mode and VRR timing; besides,
it generates TVFIFO read control, and completes timing alignment. It
can be configured as 1/2/4 pixel output mode.
It is the output module of control and data signals. It completes the

ctrl_data_out

polarity adjustment based on the video timing signals generated by
ctrl_gen.

ctrl_reg

The application instructions of pixel modes

The multiple modes are designed for lowering the high refreshing rate and the pixel clock
frequency in the high resolution. For instance, in the 4 pixel mode, the video format of 8K@60fps
can be lowered from 2376MHz to 594MHz, which is more friendly to timing restriction and
backend implementation. In the other resolutions, it is recommended to use multiple modes as
needed to effectively lower the requirements on the pixel clock frequency.
b)

The application restrictions of pixel modes

The pixel modes of TCON_TV should be consistent with those of HDMI controller, eDP controller,
and DE.
c)

The configuration guidelines of pixel modes

The pixel modes are selected from 1/2/4 pixels in the TV_GCTL_REG.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential

beginning of every effective pixel data except for last group. The unstrict timing mode is mainly
for meeting the requirements of DSC and eDP, which is configured in the TV_GCTL_REG.

VDBIST
TCON_TV can generate the following pattern modes for the lane testing and debug of
TCON_TV->HMDI(EDP)->Screen.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

707

Confidential
Figure 15-23 RGB Colorbar Pattern

Theory: The display area is divided into 4 equal parts vertically, which are red, green, blue, and
gray color bars.
Take an example of 8bit.
Red color bars: R=0X00+i

G=0X00

B=0X00

Green color bars: R=0X00

G=0X00+i

B=0X00

Blue color bars: R=0X00

G=0X00

B=0X00+i

Grey color bars: R=0X00+i

G=0X00+i

B=0X00+i

NOTE
The value of i ranges from 0~255. Only R component is variable.

Figure 15-24 Grey Pattern

Theory: The display area is horizontally divided based on the gray scale. When the screen width
is less than that of gray scale, the gray scale of pixels in each line changes sequentially. When the
screen width is larger than that of gray scale, multiple pixels in each line will be in the same gray
scale.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

708

Confidential

NOTE
The black bar on the right side of the screen is also gradient, although it is not visible to the
naked eyes. Divide the display area into 4 equal parts vertically. The closer to the bottom of
screen, the thinner the grey density.

Take an example of 8bit, the horizontal gray scale is as follows.
R=0X00+i

G=0X00+i

B=0X00+I (The color component ranges from 0~255)

Figure 15-25 Dot Pattern

The pixels in each line alternate between white and black.
Take an example of 8bit.
Black: R=0X00

G=0X00

B=0X00

White: R=0XFF

G=0XFF

B=0XFF

Figure 15-26 Grid Pattern

Theory: The grid pattern consists of many 32x32 grids with white borders. In addition, the four
borders of display area are white, and the rest are black.
Take an example of 8bit.
Black: R=0X00

G=0X00

B=0X00

White: R=0XFF

G=0XFF

B=0XFF

15.2.6.4

3D Mode
TCON_TV supports inserting the active space in the frame_packing mode. In this mode, the
timing of 3D display is described as below. The left is progress scanning, and the right is
interlaced scanning.

15.2.7

Programming Guidelines

15.2.7.1

Pixel Clock Configuration
TCON_TV supports connecting to HDMI and eDP.
In the HDMI mode, the pixel clock of TCON_TV is that of CCU or HDMI PHY, which can be selected
by the hdmi_ck_phy_ccu_sel.
In the eDP mode, the pixel clock of TCON_TV is that of eDP PHY.

15.2.7.2

Module Configuration
Step 1

Select from 1/2/4 pixel modes in the TV_GCTL_REG[5:4].

Step 2

Configure color depth, video format, and even-odd field indication control in the
TV_PIXELDEPTH_MODE_REG.

Step 3

Configure the video parameters, and set the line and field as required by the screen
timing.

Step 4

Configure the DDR frequency modulation mode and frequency modulation line interval
in the TV_SAFE_PERIOD_REG0 and TV_SAFE_PERIOD_REG1. (Optional. Frequency
modulation is not permitted by default. Skip this step if no frequency modulation is
needed.)

Step 5

Set and enable the line/field interrupts in the TV_GINT0_REG and TV_GINT1_REG.
(Optional. Skip this step if no line/field interrupt needs to be enabled.)

Step 6

Decide whether to enable RGB output. (Optional. Skip this step if RGB output doesn’t
need to be enabled.)
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

710

Confidential

CAUTION
When RGB output is enabled, only 1 Pixel Mode can be selected in the step 1.

Step 7

Select the data source and testing pattern from the TV_SRC_CTL_REG [0] and
TV_SRC_CTL_REG [2:1].

Step 8

Set the Start_Delay in the TV_CTL_REG [19:4] to control the time of de-asserting the
sync signal to DE. Then enable the module in the TV_CTL_REG [31].

15.2.7.3

Line and Field Interrupt Configuration
TCON_TV provides a field interrupt. An interrupt will be generated after each field finishes
(namely, the Vacvitive finishes transmitting). It provides four configurable line interrupts, which
will be generated when the timing enters the triggering lines.
The line counting is shown as below. When the timing enters the VSA, the line counters starts
counting from 1.
