15.3

HDMI
The High Definition Multimedia Interface (HDMI) is a wired digital interconnect that replaces the
analog SCART connection. HDMI is capable of transferring uncompressed video, audio, and data
using a single cable.
HDMI system architecture consists of sources (transmitter) and sinks (receiver). The HDMI cable
and connectors carry four differential pairs that make up the TMDS data and clock channels.
These channels are used to carry video, audio, and auxiliary data. In addition, HDMI carries a
VESA Data Display Channel (DDC). The DDC is used for configuration and status exchange
between a single source and a single sink. The optional CEC protocol provides high-level control
functions between all of the various audiovisual products in a user’s environment.
The HDMI includes the follow features:


Supports HDMI1.4/HDMI2.0



Supports CEC, DDC, HPD



Supports HDCP1.4/HDCP2.2



Supports RGB888/YUV444/YUV422/YUV420 format and 8-/10-bit width



Supports

maximum

4K@60fps,

and

other

typical

video

format

like

4096x2160@60Hz/1920x1080@60Hz/1280x720@60Hz


Supports 8-channel I2S audio transmission, up to 192 KHz sampling rate



HDMI PHY on-chip reference clock frequency is 13.5-600M PCLK



HDMI PHY supports hot plug detection



HDMI PHY supports SCAN, I/O Continuity, BIST, and other test



Supports exclusive PAD like CEC and DDC and embedded with reference resistor

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

15.4

eDP1.4

15.4.1

Overview
The embedded Display Port (eDP) is a standard protocol in the digital display field. It is
completely compatible with DP and consists of main link, auxiliary channel, and hot plugging.
The eDP includes the following features:

15.4.2



A set of eDP1.4b/DP1.4 TX



Supports 1-lane, 2-lane, or 4-lane transmission, up to 5.4 Gbps/lane.



Video formats: RGB, YCbCr4:4:4, YCbCr4:2:2, and YCbCr4:2:0



Color depth: 6-bit, 8-bit, and 10-bit per channel



Supports I2S interface
-

Supports 2, 5.1, and 7.1 sound channel.

-

Maximum sampling rate: 192 kHz



Supports HDCP1.4 and HDCP2.3



Supports Hot Plug detection



The working frequency of AUX channel is 1MHz, and Manchester-II coding is used.



Supports the timing standards of VESA DMT and CVT.

Functional Descriptions
Pixel Mode
eDP can be configured as single/dual/quad pixel modes by altering clock parameters. For
example, to transmit 1920x1080@60Hz videos, the pixel clock is 148.5 MHz in the single pixel
mode, 74.25 MHz in the dual pixel mode, and 37.125 MHz in the quad pixel mode.

15.4.4.2

Audio Interface
For the input and output of audio information for secondary stream support, the DisplayPort
Transmitter core supports the I2S interface. The core implements between 1 and 4 instances of
the I2S interface. A single lane allows for the support of 2 channel data while 4 lanes are required
to support 7.1 channel audio data.

Programming Guidelines
Link Training
The host processor initiates link training commands by writing to the internal control register set.
When set into the link training mode, the functional data path is blocked and the link training
controller issues either training pattern 1 for clock recovery or training pattern 2, 3 or 4 for
symbol lock. Care must be taken to place the sink device in the proper link training mode using
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

735

Confidential
AUX transactions before the transmitter begins issuing the training pattern. Otherwise,
unpredictable results may occur. The link training process is summarized below. The DPTx core
ships with a complete link policy make implemented in C that may be used directly or as a
starting point for link training.
Figure 15-32 Link Training States

After the successful completion of the clock recovery and channel equalization phases of link
training, the transmitter may write one or more of the SOURCE_ENABLE bits to a 1 to begin link
symbol transmission. Training must be completed for each lane required to support a specific
receiver. For DisplayPort 1.2 and higher, training pattern 3 is available for sink devices that
indicate support for the advanced pattern. Similarly, training pattern 4 is available for
DisplayPort 1.3 and higher compliant sink devices.
15.4.5.2

Transmitter Clock Generation
The transmitter internal architecture supports the asynchronous and synchronous clocking
modes included in the DisplayPort Standard. The clocking mode is selected with bit 0 of the
SRCx_MAIN_STREAM_MISC0

register

in

the

Main

Stream

Attributes

block.

The

SRCx_MAIN_STREAM_MISC0 register should be set to a 0, and the asynchronous clock mode is
enabled. In the asynchronous clocking mode, the relationship between MVid and NVid is
calculated and not fixed. In this mode, the transmitter core will transmit the required constant
value for NVid (0x8000). The value of MVid will be calculated internally by the core using the input
video pixel clock and the link symbol clock as a reference. On a read of the MVid host register,
programmed value will be ignored and the computed MVid value will be returned.
15.4.5.3

Data Path Configuration
The DisplayPort Transmitter core must be properly configured through the host register set prior
to enabling the transmission of any main link video stream.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential

The main stream attribute registers are directly mapped to the equivalent fields of the MSA
secondary data packet. The DisplayPort specification contains complete information regarding
the proper use of these fields.
The base transaction unit size is contained in the TRANSFER_UNIT_CONFIG_SRC_x register lower
two bytes, bits 15:0. This value may be any multiple of two in the range supported by the
DisplayPort standard which is 32 and 64. Odd values written to this register field will be rounded
down to the next lowest even number.
For the number of valid data symbols carried within each Transaction Unit (TU), the transmitter
core supports two modes of operation, automatic and manual. The automatic mode is enabled
by setting the SYMBOLS_PER_TU_SRC_x field, bits 22:16, to a value of 0x00. In this mode, the
transmitter core will automatically populate the video data symbols of the TU with the available
data from the user input port. This mode provides ease of programming for most embedded
applications but may not be compatible with all sink devices. For applications requiring box to
box connections with a wide range of sink devices, the manual mode is recommended.
In the manual mode of determining the TU size, a calculation is performed using the equations in
section 2.2.1.4 of the DisplayPort standard. The calculated value is programmed into the
SYMBOLS_PER_TU_SRC_x field and limits the transmitter core to a maximum number of video
data symbols per TU less than or equal to this value. The manual mode provides a consistent
and predictable number of valid data bytes per transaction unit as required by some sink
devices.
LinkBW = LINK_BW_SET * 27 * LANE_COUNT_SET
Data Rate = (Input Clock Rate * bits per pixel) / 8
Data Per TU = Data Rate / LinkBW * TU_SIZE
The core also requires a second calculation that determines the number of video data symbols
per line of active video. This value is determined using the following equation and programmed
into the USER_DATA_COUNT register.
The core also requires a second calculation that determines the number of video data symbols
per line of active video. This value is determined using the following equation and programmed
into the
USER_DATA_COUNT register.
SYMBOL_COUNT = ((HRES * bits per pixel) + 7) / 8
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

737

Confidential
USER_DATA_COUNT = (SYMBOL_COUNT + lane_count – 1) / lane_count
The bits per pixel are the total number of bits used to represent a single pixel. For example, a
10-bit per color RGB source would require 30 bits to represent a single pixel. The lane_count is
the currently configured number of lanes.
The final register that requires programming is the USER_SYNC_POLARITY. These four, single bit
fields determine the polarity of the user data input control signals VSync, HSync, Data Enable
and OddEven. A value of 1 for any of these bits indicates that the related input control signal is
active high. Please note that this polarity is the opposite of the polarities specified in the
DisplayPort Main Stream attribute packet.
Once the above register and register fields have been properly set, the main link may be enabled
through the SOURCE_ENABLE and VIDEO_STREAM_ENABLE host registers. Output from the
DisplayPort Transmitter link will be enabled at the first user input vertical sync after the host
register has been programmed. Partial frames will not be sent over the link when the main link is
either enabled or disabled. To ensure full compatibility for box-to-box DisplayPort connections,
special attention must be given to the configuration of the SYMBOLS_PER_TU_SRC_X register.
Embedded DisplayPort connections may be able to ignore this requirement based on the
characteristics of the target panel by enabling the sparse mode described in the Embedded
DisplayPort section of this document. The DisplayPort standard requires that the Blanking Start
symbol occurs during the same symbol time for each active line and at the same symbol time
during vertical blanking.
15.4.5.4

TU Data Accumulation Delay
In addition to the active data per transaction unit, the DATA_ACCUMULATION_DELAY field of the
USER_DATA_CONTROL register must be properly set to allow for the internal rate control logic to
provide a guaranteed number of active data symbols in each transaction unit. This delay also
provides a fixed reference for the internal framing logic to properly place the BE symbol on the
link. The value of this register should be set to a depth of at least one half of the TU size. For
example, a TU size of 64 would require this field to be set to a minimum value of 32. The
DATA_ACCUMULATION_DELAY register controls the number of link clock cycles that the TU
packetization logic waits between the first valid pixel data received and the start of the first
active packet.
Figure 15-33 Data Accumulation Delay

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

738

Confidential
This delay allows for a fixed timing reference from the first active pixel to allow the first
Transaction Unit of each line to be placed in the proper position on the link. A failure to set this
register properly could result in an inconsistent time interval between Blanking Start symbols.
Larger values may be used for this register with a maximum equal to the programmed TU size.
Settings that are greater than one half of the TU size will result in an increased latency in the data
processing pipeline.
15.4.5.5

TU FIFO Accumulation Delay
The internal data pipeline also provides the ability to allow for an accumulation of data in the
internal FIFO to prevent any possible data underrun in the TU data stream. The
FIFO_ACCUMULATION_DELAY field of the USER_DATA_CONTROL register allows the host to set
the minimum FIFO depth before active data begins being transmitted for a specific line. While a
wide range of values are acceptable for this register, there are specific guidelines that have been
validated with a wide range of the video modes and color modes.
The transaction unit utilization is based on the percentage of active symbols that are present in
each TU.
Figure 15-34 FIFO Accumulation Delay Settings
TU Utilization

FIFO_ACCUMULATION_DELAY

< 7%

8

26% - 74%

7

8% - 25%

6

75% - 92%

5

93%-100%

4

The FIFO has a maximum depth of thirty-two (32) entries. These recommendations are based on
a classification of the link utilization for active data. If a large value is used for this register, the
previous line may not complete transmission before the next active video line begins.
15.4.5.6

Host Interrupts
The DisplayPort Transmitter core generates an interrupt to the host processor under one or
more possible conditions. When any one of these conditions is detected, the core will set the
apb_int signal high. All interrupts are cleared when a read is performed from the
INTERRUPT_STATUS register.
Figure 15-35 Interrupt Detection Logic

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

739

Confidential
15.4.5.7

General-purpose Timer
The DisplayPort Transmitter core design includes a single general purpose 20-bit timer for use by
the host processor system. Each timer has a resolution of one microsecond and can provide a
timing reference between 1 microsecond and 1 second. The timer may be configured to
automatically reload the count value and may also generate an interrupt. The general purpose
timer is located in the GP_HOST_TIMER register and contains four fields that are used to control
the operation of the timer.

15.4.5.8

Hot Plug Detection
The transmitter core continuously monitors the value of the hot plug detect (HD) input signal for
an interrupt event or a disconnect event. For a detected active low pulse width between 500
microseconds and 1 millisecond, the sink device has requested an interrupt. The interrupt is
passed to the host processer through the APB interface when the interrupt source is not masked.
When the HPD signal remains low for greater than 2 milliseconds, this indicates that the sink
device has been disconnected and the link should be shut down. This condition is also passed
through the APB interface as an interrupt when not masked. The host processor must properly
determine the cause of the interrupt by reading the appropriate DPCD and/or host registers and
take the appropriate action.

15.5

MIPI DSI

15.5.1

Overview
The Display Serial Interface is a high-speed interface between a host processor and peripheral
devices that adhere to MIPI Alliance specifications for mobile device interfaces. This DSI module
is composed of a DSI controller which is compliance with MIPI DSI specification V1.02 and a
D-PHY module which is compliance with MIPI DPHY specification V1.0.
The MIPI DSI includes the following features:
DSI Host Features


Compliance with MIPI DSI v1.02



Supports up to 4 lanes



Without DSC, single-link DSI supports up to 1920*1200@60fps



Dual-link DSI supports 2.5K@60fps and 4K@45fps



Only DSI0 supports DSC function, supporting up to 2000x1200@120fps



Supports non-burst mode with sync pulse/sync event, burst mode



Supports pixel format: RGB888, RGB666, RGB666 loosely packed and RGB565



Supports continuous lane clock mode and non-continuous lane clock mode



Compliance with MIPI DCS v1.01, bidirectional communication in LP through data lane 0



Supports bidirectional communication of all generic commands in LP through data lane 0



Supports Low Power Data Transmission



Supports ULPS and Escape modes



Hardware Checksum capabilities

D-PHY Features


Compliance with D-PHY V1.2



Supports up to 4 lanes



Aggregate throughput up to 6 Gbps with 4 data lanes



Bidirectional communication in Low Power mode through data lane 0



Supports Low Power Escape modes and Ultra Low Power state



Supports multiplex with GPIO, GPIO can work in 3.3V or 1.8V power supply



1.8V±5% analog supply operation

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

15.5.6

Programming Guidelines
NOTE
Frequent PLL enable/disable is not recommended, as the PLL enable/disable will arise the
mutual interference of PLLs and system instability.

15.5.6.1

15.5.6.2

15.5.6.3

Enable PLL
Step 1

Write 1 to the PLL_EN, EN_LVS, and, LDO_EN of the DPHY_PLL_REG0.

Step 2

Set LOCK_ENABLE as 1 in the DPHY_PLL_REG1.

Step 3

Wait the lock status to change to 1. Perform the adjudgement for three times.

Step 4

Wait 20 us latency.

Step 5

Configure the M0/M1, M2/M3, P, N factors in the DPHY_PLL_REG0.

Step 6

Write 1 to the PLL_UPDATE of the DPHY_PLL_REG0.

Step 7

Wait the PLL_UPDATE of the DPHY_PLL_REG0 to be cleared.

Step 8

Wait the lock status to change to 1. Perform the adjudgement for three times.

Step 9

Wait 20 us latency, and then the PLL is available.

Disable PLL
Step 1

Set LOCK_ENABLE as 0 in the DPHY_PLL_REG1.

Step 2

Write 0 to the PLL_PLL_EN and PLL_LDO_EN of the DPHY_PLL_REG0.

PLL Pre-Divider Frequency Modulation
The PLL linear frequency modulation supports smooth transition to target N value at a certain
modulation rate value without re-locking. However, only the linear frequency modulation of N
value is supported. When the pre-divider factor alters, PLL should be re-locked.
When not enabling linear frequency modulation, or when the pre-divider should be adjusted in
the condition that liner frequency modulation is enabled. Follow the steps below to perform PLL
pre-divider frequency modulation.
Step 1

Set the LOCK_ENABLE in the DPHY_PLL_REG1 as 0.

Step 2

Set the LOCK_ENABLE in the DPHY_PLL_REG1 as 1.

Step 3

Configure N, M1, M0, and P in the DPHY_PLL_REG0.

Step 4

Set the PLL_UPDATE in the DPHY_PLL_REG0 as 1.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

791

Confidential

15.5.6.4

Step 5

Set the PLL_UPDATE in the DPHY_PLL_REG0 as 1.

Step 6

Wait the lock status to change to 1. Perform the adjudgement for three times.

Step 7

Wait 20 us latency.

PLL Linear Frequency Modulation
The linear PLL frequency modulation mode is designed to address the re-locking issue
encountered when switching N values in integer frequency duplication. In this mode, the N value
can be directly configured, and the PLL will smoothly converge the N value to the target
frequency point based on the configured frequency slope.
When configuring linear frequency modulation, static parameters in the fractional divider need
to be set, while the control parameters are automatically managed by the linear frequency
modulation.
Step 1

Set PLL_EN in the DPHY_PLL_REG0 as 1, and wait DISPLL lock state is stable.

Step 2

Set Spread Frequency Mode in the DPHY_PLL_PAT0_CTL_REG as 10 or 11. Set
PLL_PI_EN as 1 and SDM Smooth Enable as 0 in the DPHY_PLL_PAT1_CTL_REG.

Step 3

Set PLL_LFM_STEP in the DPHY_PLL_LFM_REG. STEP is 12 bit. The formula is as below:
FREQ = FCLK*FCLK*STEP/2^17

In the above formula. FREQ is the target modulation rate at the unit of MHz/us. The FCLK is
reference clock frequency at the unit of MHz. Thus, the step can be gotten by the formula as
below:
STEP = FREQ*2^17/FCLK/FCLK
Step 4

Set the PLL_LFM_EN in the DPHY_PLL_LFM_REG as 1.

Step 5

Set the Reg_update in the DPHY_PLL_REG0 as 1.

Step 6

Wait the Reg_update in the DPHY_PLL_REG0 to be 0.

Step 7

Set the FB_DIV in the DPHY_PLL_REG0 and then write 1 to the PLL_UPDATE.

Step 8

Wait the Reg_update to be 0, indicating the linear frequency modulation completes.

Step 9

To re-configure N value, go back to the step 7.

Step 10 To disable linear frequency modulation, set PLL_LFM_EN in the DPHY_PLL_LFM_REG as
0, and set Reg_update in the DPHY_PLL_REG0 as 1.
15.5.6.5

PLL Spreading/Fractional Division
The fractional division is to add a fractional value to the divider N of a PLL to achieve a more
precise frequency configuration. By applying fractional division, the multiplication factor N of the
PLL can be expressed as N.x, where N represents the added fractional value.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

792

Confidential
The PLL spreading is to add a triangular wave to the N value of a PLL to let the final output
frequency exhibit a triangular wave variation. Spreading parameters consist of spread amplitude
and spread spectrum period. The spread amplitude refers to the range of variation in the output
frequency; while the spread spectrum period is the duration of one cycle of the triangular wave
modulation, whose reciprocal is spread spectrum frequency.
PLL spreading/fractional division is configured through DPHY_PLL_PAT0_CTL_REG and
DPHY_PLL_PAT1_CTL_REG; therefore, the generic/linear PLL spreading/fractional division
procedures are the same. All the parameters in the two types of registers are divided into static
parameters and control parameters.
Static parameters are used to adjust the order and phase interpolation of the fractional division
loop and don’t support dynamic switching. To alter parameters, disable PLL spreading/fractional
division, configure static parameters, and then enable PLL spreading/fractional division. The
parameters are shown as below.


SPR_FREQ_MODE: SDM mode switching.



PLL_PI_EN: It is used to decide whether to enable phase interpolation (PI) mode.



PLL_PI_CFG: PI circuit current control.



SMOOTH_EN: It is used to enable frequency modulation smooth.



DITHER_EN: It is used to enable dither. When dither is enabled, a pseudo-random sequence
will be added to the frequency modulation curve.

Control parameters are used to control frequency modulation curve and support dynamic
switching. It should be reminded that if the SMOOTH_EN is set, control parameters only can be
switched in the condition that SDM_BUSY is set to 0. The control parameters are shown as
below.


WAVE_STEP: Spreading step. The formula is shown as below.
WAVE_STEP = 2^17*(x2-x1)*2/(Fclk/FREQ)
x2 is the upper limit; x2 is the lower limit; Fclk is the PLL reference clock frequency; FREQ is
the spreading slope. PLL multiplication factors range from N.x1 to N.x2.



WAVE_BOT: Spreading starting point. The formula is shown as below.
for upward frequency spreading, SDM_BOT = x1*2^17
for downward frequency spreading, SDM_BOT = x2*2^17



FREQ: Spreading slope. To dynamically switch this parameter, switch WAVE_STEP at the
same time.



SDM_DIRECTION: Spreading direction, including upward frequency spreading and
downward frequency spreading. During upward frequency spreading, the curve starts from
x1 and then adjusts to x2 before reversing; during downward frequency spreading, the curve
starts from x2 and then adjusts to x1 before reversing. To dynamically switch this parameter,
switch WAVE_BOT at the same time.



FRAC_EN: Fractional division enable.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

793

Confidential


FRAC_IN: Fractional division frequency point. The formula is shown as below.
FRAC_IN = x*2^17

The master switch of PLL spreading/fractional division is SIG_DELT_PAT_EN. It should be
enabled before PLL spreading/fractional division usage.
PLL spreading/fractional division configuration is shown as below.
SIG_DELT_PAT_EN

FRAC_EN

WAVE_STEP

FRAN_IN

MODE

1

0

/

1

0

The PLL spreading/fractional division procedure is as follows.
Step 1

Enable PLL by referring to section Enable PLL.

Step 2

Configure static parameters as follows.

Step 3



SPR_FREQ_MODE: It is recommended to be 2 or 3.



PLL_PI_EN: It is recommended to be 1.



PLL_PI_CFG: It is recommended to use default value.



SMOOTH_EN: It is recommended to be 1.



DITHER: It is recommended to be 0.

Configure WAVE_STEP, WAVE_BOT, FREQ, SDM_DIRECTION, FRAC_IN, and FRAC_EN
according to formulas described in this section.

Step 4

Configure SIG_DELT_PAT_EN and other parameters to enable PLL spreading/fractional
division.

Step 5

To adjust static parameters, configure SIG_DELT_PAT_EN as 0. When SDM_BUSY is 0, go
back to Step 1

Step 6

To adjust control parameters after PLL spreading/fractional division is enabled,
configure WAVE_STEP, WAVE_BOT, FREQ, SDM_DIRECTION, and FRAC_IN.

Step 7

To disable PLL spreading, set SIG_DELT_PAT_EN as 0. To enable it again, judge that
SDM_BUSY is 0.

16 Video Input
16.1

CSIC

16.1.1

Overview
The CMOS Sensor Interface Controller (CSIC) is an image or video data receiver, which can
receive image or video data via camera interface. The controller can transfer valid data to
embedded ISP or store the data in memory directly.
The CSIC includes the following features:
MIPI CSI


Supports 4+4+2-lane MIPI interface
-

MIPI PHY A 4 data lane

-

MIPI PHY B 4 data lane

-

MIPI PHY C 2 data lane



Conforms to MIPI CSI2 V1.1 and MIPI DPHY V1.2. Supports 2.0 Gbit/s per lane



Supports Crop Function



Supports Frame Rate Down



Supports 8M@60fps, size 3264(H) x 2448(V)



Supports max resolution 3264(H) x 4224(V) (ISP on-line), 5664(H) x 4248(V) (ISP off-line)



Supports Sensor Fsync

Parallel CSI


8/10/12/16-bit width



Supports DC, BT.656, BT.601, BT.1120 protocol



DDR sample mode with pixel clock up to 148.5MHz



BT1120 4CH up to 1080P@30fps



BT656 4CH up to 4-ch 720P@30fps

BK


BK0/1 supports up to 20M@30fps or 24M@25fps; BK2/3 supports up to 2.5K@60fps; BK4/5
supports up to 1080P@30fps



BK supports independent frame-done interrupts. Up to 4 groups, with arbitrary allocation
among groups.



BK0/1/2/3 supports 4-lane time-division multiplexing.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

833

Confidential


Supports 6 DMA for 6 video stream storage



Supports converting interlaced input into progressive output. No anti-aliasing, noise
reduction functions.

16.1.2



Supports conversion for YUV422 to YUV420, YUV422 to YUV400, YUV420 to YUV400



Supports horizontal and vertical flip for YUV422/YUV420/RAW format

Note: P0-P3 is used for verification in Channel 1 and channel ID marking in Channel 2/4.
Except for 16-bit data width, BT1120 is same to BT656, including EAV and SAV encoding. On the
16-bit data bus of BT1120, the low 8 bits are for transmitting UV components and the high 8 bits
are for transmitting Y components, or the low 8 bits are for transmitting Y components and the
high 8 bits are for transmitting UV components. In addition, EAV and SAV encoding still use low 8
bits. BT1120 also supports 2-/4-channel time-division multiplexing for image data transmission.
BT601 supports transmitting interlaced YUV422 data with 8-bit signal lines. The information
synchronization such as field, vsyn, hsyn is completed with independent signal lines. Different
from the standard CSI, its field signals can be embedded in the vsyn signals in the v2f_mode or
vsyn signals can be embedded in the field signals in the f2v_mode. Both field and vsyn can exist
in the vf_mode.
In the v2f_mode, field signals are obtained from vsyn and hsyn signals. If the vsyn goes down at
the falling edge of hsyn, field 0 is obtained; if the vsyn goes down at the rising edge of hsyn, field
1 is obtained.

Offset Definition
Offset in horizontal and vertical can be added when receiving image. Unit is pixel.

16.1.5.5



For YUV422 format, pixel unit is a YU/YV combination.



For YUV420 format, pixel unit is a YU/YV combination in YC line, and only a Y in Y line.



For Bayer and RAW format, pixel unit is a R/G/B single component.
Flip Definition

Both horizontal and vertical flip are supported at the same time. This function is implemented in
the process of each FIFO writing data to memory, only flipping the data of separate FIFO, not
changing component to FIFO distribution.
If horizontal flip is enabled, one or more pixels will be taken as a unit:

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

839

Confidential
For YUV format, a unit of Y0U0Y1V1 will parser and flip the Y component in one channel, and UV
will be treated as a whole. In planar output mode, U and V will be flipped separately. In UV
combined output mode, UV will be flipped as a whole. So, a sequence of Y1U0Y0V1 will be.
For Bayer_raw format, situation is much like. A GR/BG sequence will be changed to BG/RG. A unit
of square has four pixels.

16.1.6

Programming Guidelines

16.1.6.1

Async Bridge Configuration


If the working clock frequency of ISP is lower than that of parser and post.

Step 1

Configure the field ISP_BRIDGE_EN (bit [3]) of CSIC_TOP_EN_REG as 1 to enable async
bridge.

Step 2

Configure the field MCSI_PARSER_CLK_MODE (bit [0]) of CCU_CLK_MODE_REG as 1 to
make CSI parser work in CSI clock.

Step 3

Configure the field MCSI_POST_CLK_MODE (bit [1]) of CCU_CLK_MODE_REG as 1 to
make CSI post work in CSI clock.



If the working clock frequency of ISP is same as that of parser and post.

Step 1

Configure the field ISP_BRIDGE_EN (bit [3]) of CSIC_TOP_EN_REG as 1’b0 to disable
and bypass async bridge.

Step 2

Configure the field MCSI_PARSER_CLK_MODE (bit [0]) of CCU_CLK_MODE_REG as 0 to
make CSI parser work in ISP core clock.

Step 3

Configure the field MCSI_POST_CLK_MODE (bit [1]) of CCU_CLK_MODE_REG as 0 to
make CSI post work in ISP core clock.

16.1.6.2

CSI and SDRAM Dynamic Frequency Modulation
Step 1

After the CSIC reset is de-asserted, configure the FACTOR_N and FACTOR_M in the
CSIC_CCU_CHFREQ_CLK_CTRL_REG to set the working clock of chfreq. It is 1 MHz by
default.

Step 2

Set CHFREQ_CLK_GATING(bit[0]) as 1 in the CSIC_CCU_CHFREQ_CLK_CTRL_REG to
enable chfreq_clk.

Step 3

Configure

CHFREQ_PAR2ISP_SEL(bit[31:16])

in

the

CSIC_CHFREQ_CFG0_REG

as

required by the application.
Step 4

Set CHFREQ_RST[bit0] as 1 in the CSIC_CHFREQ_CFG0_REG to de-assert the dynamic
frequency module.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

840

Confidential
Step 5

Execute the steps providing that CSI must join dynamic frequency modulation. Set the
CHFREQ_ALLOW[bit1] as 1 in the CSIC_CHFREQ_CFG0_REG. Then, enable the
corresponding ISPs, VIPPs, and BKs. Prolong the period of DDR dynamic frequency
modulation, and then configure the procedure of sensor sending data.

Step 6

Execute the steps providing that the data stream output by the current sensor modes is
judged to determine that CSI join dynamic frequency modulation. Set the
CHFREQ_RDY_MASK[bit3] as 1 in the CSIC_CHFREQ_CFG0_REG. Prolong the period of
DDR dynamic frequency modulation, enable the corresponding ISPs, VIPPs, and then
configure sensor the procedure of sensor sending data. Repeatedly read back
CHFREQ_FRM_DONE_TIME

and

CSIC_CHFREQ_OBS_REG

(bit[31:16]),

and

CHFREQ_VBLANK_LENGTH (bit[15:0]) in the CSIC_CHFREQ_OBS_REG to observe their
values and stability. Afterwards, determine whether to set CHFREQ_ALLOW (bit[1]) as 1
after considering the period of the DDR dynamic frequency modulation. Then, set
CHFREQ_RDY_MASK (bit[3]) as 0 in the CSIC_CHFREQ_CFG0_REG and set the
CHFREQ_ALLOW (bit[1]) as 0 or 1 as required.
16.1.6.3

CSI Clock Frequency Configuration
The minimum clock configuration requirements for CSI_CLK are as follows:
One-pixel mode: CSI_CLK = lanespeed/8
Two-pixel mode: CSI_CLK = lanespeed/8/2
Unit: lanespeed – Gbit/s or Mbit/s; CSI_CLK — GHz or MHz
NOTE
Only 4-lane CSI supports two-pixel mode.

16.1.6.4

Interrupt Coalescing and Timestamp Configuration
Step 1

After the CSIC reset is de-asserted, configure the FACTOR_N and FACTOR_M in the
CSIC_CCU_CHFREQ_CLK_CTRL_REG to set the working clock of chfreq. It is 1 MHz by
default.

Step 2

Set

BK_INTPOOL_CLK_GATING

(bit[0])

as

1

in

the

CSIC_CCU_BK_INTPOOL_CLK_CTRL_REG to enable the chfreq_clk.
Step 3

Configure INT_SRC_SEL (bit[1]) of CSIC_BK_INTPOOLx_CFG0_REG to select the source
of BK interrupt coalescing. If it is 1 (default configuration), select the VS_INT of BK as the
source of BK interrupts; if it is 0, select the FD_INT of BK as the source of BK interrupts.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

841

Confidential
Step 4

Configure

CSIC_BK_INTPOOLx_CFG0_REG

(bit[31:16])

and

CSIC_BK_INTPOOLx_CFG1_REG (bit[31:0]) to select the channel source of coalesced
interrupts. All the BK channels doesn’t coalesce by default. If some channel wants to
join interrupt coalescing, set the corresponding SRC_MSK_BK*_CH* as 0.
Step 5

Configure TRIG_MOD (bit[2]) in the CSIC_BK_INTPOOLx_CFG0_REG to select trigger
mode. If it is set as 0 (default configuration), the fifo_level trigger mode will be selected.
In the mode, fifo level needs to be set. When the number of BK interrupts in the INT FIFO
is more than the set value, interrupts will be triggered. After receiving interrupts, the
software will get data in the INT fifo. For the following steps, refer to Step 6. If it is set as
1, the target trigger mode will be selected. In the mode, target BK ID and target channel
number need to be set. When one interrupt is stored in INT FIFO, whose BK ID is equal to
target BK ID and the channel number is equal to the target channel number, an
interrupt will be triggered. After receiving interrupts, the software will get data in the INT
FIFO. For the following steps, refer to Step 7.

Step 6

Configure FIFO_AVL_INT_EN (bit[0]) in the CSIC_BK_INTPOOLx_INT_EN0_REG to enable
FIFO_AVL interrupts. Configure TRIG_LEVEL (bit[9:4]) ranging from 1 to 63 in the
CSIC_BK_INTPOOLx_CFG0_REG. Then, configure BK_INT_POOL_EN (bit[0]) as 1 in the
CSIC_BK_INTPOOLx_CFG0_REG to dis-assert the reset of BK INT POOL circuit.
Afterwards, when the total interrupt number in the INT FIFO is larger than or equal to
the set TRIG_LEVEL, report the FIFO_AVL interrupts. If they are received by software,
read the CSIC_BK_INT_FIFO_REG for the times of TRIG_LEVEL to obtain the BK
interrupts. Then, it is recommended to read again the FIFO_LEVEL (bit[6:0]) in the
CSIC_BK_INTPOOL_OBS0_REG to query how many BK interrupts are stored in INT FIFO
by hardware in the course of reading CSIC_BK_INT_FIFO_REG. Then, fetch the latest
stored interrupts by reading CSIC_BK_INT_FIFO_REG until the FIFO_LEVEL (bit[6:0]) in
the CSIC_BK_INTPOOL_OBS0_RE is 0. Then, read the ACCESS_DELAY (bit[15:0]) in the
CSIC_BK_INTPOOL_OBS1_REG. Finally, write 1 to FIFO_AVL_INT_PD (bit[0]) in the
CSIC_BK_INTPOOL_INT_STA0_REG to clear the pending interrupts. The format of 32-bit
data

fetched

from

CSIC_BK_INT_FIFO_REG

is

{4’h0,Time

Stamp

Delta

(20

bit),2’h0,Channel Number(2 bit),BK ID(4 bit)}. Among them, Time Stamp Delta indicates
the time intervals between the currently read interrupt and last read interrupt; Channel
Number indicates the channel number of current read interrupt source; BK ID indicates
the BK ID of current read interrupt source.
Step 7

Configure FIFO_AVL_INT_EN (bit[0]) in the CSIC_BK_INTPOOLx_INT_EN0_REG to enable
FIFO_AVL interrupts. Configure TRIG_ID (bit[13:10]) from 0 to 11 and TRIG_CH (bit[15:14])
from 0 to 3 in the CSIC_BK_INTPOOLx_CFG0_REG. Set BK_INT_POOL_EN (bit[0]) in the
CSIC_BK_INTPOOL_CFG0_REG to de-assert the reset of BK INT POOL circuit. Afterwards,
when the BK ID is equal to TRIG ID among interrupts stored in the INT FIFO, and channel
number is equal to the interrupts of TRIG_CH, report FIFO_AVL interrupts. If they are
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

842

Confidential
received by software, read the CSIC_BK_INT_FIFO_REG until the interrupts that BK ID is
equal to TRIG_ID and channel number is equal to TRIG_CH. Then, it is recommended to
read again the TRIG_TGT_LEVEL (bit[22:16]) in the CSIC_BK_INTPOOLx_OBS0_REG to
query how many BK interrupts are stored in INT FIFO by hardware in the course of
reading CSIC_BK_INT_FIFO_REG. Then, fetch the latest stored interrupts by reading
CSIC_BK_INT_FIFO_REG

until

the

TRIG_TGT_LEVEL

(bit[22:16])

in

the

CSIC_BK_INTPOOL_OBS0_RE is 0. Then, read the ACCESS_DELAY bit[15:0] in the
CSIC_BK_INTPOOL_OBS1_REG. Finally, write 1 to FIFO_AVL_INT_PD (bit[0]) in the
CSIC_BK_INTPOOL_INT_STA0_REG to clear the pending interrupts.
16.1.6.5

Timestamp Restoration Calculation
For instance, if the TRIG_MOD is set as 0 and FIFO_level is set as 3, the fifo_avl interrupts will be
reported when more than 3 BK interrupts are stored in the INT FIFO. Assuming that four
interrupts are read by software after reception.
Interrupts

Channel Number

measured by
software

1

0

The 3rd interrupt

2

1

1

1000 us

st

nd

When the 4th interrupt is read, record the current system time by software, and then read the
ACCESS_DELAY bit[15:0] in the CSIC_BK_INTPOOL_OBS1_REG. Assuming that the value of
ACCESS_DELAY is 200 us, it indicates that the time interval of the 4th interrupt from being written
into INT FITO to being read out is 200 us. Therefore,
The 4th interrupt time is 1000 us – 200 us =800 us
The 3rd interrupt time is 800 us – 50 us = 750 us
The 2nd interrupt time is 750 us – 34 us = 716 us
The 1st interrupt time is 716 us – 6 us = 710 us
You can restore the time stamp successively in the above way.
16.1.6.6

Exception Handling
There are two exception interrupts in the hardware, which are FIFO_FULL_INT in the
CSIC_BK_INTPOOL_INT_STA0_REG

and

BK*_CH*_INT_LOST

in

the

CSIC_BK_INTPOOL_INT_STA0/1_REG.
The FIFO_FULL_INT will be reported in case that the INT FIFO is full. Then, back pressure on the
previous stage circuit will occur. Therefore, the interrupts already stored in the INT FIFO will not
be overridden by the new interrupts. Once FIFO FULL interrupts are triggered, they should be
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

843

Confidential
handled immediately by repeatedly reading CSIC_BK_INT_FIFO_REG and FIFO_LEVEL bit[6:0] in
the CSIC_BK_INTPOOL_OBS0_REG to read out the interrupts in the INT FIFO until it is empty. You
can restore the time stamp of interrupts when the FIFO is full by reading FULL_ ACCESS_DELAY
(bit[31:16]) and taking into consideration of the time of reading the last interrupt recorded by the
software.
BK*_CH*_INT_LOST interrupts will be reported when the interrupts of BK and Channel are lost. If
the previous interrupt of BK channel is yet to be written into INT FIFO, and a new interrupt is
triggered, interrupt lost will occur. This kind of exception needs to be handled immediately, too.
The above exception interrupts can be enabled in the CSIC_BK_INTPOOL_INT_EN0_REG and
CSIC_BK_INTPOOL_INT_EN1_REG.
16.1.6.7

BK Image Cache Address Self-refreshing Mode
The steps to configure the BK image buffer address self-refresh mode are as follows:
Step 8

Write 1 to the BUF_ADDR_MODE of the CSIC_DMA_CH3_EN_REG register.

Step 9

Configure the CPU to write plural sets of buffer addresses into the buffer address FIFO.

Step 10 Configure

the

CSIC_DMA_BUF_ADDR_FIFO_THRESHOLD

bit

and

the

CSIC_DMA_STORED_FRM_THRESHOLD bit of the CSIC_DMA_CHx_BUF_TH_REG (x = 0 to
3).
Each time when a new frame of image is input, the hardware will check whether the number of
remaining addresses in the buffer FIFO is equal to or less than the threshold set by the
CSIC_DMA_BUF_ADDR_FIFO_THRESHOLD bit. If so, an interrupt will be asserted to remind the
software to configure a new address; if the hardware checks that the FIFO of the current buffer
address is empty, the input data of the current frame will be automatically ignored and a frame
loss interrupt will be generated.
Each time when a new frame of image buffering ends, check whether the number of cached
images has reached the threshold set by the CSIC_DMA_STORED_FRM_THRESHOLD bit. If so, an
interrupt that replaces the frm_done interrupt in the register mode will be generated to remind
the software to fetch the cached image data and clear the cached frame counting value.
Notice that every output format (1 FIFO, 2 FIFO, and 3 FIFO) needs to be configured with Y, U, and
V addresses in the course of image cache address FIFO configuration. The addresses that will not
be used can be configured as 0. In addition, when the cap_done interrupt is asserted after
capture,

you

need

to

check

the

CSIC_DMA_STORED_FRM_CNT

of

the

CSIC_DMA_CHx_STORED_FRM_CNT_REG (x = 0 to 3) register to confirm whether there is any
cached frame that is yet to reach the threshold set by the CSIC_DMA_STORED_FRM_THRESHOLD
bit.

other: Start
Software write this bit to “1” to start pattern
generating from DRAM. When finished, the hardware
will clear this bit to “0” automatically. Generating
cycles depends on PTN_CYCLE.

17 Audio
17.1

I2S/PCM

17.1.1

Overview
The I2S/PCM controller is designed to transfer streaming audio data between the system
memory and the codec chip. The controller supports standard I2S format, Left-justified mode
format, Right-justified mode format, PCM mode format, and TDM mode format.
The I2S/PCM controller includes the following features:




5x I2S/PCM (I2S0-4)
-

4-lane I2S0 is used for digital amplifier.

-

2-lane I2S1 is used for Bluetooth audio call.

-

4-lane I2S2 is used for digital amplifier and supports ASRC.

-

4-lane I2S3 is used for HDMI or eDP.

-

2-lane I2S4 is used for Bluetooth audio call or multiplexed to eDP.

Compliant with standard Philips Inter-IC sound (I2S) bus specification
-

Left-justified, Right-justified, PCM mode, and Time Division Multiplexing (TDM) format

-

Programmable PCM frame width: 1 BCLK width (short frame) and 2 BCLKs width (long
frame)





FIFOs for transmitting and receiving data
-

Programmable FIFO thresholds

-

128 depth x 32-bit width TXFIFO and 64 depth x 32-bit width RXFIFO

Supports multiple function clocks
-

Clock up to 24.576 MHz Data Output of I2S/PCM in Master mode (Only if the IO PAD and
Peripheral I2S/PCM satisfy Timing Parameters)

-

Clock up to 12.288 MHz Data Input of I2S/PCM in Master mode (Only if the IO PAD and
Peripheral I2S/PCM satisfy Timing Parameters)



Supports TX/RX DMA slave interface



Supports multiple application scenarios
-

Up to 16 channels (fs = 48 kHz) which has adjustable width from 8-bit to 32-bit

-

Sample rate from 8 kHz to 384 kHz (sample rate*channels*slot width≤24.567 MHz)

-

8-bit u-law and 8-bit A-law companded sample

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1083

Confidential


Supports master/slave mode

BCLK are input pins.

Asynchronous Sample Rate Converter
The Asynchronous Sample Rate Converter (ASRC) module supports sampling rate conversion
between the up-sampling and down-sampling. The ASRC also supports sampling rate conversion
between dual-channel audio data, and the size of the sampling data is up to 24 bits.
The ASRC module has the following features:


Typical THD + N: -130 dB (Range: -125 dB to -139 dB)



Supports sampling rate conversion between the up-sampling and down-sampling to
implement the sampling rate conversion for stereo data
-

The up-sampling ratio ranges from 1 to 7.5x

-

The down-sampling ratio ranges from 8 to 1x



Supports sampling rate conversion between two identical frequencies



Sampling rate for both the input and output range is from 8 kHz to 192 kHz and can be
decimal
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1087

Confidential


Sampling rate can be configured manually or via adaptive generation



The ASRC input is connected to I2S RX_FIFO_WDATA [31:8], and the input data is 24-bit MSB
big-endian. For the input data that is less than 24 bits, use zeros to pad out the values at the
low bits instead of high bits



The ASRC needs some time to calculate the result. The output outsample a/b will keep 0
during the calculation, and then change to the valid value when the result comes out

Calculating the ASRC Latency
Calculate the ASRC up-sampling and down-sampling latency according to the following
formulas.

Upsampling Latency  Phase Delay  FIFO Delay  32  16  48 Input Sample Periods

Downsampli
ng Latency PhaseDelay FIFODelay (32* fsout/fsin) 16 InputSample Periods

17.1.6.1

Programming Guidelines
System Setup and I2S/PCM Initialization
The first step in the system setup is properly programming the GPIO because the I2S/PCM port is
a multiplex pin. For functions of the multiplex pins, refer to the section GPIO.
For the system setup, perform the following steps to set clock source.
Step 1

Disable the PLL_AUDIO through PLL_AUDIOx Control Register[PLL_ENABLE] in the CCU.

Step 2

Set up the frequency of the PLL_AUDIO in the PLL_AUDIOx Control Register.

Step 3

Enable the I2S/PCM gating through the I2S/PCMx_CLK_REG when you check out that the
PLL_AUDIOx Control Register[LOCK] becomes to 1.

Step 4

Reset and enable the I2S/PCM bus gating by setting I2S_BGR_REG.

After the system setup, the register of I2S/PCM can be setup.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1089

Confidential
Step 5

Initialize the I2S/PCM. You should close the Globe Enable bit (I2S/PCM_CTL[0]),
Transmitter Block Enable bit (I2S/PCM_CTL[2]), and Receiver Block Enable bit
(I2S/PCM_CTL[1]) by writing 0.

Step 6

Clear the TX/RX FIFO by writing 0 to the bit[25:24] of I2S/PCM_FCTL.

Step 7

Clear the TX FIFO and RX FIFO counter by writing 0 to I2S/PCM_TXCNT and
I2S/PCM_RXCNT.

17.1.6.2

Channel Setup and DMA Setup
Step 1

Set up the I2S/PCM of master and slave. The configuration can be referred to the
protocol of I2S/PCM.

Step 2

Set up the translation mode, the sample resolution, the wide of the slot, the channel
slot number, and the trigger level, and so on. The setup of the register can be found in
the specification.

Step 3

The I2S/PCM supports two methods to transfer the data. The most common way is DMA,
the setup of DMA can be found in the section DMA. In this module, you just enable the
DRQ.

17.1.6.3

17.1.6.4

Enable and Disable I2S/PCM
Step 1

Enable TX/RX by writing I2S/PCM_CTL[TXEN]/I2S/PCM_CTL[RXEN].

Step 2

Enable I2S/PCM by writing 1 to I2S/PCM_CTL[Globe Enable].

Step 3

Write 0 to the Globe Enable bit to disable I2S/PCM.

Process ASRC Input and Output Data
The following example shows a typical application of ASRC: the input data is 24-bit valid, and the
output data is a 32-bit data whose highest 24 bits are valid output and the lowest eight bits are
padded out with zeros.
To implement the application, configure the sample resolution and slot width as 32 bits. Follow
the steps below:
Step 1

For the input register: 0x04 [6:4] sample_res = 3`h7, 0x04 [2:0] slot_width = 3`h7. The
format of the input data: 32’hXXXXXXXX, where, bit [31] is the MSB and X is the valid
data bit.

Step 2

For the output register: 0x04 [6:4] sample_res = 3`h7, 0x04 [2:0] slot_width = 3`h7. The
format of the output data: 32’hXXXXXX00, where, bit [31] is the MSB, X is the valid data
bit, and bit [7:0] are the padded zeros.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1090

Confidential
17.1.6.5

Convert the Sampling Rate with ASRC
Converting a 48 kHz sampling rate to 16 kHz is the most common scenario in actual applications.
Follow the steps below to convert the sampling rate from 48 kHz to 16 kHz for the 32-bit data.
Step 1

Configure the PLL_AUDIO Register
a)

Configure PLL_AUDIO_CTRL_REG[31:0] as 0x8814AB01. That is, PLL_AUDIO =
24*(171+1)/(1+1)/(1+0)/(1+20) = 98.286 MHz. According to the relationship among
the Fsin, Fsout, and MCLK, the MCLK should be greater than 60 MHz. In the
simulation phase, the SYS_CLK24M frequency is 24 MHz, so the output frequency of
PLL_AUDIO should be 25*(171+1)/(1+1)/(1+0)/(1+20) = 102.381 MHz. In the IC test
phase, configure the frequency of PLL_AUDIO according to its actual output
frequency.

b)

It is suggested that you configure the ASRC MCLK as an equal-duty-cycle signal. You
can specify an odd number for bit[21:16] (PLL_POST_DIV_P) of
PLL_AUDIO_CTRL_REG to get an equal-duty-cycle output clock of PLL_AUDIO.

c)
Step 2

Configure bit[25:24] of I2S3_ASRC_CLK_REG as 0x00 to select the PLL_AUDIO(4X).

Configure the I2S Registers
a)

Configure bit[7:4] (BCLKDIV) of I2S/PCM_CLKD as 4`h9, that is, the frequency of
BCLK will be 98.286 MHz/32 = 3.072 MHz.

b)

Configure bit[17:8] (LRCK_PERIOD) of I2S/PCM_FMT0 as 10`h1F. That is, the
LRCK_PERIOD width is configured as 32 BLCKs and can generate the ASRC CLKIN
with a 48 kHz sampling rate. (

c)

3.072MHz
= 48 kHz )
32* 2

Configure bit[6:4] (Sample Resolution bits) of I2S/PCM_FMT0 as 3`h7 to specify the
sample resolution as 32-bit.

d)

Configure bit[2:0] (Slot Width bits) of I2S/PCM_FMT0 as 3`h7 to specify the slot
width as 32-bit.

Step 3

Configure the ASRC Registers
a)

Configure bit[16] (clock gate) of MCLKCFG as 1`h1 to open the clock gating.

b)

Configure bit[3:0] (division factor) of MCLKCFG as 1`h1 to specify the division factor
as 1.

c)

Configure bit[20] (clock gate ) of FsoutCFG as 1`h1 to open the clock gating.

d)

Configure bit[19:16] (clock select) of FsoutCFG as 4`h0 to select I2S0_ASRC_CLK as
the clock source.

e)

Configure bit[7:4] (the first division factor) of FsoutCFG as 16`h13 to configure the
first division factor as 128.

f)

Configure bit[3:0] (the second division factor) of FsoutCFG as 16`h10 to configure
the second division factor as 48.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1091

Confidential
g)

Configure the ASRC ratio.

To configure the ASRC ratio manually, configure bit[31] (Manual Configuration of ASRC
Ratio Enable) of ASRCMANCFG as 1`h1 to enable the manual configuration of ASRC ratio.
Configure bit[25:0] of ASRCMANCFG as 26`h155555 to specify the ratio value as
0x155555. The calculation formula for the ratio value: Dec2Hex (Fsout/Fsin) *222). In this
example, Fsout/Fsin = 16 kHz/48 kHz =1/3, then the ratio is 0x155555.
To configure the ASRC ratio automatically, configure bit[31] (Manual Configuration of
ASRC Ratio Enable) of ASRCMANCFG as 1`h0 to enable the automatic configuration of
ASRC ratio. Then the system will automatically calculate the ratio value based on the
MCLK, Fsout, and Fsin.

17.2

DMIC

17.2.1

Overview
The Digital MIC controller supports one 8-channel digital microphone interface and can output
128 fs or 64 fs (fs = ADC sample rate).
The DMIC controller includes the following features:

17.2.2



Supports up to 8 channels



Sample rate from 8 kHz to 48 kHz

Block Diagram
The following figure shows a block diagram of the DMIC.
Figure 17-10 DMIC Block Diagram

gating information, refer to the section CCU.

Programming Guidelines
The software operation of the DMIC is divided into five steps: system setup, DMIC initialization,
channel setup, DMA setup, and Enable/Disable module.
The following figure shows the flow chart of the whole operation, the system setup, and the DMIC
initialization.
Figure 17-11 DMIC Operation Mode
DMIC
System Setup

System Setup

Pin Multiplex

DMIC Initial

Globe Disable

DMIC Initial
PLL_AUDIO Frequence and Enable
Channel Setup
DMA Setup
Enable/Disable Module

17.2.5.1

Fluse RXFIFO
CLK Reset and Gating

Bus Reset and Gating

Clear DATA/RXFIFO Counter

System Setup and DMIC Initialization
The first step in the system setup is properly programming the GPIO because the DMIC port is a
multiplex pin. For functions of the multiplex pins, refer to the section GPIO.
For the system setup, perform the following steps to set clock source.
Step 1

Disable the PLL_AUDIO through PLL_AUDIOx Control Register[PLL_ENABLE].

Step 2

Set up the frequency of the PLL_AUDIO in PLL_AUDIOx Control Register. Then enable
PLL_AUDIO.

Step 3

Enable the DMIC gating through DMIC_CLK_REG when you check out that the LOCK bit
of PLL_AUDIOx Control Register becomes 1.

Step 4

Reset and enable the DMIC bus gating by DMIC_BGR_REG.

After the system setup, the register of DMIC can be setup.
Step 5

Initialize the DMIC. You should close the globe enable bit (DMIC_EN[8]), data channel
enable bit (DMIC_EN[7:0]) by writing 0 to it.

Step 6

Flush the RXFIFO by writing 1 to DMIC_RXFIFO_CTR[31].

Step 7

Clear the Data/RXFIFO counter by writing 1 to DMIC_RXFIFO_STA, DMIC_CNT.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1136

Confidential
17.2.5.2

Channel Setup and DMA Setup
You can set up the sample rate, the sample resolution, the over-sample rate, the channel number,
the RXFIFO output mode, the RXFIFO trigger level, and so on. The setup of the register can be
found in the specification.
The DMIC supports two methods to transfer the data. The most common way is DMA; the setup
of DMA can be found in section DMAC. In this module, you just enable the DRQ.

17.2.5.3

17.2.6

Enable and Disable DMIC
Step 1

Enable the data channel enable bit (DMIC_EN[7:0]) by writing 1 to it.

Step 2

Enable DMIC by writing 1 to the Globe Enable bit (DMIC_EN[8]).

Step 3

Write 0 to DMIC_EN[8] to disable DMIC.

17.3

One Wire Audio (OWA)

17.3.1

Overview
The One Wire Audio (OWA) provides a serial bus interface for audio data. This interface is widely
used for consumer audio connection.
The OWA includes the following features:


One OWA TX and One OWA RX



Compliance with S/PDIF interface



Compatible with standard IEC-60958 and IEC-61937



IEC-60958 supports data formats: 16 bits, 20 bits, and 24 bits



TXFIFO and RXFIFO
-

One 128×24bits TXFIFO and one 64×24bits RXFIFO for audio data transfer

-

Programmable FIFO thresholds



Supports TX/RX DMA slave interface



Multiple function clock
-

Separate clock for OWA TX and OWA RX

-

OWA TX function clock includes a series of 24.576MHz/49.152MHz and 22.579MHz
frequency (TX function clock 49.152MHz support ample rate 384KHz)

-

OWA RX function clock includes a series of 400MHz frequency (RX function clock 400MHz
support CDR of sample rate from 8KHz to 384KHz)



Supports hardware parity on TX/RX
-

Hardware parity generation on the transmitter

-

Hardware parity checking on the receiver



Supports channel status capture on the receiver



Supports channel sample rate capture on the receiver



Supports insertion detection for the receiver



Supports channel status insertion for the transmitter

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential

17.3.5

Functional Description

17.3.5.1

Biphase-Mark Code (BMC)
In the OWA format, the digital signal is coded using the biphase-mark code (BMC). The clock,
frame, and data are embedded in only one signal—the data pin. In the BMC system, each data bit
is encoded into two logical states (00, 01, 10, or 11) at the pin. The following figure and table
show how data is encoded to the BMC format.
The frequency of the clock is twice the data bit rate, as shown in the following figure. Also, the
clock is always programmed to 128 x fs, where fs is the sample rate. The device receiving in the
OWA format can recover the clock and frame information from the BMC signal.
Figure 17-13 OWA Biphase-Mark Code

IEC60958 Transmit Format
The OWA supports digital audio data transfer and receive. It also supports full-duplex
synchronous work mode. The software can set the work mode by the OWA Control Register.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1152

Confidential
Every audio sample transmitted in a sub-frame consists of 32-bit, numbered from 0 to 31. The
following figure shows a sub-frame.
Figure 17-14 OWA Sub-Frame Format
0

Bits 0-3 carry one of the four permitted preambles to signify the type of audio sample in the
current sub-frame. The preamble is not encoded in BMC format, and therefore the preamble
code can contain more than two consecutive 0 or 1 logical states in a row.
Bits 4-27 carry the audio sample word in linear 2s-complement representation. The
most-significant bit (MSB) is carried by bit 27. When a 24-bit coding range is used, the
least-significant bit (LSB) is in bit 4. When a 20-bit coding range is used, bit [8:27] carry the audio
sample word with the LSB in bit 8. Bit [4:7] may be used for other applications and are
designated auxiliary sample bits.
If the source provides fewer bits than the interface allows (either 20 or 24), the unused LSBs are
set to logical 0. For a nonlinear PCM audio application or a data application, the main data field
may carry any other information.
Bit 28 carries the validity bit (V) associated with the main data field in the sub-frame.
Bit 29 carries the user data channel (U) associated with the main data field in the sub-frame.
Bit 30 carries the channel status information (C) associated with the main data field in the
sub-frame. The channel status indicates if the data in the sub-frame is a digital audio or some
other type of data.
Bit 31 carries a parity bit (P) such that bit 4-31 carry an even number of 1s and an even number of
0s (even parity). As shown in the following table, the preambles (bit 0-3) are also defined with
even parity.

17.3.5.3

IEC61937 Transmit Format
IEC 61937 applies to the digital audio interface by using the IEC 60958 series for the conveying of
non-linear PCM encoded audio bitstreams. The non-linear PCM encoded audio bitstream is
transferred by using the basic 16-bit data area of the IEC 60958 subframes, i.e. in time-slots 12 to
27. Because the non-linear PCM encoded audio bitstream to be transported is at a lower data
rate than that supported by the IEC 60958 interface, the audio bitstream is broken into a
sequence of discrete data-bursts, and stuffing between the data-bursts is necessary.
IEC 60958 Data Burst
The method of placing the data into the IEC 60958 bitstream is to format the data to be
transmitted into data-bursts and to send each data-burst in a continuous sequence of IEC 60958
frames.
Table 17-7 Bit Allocation of Data-Burst in IEC 60958 Subframes

Data Burst Format
Each data-burst contains a burst-preamble consisting of four 16-bit words (Pa, Pb, Pc and Pd)
followed by the burst-payload which contains data of an encoded audio frame.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1154

Confidential
Figure 17-16 Data-Burst Format



Burst-preamble

The burst-preamble consists of four mandatory fields. Pa and Pb represent a synchronization
word. Pc gives information about the type of data, and some information/control for the receiver.
Pd gives the length of the burst-payload, and is limited to 65535 bits in the case of Pd represent
bits’ length, or is limited to 65535 bytes in the case of Pd represent bytes’ length.
Figure 17-17 Data-burst Preamble

The four preamble words are contained in two sequential IEC 60958 frames. The frame beginning
the data-burst contains preamble word Pa in subframe 1, and Pb in subframe 2. The next frame
contains Pc in subframe 1 and Pd in subframe 2. When placed into an IEC 60958 subframe, the
MSB of a 16-bit burst-preamble word is placed into time-slot 27 and the LSB is placed into
time-slot 12.
Figure 17-18 Data-burst Preamble words



Burst-information

The 16-bit burst-information contains information about the data which will be found in the
data-burst.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1155

Confidential
Figure 17-19 Fields of Burst-information

The 7-bit data-type is defined in bits 0-6 of the burst-preamble Pc, the bit 6 is the MSB. This
data-type field indicates the format of the burst-payload, which will be conveyed in the
data-burst. Typical properties of a data-type are the reference point and repetition period of the
burst, which is the number of sampling periods of the audio between the reference point of the
current data-burst and the reference point of the next data-burst. The reference point is
inherently defined for each data-type.
The error-flag bit is available to indicate if the contents of the data-burst contain data errors. If a
data-burst is thought to be error-free, or if the data source does not know if the data contains
errors, then the value of this bit is set to a ‘0’. If the data source does know that a particular
data-burst contains some errors this bit may be set to a ’1’. The usage of this bit by receiver is
optional.
The meaning of the 5-bit data-type-dependent info depends on the value of the data-type.
The 3-bit bitstream-number indicates to which bitstream the data-burst belongs. Eight codes
(0-7) are available so that up to eight independent bitstreams may be multiplexed in one
bitstream in a time multiplex. Each independent bitstream shall use a unique bit-stream
number.


Length-code

The length-code indicates the number of bits or bytes according to data-type within the data
burst, from 0 to 65535. The size of the Pa, Pb, Pc and Pd is not counted in the value of the
length-code. In other words, the length-code indicates the number of bits of the burst-payload in
bits, plus the conditional length of Pe and Pf, or the number of bytes of the burst-payload in
bytes, plus the conditional length of Pe and Pf if exists.
Figure 17-20 Length of the Burst-Payload Specified by Pd

17.3.5.4

Audio Sample Ratio Detection
The sampling rate is calculated according to the data pulse back-stepping method. In the first
phase lock of the CDR, find the period of 1 Frame. Then count by using the high-speed sampling
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1156

Confidential
clock and read the counting value of the pulse width of Period Max, then the sampling rate can
be calculated.

Programming Guidelines
The software operation of the OWA is divided into five steps: system setup, OWA initialization,
channel setup, DMA setup and enable/disable module. The following sections describe these five
steps.
Figure 17-21 OWA Operation Flow
OWA

System Setup

System Setup

Pin Multiplex

OWA Initial

Globe/TX/RX Disable

OWA Initial
PLL_AUDIO Frequence and Enable
Chanel Setup

DMA Setup

Enable/Disable Module

17.3.6.1

Clear TXFIFO/RXFIFO
CLK Reset and Gating

Bus Reset and Gating

Clear TXFIFO/RXFIFO Counter

System Setup and OWA Initialization
The first step in the OWA initialization is properly programming the GPIO because the OWA port
is a multiplex pin. For functions of the multiplex pins, refer to the section GPIO.
For the system setup, perform the following steps to set clock source.
Step 1

Disable the PLL_AUDIO through PLL_AUDIOx Control Register[PLL_ENABLE].

Step 2

Set up the frequency of the PLL_AUDIO in PLL_AUDIOx Control Register. Then enable
PLL_AUDIO.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1157

Confidential
Step 3

Enable the OWA gating through OWA_TX_CLK_REG and OWA_RX_CLK_REG when you
check out that the LOCK bit of PLL_AUDIOx Control Register becomes 1.

Step 4

Reset and enable the OWA bus gating by OWA_BGR_REG.

After the system setup, the register of OWA can be set up.
Step 1

Reset the OWA by writing 1 to OWA_GENCTL[0] and clear the TX/RX FIFO by writing 1 to
OWA_FCTL[17:16].

Step 2

Enable the globe enable bit by writing 1 to OWA_GENCTL[1].

Step 3

Clear

the

interrupt

and

TX/RX

counter

by

setting

OWA_ISTA

and

OWA_TX_CNT/OWA_RX_CNT.
17.3.6.2

Parameter Setup and DMA Setup
You can set up the audio type, clock divider ratio, the sample format, and the trigger level, and so
on. The setup of the register can be found in the specification.
The OWA supports two methods to transfer the data. The most common way is DMA; the
configuration of DMA can be found in section DMAC. In this module, you just enable the DRQ in
OWA_INT[7].

17.3.6.3

17.3.7

Enable and Disable OWA
Step 1

Enable TX/RX by writing OWA_TX_CFIG[31]/OWA_RX_CFIG[0].

Step 2

Enable OWA by writing 1 to OWA_GENCTL[1].

Step 3

Write 0 to OWA_GENCTL[1] to disable OWA.

18 Peripherals
18.1

GMAC

18.1.1

Overview
The Gigabit Medium Access Controller (GMAC) enables a host to transmit and receive data over
Ethernet in compliance with the IEEE 802.3-2015 standard.
The GMAC has the following features:


Supports 10/100/1000Mbps data transfer rates



Supports RMII/RGMII PHY interface



AMBA4 AXI master interface with 64bit data transfer



Supports both full-duplex and half-duplex operation



Full-duplex flow control



IEEE 1588-2008 for precision networked clock synchronization. Supports Ethernet packet
timestamping as described in IEEE 1588-2002 and IEEE 1588-2008



Programmable frame length to support Standard or Jumbo Ethernet frames with sizes up to
16 KB



Source Address field and VLAN insertion or replacement, Double VLAN



Supports transmitting TCP/IP Checksum Offload



Supports a variety of flexible address filtering modes, including Hash filter function



Optimization for packet-oriented DMA transfers with frame delimiters



Supports linked-list descriptor list structure



Descriptor architecture, allowing large blocks of data transfer with minimum CPU
intervention: each descriptor can transfer up to 32 KB of data



Comprehensive status reporting for normal operation and transfers with errors



Supports 4KB TXFIFO for transmission packets and 8KB RXFIFO for reception packets



Supports 16Descriptors Descriptor Pre-fetch cache for TXDMA and RX DMA



Programmable interrupt options for different operational conditions



Supports MDIO Interface for PHY device configuration and management



Configurable big-endian and little-endian mode for Transmit and Receive paths



Supports statistics on the received and transmitted packets



Supports Split Header

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1182

Confidential


Supports Power Management Module (PMT) with remote wake-up packet and magic packet
processing options



The DMA controller interfaces with the application through the

AHB Slave Interface
PHY interface

The 32-bit AHB slave interface provides access to the DMA, MTL, and
MAC CSR space.
The PHY interface can be configured to RGMII and RMII.
A DMA Channel has independent Transmit (TX) and Receive (RX)
engines, and a CSR space. The TX engine transfers data from the

DMA

system memory to the device port (MTL), whereas the RX engine
transfers data from the device port to the system memory. The DMA
engine uses descriptors to efficiently move data from source to
destination with minimal application CPU intervention.

18.2

SerDes Subsystem

18.2.1

Overview
The SERDES is responsible for the data input/output through the high-speed interfaces. It
integrates a PCIe3.0 DM controller, a USB3.1 GEN2 DRD controller, COMB0/1_PHY_SERDES, a
AUX_HPD_PHY designed for DP, and a USB2.0 PHY.
The SERDES have the following features.
COMB0_PHY_ SERDES


Supports PIPE interface mode
-



USB3.1 SS and SS+, up to 10 Gbps

Supports Raw SerDes (or PMA direct connect) interface mode
-

DisplayPort Tx (RBR, HBR, HBR2)

-

embedded DisplayPort Tx (UI_Rate_1-UI_Rate_8), up to 5.4 Gbps



Supports up to 4 lanes



Supports single protocol and independent multi links



-

Up to 2 USB3.1 Links

-

Up to 2 DP/eDP TX Links

USB2.0 PHY


Universal Serial Bus 2.0 physical layer connects a USB OTG controller to a USB system.



The USB2.0 femtoPHY supports the USB2.0 480-Mbps protocol and data rate, and is
backward compatible with the USB 1.1 1.5-Mbps and 12-Mbps protocol and data rates.





On-chip PLL provides various clocks for USB operation, deriving from one input reference
clock.

Suspend, Resume, and Remote Wakeup mode support.

1206

Confidential
Offset: 0x2000
Bit

Read/Write

Register Name: COMB1_PHY_PINS_LINK_CTRL0
Default/Hex

Description
COMB1_PHY_LINK_CFG_LN
PHY link/lane configuration. Used to map lanes to
links.
0: designates a lane as a link slave.
1: designates a lane as a link master.
Lanes are grouped into links from lowest lane
number to highest. Adjacent slave lanes are part of
multilane link down to the lowest numbered
adjacent master lane.
Lane 0 is always a master and thus does not
require its own phy_link_cfg input.
For example, for a 4 lane PHY can be configured as
follows:
{phy_link_cfg_ln_3, phy_link_cfg_ln_2,
phy_link_cfg_ln_1}
111: 4x1 configuration (i.e. 4 independent links)
000: 1x4 configuration (i.e. single 4 lane link with
lane 0 as the master lane)

6:4

R/W

0x0

010: 2x2 configuration (i.e. 2 2-lane links with lane
0 and lane 2 as the master lanes)
011: 2x1+1x2 configuration (i.e. 2 single lane links
plus 1 2-lane link with lanes 0, 1 and 2 as the
master lanes)
101: 2x1+1x2 configuration (with lane 0, 1 and 3 as
master lanes)
110: 2x1+1x2 configuration (with lane 0, 2 and 3 as
master lanes)
100: 1x3+1x1 configuration (i.e. 1 3-lane link plus 1
single lane link with lane 0 and 3 as master lanes)
001: 1x3+1x1 configuration (with lane 0 and 1
master lanes)
Note: phy_reset_n and apb_preset_n must be
asserted to modify this signal.
The master lane of each link is that link’s lane 0. It
shall not be disabled unless all other lane’s in the
link are disabled.
When each phy_link_cfg_ln_* = 0, the PHY is in a
single-link configuration.

3:1

/

/

/

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

18.3

PCIe3.0 DM

18.3.1

Overview
The PCI Express (PCIe) Controller is a general purpose I/O interconnect, which provides low pin
count, high reliability, and high-speed data transfer at rates of up to 8.0 Gbps per lane per
direction. There is 1 PCI Express controller in SoC, referred as PCIe.
The PCIe controller includes the following features:


All non-optional features of the PCI Express Base Specification, Revision 3.0, Version 1.0



Supports Gen1 (2.5Gbps), Gen2 (5Gbps), Gen3 (8Gbps) speed



Device Type: Supports DM



Link Width: 1 lane



2 Virtual Channels (VCs)



Multiple Functions: Supports 4 Functions for PCIe in EP Mode



Configurable Max_Payload_Size, up to 512 bytes



Embedded DMA with Hardware Flow Control. Supports 4 Write/Read Channels



Internal Address Translation Unit. Supports 16 Inbound Address Translation regions and 16
Outbound Address Translation regions



MSI with Per-Vector Masking (PVM), Extended message data for MSI



The following optional features of the specification:
-

ID-Based Ordering (IDO) by your application

-

L1 Substates (L1SS)

-

Resizable BAR (RBAR) with Expanded RBAR and VF Resizable BAR support

-

Readiness Notifications (RN)

-

PCI Express Active State Power Management (ASPM)

-

PCI Express Advanced Error Reporting (AER)

-

Vital Product Data (VPD)

-

Access Control Services (ACS)

-

Dynamic Power Allocation (DPA)

-

Function Level Reset(FLR)

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

18.3.5

Functional Description

18.3.5.1

PCIe Memory Mapping
The address space of PCIe controller can be partitioned into three spaces.


Core Configuration Space (CCS): The configuration register space of the PCIe controller itself.
It is also the standard configuration register space defined by the PCIe Specification.



User Defined Space (UDS): The user-defined register space for the PCIe controller itself.



Slave Command Space (SCS): Address space for configuration transaction and memory
transaction. The read and write operations of this space will be transformed by the PCIe
controller into configuration read and write transactions or memory read and write
transactions in PCIe domain. The PCIe command space segmentation is 0x200000000x2FFFFFFF and 0x440000000-0x53FFFFFFF.

18.3.5.2

ATU Operation
ATU is an address translation unit in PCIe controller and is used for transaction transformation
and address translation. There are two types of ATU: Outbound ATU and Inbound ATU.
Outbound ATU
Outbound ATU is used to transform the read/write operation in CPU domain of the original
address space into the read/write transaction in PCIe domain of the target address space. If the
Outbound ATU is not used, the PCIe controller will not perform address translation against the
read/write operation in the CPU domain; instead, the read/write transaction initiated in the CPU
domain will be transformed into the read/write operation at the same address in the PCIe
domain. If the Outbound ATU is used, the read/write transaction initiated in the CPU domain will
be transformed into that at the different address in the PCIe domain.
The following takes the region N as an example:


When Outbound ATU is not used, read/write operation initiated at the address Region N of
CPU domain will be directly transformed into the read/write transaction at the address
Region N of PCIe domain.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1222

Confidential


When Outbound ATU is used, set address transaction as “transform the Region N of CPU
domain into the Region K of PCIe domain. The read/write operation initiated at the address
Region N of CPU domain will be transformed into the read/write transaction at the address
Region K of PCIe domain.

Inbound ATU
Inbound ATU is used to transform the read/write transaction in the PCIe domain of the original
address space into the read/write operation in the CPU domain of the target address space. If the
Inbound ATU is not used, the PCIe controller will not perform address translation; instead, the
read/write transaction initiated in the PCIe domain will be transformed into the read/write
operation at the same address in the CPU domain. If the Inbound ATU is used, the read/write
transaction initiated in the PCIe domain will be transformed into that at the different address in
the CPU domain.
The following takes the region N as an example:


When Inbound ATU is not used, read/write transaction initiated at the address Region N of
PCIe domain will be directly transformed into the read/write operation at the address
Region N of CPU domain.



When Inbound ATU is used, set address transaction as “transform the Region N of PCIe
domain into the Region K of CPU domain. The read/write operation initiated at the address
Region N of PCIe domain will be transformed into the read/write transaction at the address
Region K of CPU domain.

18.3.5.3

4G

DMA Operation
There is a private DMA with read channels and write channels in the PCIe controller. The
following figure describes the DMA write and read process.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1224

Confidential
Figure 18-7 DMA Operation



DMA Write Channel
The DMA write channel is used for data transfer from local bus address space to the address
space in the PCIe domain. First, DMA controller reads data from the local bus address space
and writes them to the address space in the CPU domain. Then, the PCIe controller
transforms the write operation initiated by DMA into a write transaction in the PCIe domain
and writes data to the destination address space in the PCIe domain.



DMA Read Channel
The DMA read channel is used for data transfer from the address space in the PCIe domain to
the local bus address space such as DRAM address space. If a read operation is initiated by
DMA in the original address space of the CPU domain, the PCIe controller will transform the
read operation into a read transaction in the PCIe domain and write data to the local bus
address space.

18.3.5.4

MSI Operation
Message Signaled Interrupt (MSI) is a kind of mechanism that Endpoints send interrupt requests
to the CPU connected with the Root Complex. The MSI uses memory write transaction. The
memory write transaction message for transmitting interrupt information is MSI message.
Assume an Endpoint needs to send a MSI interrupt request to CPU. First, the Endpoint needs to
initiate a memory write transaction in the MSI address of PCIe domain, which will be transformed

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1225

Confidential
into a MSI interrupt signal to inform CPU by the PCIe controller after the transaction is detected
by RC.

18.3.6

Programming Guidelines

18.3.6.1

PCIe System Initialization
Initialize the PCIe system before using the PCIe controller. The steps are as below.
Step 1

Write 2b’10 to the SERDES_RST/SERDES_NOPPU_RST (bit [17:16]) register to dis-assert
Serdes_subsys reset.

18.3.6.2

Step 2

Write 2b’10 to PCIE0_BGR_REG (bit [17:16]) to dis-assert PCIe reset.

Step 3

Write 1 to XO_CTRL1_REG (bit[5]) to enable PCIe COMB PHY REF_CLK.

Step 4

Write 1 to the MBUS_MAT_CLK_GATING_REG (bit [28]) to enable MBUS_MCLK clock.

Step 5

Write 1 to the PCIE0_AUX_CLK_REG (bit [31]) to enable AUX clock.

Step 6

Write 1 to the PCIE0_AXI_SLV_CLK_REG (bit [31]) to enable SLV clock.

Step 7

Finish. CPU can access the PCIe registers.

PCIe Controller Initialization
Step 1

Write 0 to PCIe_LTSSM_ENABLE (bit [0])to disable LTSSM link training.

Step 2

Set the link, BAR space, and bus of PCIe controller

Step 3

Write 1 to PCIE_LTSSM_ENABLE (bit[0]) to enable LTSSM link training

Step 4

When like up finishes, the SII_INT_1 (bit[1:0]) will be asserted. Interrupts will be
generated.

18.3.7

Step 5

Set Gen1 as Gen2

Step 6

End. Then, the PCIe controller can transfer data with devices.

Description
MSTR_AWMISC_INFO_0
AXI Master Write Misc Information. AXI master
write transaction
associated miscellaneous information from the
TLP received by the
native PCIe controller. This is a signal that the
application can optionally
use. It is not part of the standard AXI interface.
■ Bus number, device number, function number,

and register
numbers are overlaid to the address bus when
type is configuration
transactions.
■ Message contents are also overlaid to the

address bus for MSG
TLPs. Bits [7:0] indicate the message code when
the type is
message.
31:0

R

0x0

For more details, see 'AXI Master Interface
Sideband Signals'. The bit
fields are mapped as follows:
■ [7:0]: Reserved except for MSG TLP. Bits [7:0]

indicate the message
code when the type is message.
■ [8:6]: BAR number of TLP
■ [9]: TLP is an I/O
■ [10]: TLP is in ROM range
■ [13:11]: TLP's Function number. Function

numbering starts at '0'.
This field is not used when CX_SRIOV_ENABLE =1
or CX_ARI_ENABLE
=1. For more details, see
mstr_awmisc_info_func_num.
■ [14]: TLP's NS bit
■ [15]: TLP's RO bit
■ [18:16]: TLP's TC bits
■ [23:19]: TLP's TYPE
■ [31:24]: TLP's requester ID_0

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1236

Confidential
Offset: 0x0150
Bit

Read/Write

Register Name: MSTR_BMISC_INFO
Default/Hex

Description
MSTR_BMISC_INFO_CPL_STAT
AXI Master Write Response selection bus. This
controls the response to be sent on the wire in the
case of successful write requests. The controller
always sends a CA (Completer Abort) response
when it receives SLVERR/DECERR.
▪ 00: SC (Successful Completion)
▪ 01: CA (Completer Abort)
▪ 10: UR (Unsupported Request)

1:0

R/W

0x0

▪ 11: SC (Successful Completion)
Your application must drive the same value on
mstr_bmisc_info_cpl_stat throughout the
complete response. For a multi-beat response,
when you set mstr_bmisc_info_cpl_stat to UR:
▪ If the first beat of the response produces a
slave error/decode error, the controller sends a
CPL with status as CA.
▪ If any beat (other than the first beat) of the
response has a slave/decode error, the controller
sends a CPL with status as UR.

APP_REQ_RETRY_EN
Provides a capability to defer incoming
configuration requests until initialization is
complete. When app_req_retry_en is asserted,
the controller completes incoming configuration
requests with a configuration request retry status.

8

R/W

0x0

Other incoming requests complete normally.
When the Readiness Notification mechanism is
supported, DRS messaging is blocked when
app_req_retry_en=1. When app_req_retry_en=0
and app_drs_ready=1, the controller
autonomously transmits a DRS message when
the link transitions from DL_Down to DL_Up.
