Bit

Read/Write

Register Name: PCIE_LTSSM_ENABLE
Default/Hex

Description
DEVICE_TYPE
Device/port type. Indicates the specific type of
this PCI Express function. It is also used to set the
'Device/Port Type' field of the 'PCI
Express Capabilities Register'. The controller uses
this input to determine the operating mode of the
controller at run time. Defined encodings are:
▪ 0000: PCI Express endpoint
▪ 0001: Legacy PCI Express endpoint

7:4

R/W

0x4

▪ 0100: Root port of PCI Express root complex
All other encodings (including those for PCI/PCI-X
bridges and RC Integrated endpoint) are not
supported. If CX_CROSSLINK_ENABLE is defined
and when smlh_crosslink_active is '1' then the
value device_type is modified as follows before
being used internally in the controller:
▪ if device_type =4'b0100 then device_type
=4'b0000
▪ if device_type =4'b000x then device_type
=4'b0100

3:1

/

/

/
APP_LTSSM_ENABLE
Link Training Enable
0: Disable link training
1: Enable link training
Driven low by your application after cold, warm or
hot reset to hold the LTSSM in the Detect state
until your application is ready for the link training
to begin. When your application has finished
reprogramming the controller configuration
registers using the DBI, it asserts

0

R/W

0x0

app_ltssm_enable to allow the LTSSM to
continue link establishment. Can also be used to
delay hot resetting of the controller until you have
read out any register status.
Cold Reset:
▪ Optionally hold LTSSM and delay link training,
so that you can reprogram some registers
through DBI.
▪ Set app_ltssm_enable =0 before your
application de-asserts Power-On Reset
(power_up_rst_n). Best way is to set

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1262

Confidential
Offset: 0x0c00
Bit

Read/Write

Register Name: PCIE_LTSSM_ENABLE
Default/Hex

Description
app_ltssm_enable =0 at power-up or at assertion
of core_rst_n.
▪ Wait for de-assertion of core_rst_n, sticky_rst_n,
and non_sticky_rst_n.
▪ Write any register through DBI.
▪ Set app_ltssm_enable =1.
▪ Link training starts.
Hot Reset (Link Down Reset) :
▪ Optionally delay reset of the controller, so that
you can read some registers through DBI.
▪ Set app_ltssm_enable =0 immediately
(combinatorically) upon falling edge of
smlh_req_rst_not.
▪ Keep app_ltssm_enable =0 until bridge finishes
"flushing mode".
▪ Read any register through DBI.
▪ Set app_ltssm_enable =1.
▪ Reset of controller begins (sticky_rst is not
asserted).
▪ Optionally hold LTSSM and delay link training,
so that you can reprogram some registers
through DBI.
▪ Set app_ltssm_enable =0 immediately
(combinatorically) upon falling edge of
core_rst_n.
▪ Write any register through DBI.
▪ Set app_ltssm_enable =1.
▪ Link training starts.
▪ Note: For Hot Reset, you can do both or either of
the above (delay reset and/or delay link training).
If you do both, you must do in order presented.
To do otherwise (that is, de-assert it outside of
the Detect LTSSM state) causes the controller to
be reset and the LTSSM moves immediately back
to the Detect state. This transition is outside of
the PCIe Specification and it might cause a PIPE
protocol violation.

PF0_CFG_VPD_INT
This pin is set as a one cycle pulse to notify your
application to read the VPD registers. The
sequence of events for a VPD read cycle is:
▪ The controller sends a request (single-cycle
pulse of the cfg_vpd_int signal) to your
application to read or write vital product data.
▪ Your application reads the VPD Control and
Capabilities register.
▪ The VPD Flag (bit 31) is set to '0' indicating a
read request. Your application fetches four bytes
of data from the VPD Address location and
transfers this to the VPD Data register.

0

R/W1C

0x0

▪ Your application sets the VPD Flag bit to '1'
indicating the request is complete.
The sequence of events for a VPD write cycle is:
▪ The controller sends a request (single-cycle
pulse of the cfg_vpd_int signal) to your
application to read or write vital product data.
▪ Your application reads the VPD Control and
Capabilities register.
▪ The VPD Flag (bit 31) is set to '1' indicating a
write request. Your application reads the VPD
Data register and transfers this to the location
specified by the VPD Address register.
▪ Your application sets the VPD Flag bit to '0'
indicating the request is complete.

Control and Status register is set to 1.
▪ Any bit in the Slot Status register transitions
from 0 to 1 and the associated event notification

The controller does not check if the PM state is

24

R/W1C

0x0

D1, D2, or D3hot. It is up to your application to

only if PME is enabled, but it does not matter if
hot-plug interrupts are enabled.

PF1_CFG_AER_RC_ERR_INT
Asserted when a reported error condition causes
a bit to be set in the Root Error Status register and
the associated error message reporting enable bit
is set in the Root Error Command register.
cfg_aer_rc_err_int is set when the RC internally

20

R/W1C

0x0

received by the RC. Because the RC itself

PF1_CFG_VPD_INT
This pin is set as a one cycle pulse to notify your
application to read the VPD registers. The
sequence of events for a VPD read cycle is:
▪ The controller sends a request (single-cycle
pulse of the cfg_vpd_int signal) to your
application to read or write vital product data.
▪ Your application reads the VPD Control and
Capabilities register.
▪ The VPD Flag (bit 31) is set to '0' indicating a
read request. Your application fetches four bytes
of data from the VPD Address location and
transfers this to the VPD Data register.

19

R/W1C

0x0

▪ Your application sets the VPD Flag bit to '1'
indicating the request is complete.
The sequence of events for a VPD write cycle is:
▪ The controller sends a request (single-cycle
pulse of the cfg_vpd_int signal) to your
application to read or write vital product data.
▪ Your application reads the VPD Control and
Capabilities register.
▪ The VPD Flag (bit 31) is set to '1' indicating a
write request. Your application reads the VPD
Data register and transfers this to the location
specified by the VPD Address register.
▪ Your application sets the VPD Flag bit to '0'
indicating the request is complete.

18.4

USB3.1 GEN2 DRD

18.4.1

Overview
The USB3.1 GEN2 DRD is a Dual-Role Device (DRD) controller, which supports both device and
host functions which can also be configured as a Host-only or Device-only controller, fully
compliant with the USB 3.1 Specification. It can support super-speed plus (SSP, 10-Gbps),
super-speed (SS, 5-Gbps), high-speed (HS, 480-Mbps), full-speed (FS, 12-Mbps), and low-speed
(LS, 1.5-Mbps) transfers in Host mode. It can support super-speed plus (SSP, 10-Gbps),
super-speed (SS, 5-Gbps), high-speed (HS, 480-Mbps), and full-speed (FS, 12-Mbps) in Device
mode. Standard USB transceiver can be used through its UTMI+ interface and PIPE interface.
The USB3.1 GEN2 DRD controller includes the following features:


Supports Super-Speed Plus (SSP, 10-Gbps), Super-Speed (SS, 5-Gbps), High-Speed (HS,
480-Mbps), Full-Speed (FS, 12-Mbps) in Device mode



Supports Super-Speed Plus (SSP, 10-Gbps), Super-Speed (SS, 5-Gbps), High-Speed (HS,
480-Mbps), Full-Speed (FS, 12-Mbps) and Low-Speed (LS, 1.5-Mbps) in Host mode



Supports Device or Host operation at a time



AXI interface for DMA operation



AHB Slave interface for read and write access to the core’s Control and Status Registers
(CSRs).



USB3.1 PIPE PHY interface



USB2.0 UTMI+ PHY interface. USB3.1 has independent USB2.0 PHY.



Supports up to 16 Endpoints IN（including control endpoint 0）, 16 Endpoints OUT（including
control endpoint 0）in device mode



15 pairs of endpoints share TX FIFO (21 KB) and RX FIFO (asynchronous transmission 8KB
and periodic transmission 8KB). The size of Endpoint 0 RX/TX FIFO is 64B.



Simultaneous IN and OUT transfer support in Super-Speed Plus and Super-Speed mode



Dual-port interfaces for Tx data buffering, Rx data prefetching, and descriptor and register
caching



Three RAMs are configuration as Rx Data FIFO RAM, Tx Data FIFO RAM, Descriptor/Register
Cache RAM



Hardware handles all data transfer



Implements both static and dynamic power reduction techniques at multiple levels

TESTBURNIN
Burn-in Test Enable
This input enables the built-in, self-burn-in testing
function of thePHY. At assertion of this signal, the
PHY performs a power-on-reset sequence and then
enters HS Loopback mode. In HS Loopbackmode,
the PHY continues to transmit alternating 1's and 0's
at the maximum bit rate until TESTBURNIN is
de-asserted.

14

R/W

0x0

This input has precedence over the SUSPENDM0,
PORTRESET0, ATERESET, and SLEEPM0 signals.
Therefore, these signals are internally overridden
when TESTBURNIN isasserted.
Asserting TESTBURNIN causes the FSEL[2:0] and
REFCLKSEL[1:0] signals to be overridden, so that the
PHY requires a 50-MHzreference clock on CLKCORE.
If this signal is not used, tie it low. Toaccomplish the
same function with a different reference clock
frequency, thePHY can be put into BIST Test Packet
Repeatmode.

18.5

USB2.0 DRD

18.5.1

Overview
The USB2.0 dual-role device (USB2.0 DRD) supports both device and host functions which can
also be configured as a Host-only or Device-only controller.
The USB2.0 DRD has the following features:


Compatible with USB2.0 Specification



Supports USB2.0 Host Function



-

Compatible with Enhanced Host Controller Interface (EHCI) Specification, Version 1.0

-

Compatible with Open Host Controller Interface (OHCI) Specification, Version 1.0a

-

Supports High-Speed (HS, 480 Mbps)

-

Supports Full-Speed (FS, 12 Mbps)

-

Supports Low-Speed (LS, 1.5 Mbps)

-

Supports only 1 USB Root Port shared between EHCI and OHCI

Supports USB2.0 Device Function
-

Supports High-Speed (HS, 480 Mbps)

-

Supports Full-Speed (FS, 12 Mbps)

-

Supports bi-directional Endpoint0 for Control transfer

-

Supports 9 Endpoints IN (including control endpoint 0), 9 Endpoints OUT (including
control endpoint 0)

-

Supports up to (8KB+64Bytes) FIFO for EPs (Including EP0)

-

Supports interface to an external Normal DMA controller for every EPs (Endpoint1,
Endpoint2, Endpoint3, Endpoint4, Endpoint5, Endpoint6, Endpoint7, Endpoint8)



Supports an internal DMA Controller for data transfer with memory



Supports High-bandwidth Isochronous & Interrupt transfers



Supports Automated splitting/combining of packets for Bulk transfers



Supports point-to-point and point-to-multipoint transfer in both Host and Peripheral mode



Supports Automatic ping capabilities



18.6

USB2.0 HOST

18.6.1

Overview
The USB2.0 Host Controller is fully compliant with USB 2.0 Specification, Enhanced Host
Controller Interface (EHCI) Specification Revision 1.0 and Open Host Controller Interface (OHCI)
Specification Release 1.0a. The controller supports high-speed, 480-Mbps transfers (40 times
faster than USB 1.1 full-speed mode) using an EHCI Host Controller, as well as full and low
speeds through one or more integrated OHCI Host Controllers.
The USB2.0 host controller includes the following features:


Supports industry-standard AMBA High-Performance Bus (AHB) and it is fully compliant with
the AMBA Specification, Revision 2.0.



Supports 32-bit Little Endian AMBA AHB Slave Bus for Register Access.



Supports 35-bit Little Endian AMBA AHB Master Bus for Memory Access.



Includes an internal DMA controller for data transfer with memory.



Complies with Enhanced Host Controller Interface (EHCI) Specification, Version 1.0, and the
Open Host Controller Interface (OHCI) Specification, Version 1.0a.



Supports High-Speed (HS, 480-Mbps), Full-Speed (FS, 12-Mbps), and Low-Speed (LS,
1.5-Mbps) Device.



Supports the UTMI+ Level 3 interface. The 8-bit bidirectional data buses are used.



Supports only 1 USB Root Port shared between EHCI and OHCI.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

18.7

PWM

18.7.1

Overview
The Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) module can the configurable PWM waveform output and the
input waveform capture.
The PWM has the following features:






Up to 30 PWM channels and 3 PWM controllers:
-

PWM0_[9:0] for PWM0 controller

-

PWM1_[9:0] for PWM1 controller

-

S_PWM0_[9:0] for S_PWM0 controller

Maximum 10 independent PWM channels for each PWM controller
-

Supports PWM output in cycle mode

-

Supports PWM output in pulse mode, and the pulse number is configurable

-

Output frequency range:


0 to 24 MHz if the clock source is SYS_CLK24M



0 to 100 MHz if the clock source is APB0 clock

-

Various duty-cycle: 0% to 100%

-

Minimum resolution: 1/65536

Maximum 5 complementary pairs output
-

PWM01 pair (PWM0 + PWM1), PWM23 pair (PWM2 + PWM3), PWM45 pair (PWM4 + PWM5),
PWM67 pair (PWM6 + PWM7), PWM89 pair (PWM8 + PWM9)



Supports dead-zone generator, and the dead-time is configurable

Maximum 4 groups of PWM channel output for controlling stepper motors
-

Supports any plural channels to form a group, and output the same duty-cycle pulse

-

In the group mode, the relative phase of the output waveform for each channel is
configurable





Maximum 10 channels of input capture
-

Supports detection at the rising and falling edges

-

Supports pulse-width measurement

Supports 10 channels of input waveform counting

18.7.5.1

PWM Clock Controller
The clock controller of each PWM pair, for instance PWM01, includes clock source select
(PWM01_CLK_SRC), 1-256 scaler (PWM01_CLK_DIV_M). Each PWM channel has the secondary
frequency division (PWM_PRESCAL_K), clock source bypass (PWMx_CLK_BYPASS) and clock
switch (PWMx_CLK_GATING).
The clock sources of PWM include SYS_CLK24M and APB0. The OSC comes from the external
high-frequency oscillator or 24MHz internal PLL; the APB0 is usually the 100MHz APB0 bus clock.
The clock sources of S_PWM include DCXO, RTC_32K, RC16M, and SYS_CLK24M. For details, see
the section PRCM. The clock bypass is to select the clock for PWM output. The following figure
shows the PWM01 Clock Source Bypass.

18.7.5.2

PWM Output
Take PWM01 as an example. Figure 18-13 indicates the PWM01 output logic diagram. The logic
diagrams of other PWM pairs are the same as that of PWM01.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1344

Confidential
Figure 18-13 PWM01 Output Logic Module Diagram

The timer logic module of PWM consists of one 16-bit up-counter (PCNTR) and three 16-bit
parameters

(PWM_ENTIRE_CYCLE,

PWM_ACT_CYCLE,

PWM_COUNTER_START).

The

PWM_ENTIRE_CYCLE is used to control the PWM cycle, the PWM_ACT_CYCLE is used to control
the duty cycle, the PWM_COUNTER_START is used to control the output phase (multi-channel
synchronization work requirements).
The PWM_ENTIRE_CYCLE and the PWM_ACT_CYCLE support the cache load. After PWM output is
enabled, the register values of the PWM_ENTIRE_CYCLE and the PWM_ACT_CYCLE can be
changed anytime, and the changed value caches into the cache register. When the PCNTR
counter outputs a period of PWM waveform, the value of the cache register can be updated for
the PCNTR control. The purpose of the cache load is to avoid the unstable PWM output
waveform with glitches when updating the values of the PWM_ENTIRE_CYCLE and
PWM_ACT_CYCLE. The PWM_CNTSTART doesn’t support cache load, and only can be
configured before enabling PWM output.
The PWM supports waveform output in cycle mode and pulse mode.
Cycle mode: The PWM outputs the set PWM waveform continually; that is, the output waveform
is a continuous PWM square wave.
Pulse mode: After setting the PWM_PUL_NUM parameter, the PWM outputs (PWM_PULNUM+1)
periods of PWM waveform; that is, the waveform with several pulses are output.
Note: As the data width of PWM_PUL_CNT is 16 bits, it output maximum 65536 PWM waveforms.

NOTE
As the data width of PWM_PUL_CNT is 16 bits, it output maximum 65536 PWM waveforms.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

The principle of inserting dead-time is to insert dead-time at every rising edge. If the high level
period in mark ② is less than dead-time, then dead-time will override the high level period.
Therefore, the setting of dead-time needs to consider the period and the duty-cycle of the output
waveform. The dead-time formula is defined as follows:
Dead time = (PWM01_CLK / PWM0_PRESCALE_K)-1 * PDZINTV01
18.7.5.3

PWM Group Mode
The PWM group mode is used to satisfy the PWM group signals of stepper motors in different
phases. Take PWM Group0 as an example. The PGR0.CS selects the PWM channel working in the
same group; the same parameters of PWM_ENTIRE_CYCLE, PWM_ACT_CYCLE are set through the
same clock configuration; the different PWM_COUNTER_START can output PWM group signals
with the same duty-cycle and the different phase. PCNTR counting starts from 0 by default, and
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential
the phase of output waveform can be controlled through PWM_CNTSTART configuration. If the
stepper motor uses the PWM group mode, it is recommended to divide 0, 1, 2, 3 into a group, and
4, 5, 6, 7 another group.

When the capture input function of the PWM0 channel is enabled, the PCNTR of the PWM0
channel starts to work.
When the timer logic module of PWM0 captures a rising edge, the current value of PCNTR is
locked to CRLR0, and CCR0[CRLF] is set to 1. If CRIE0 is 1, and CRIS0 is set to 1, the PWM0 channel
will send interrupt requests, and the up-counter will be reloaded to 0 and continue to count. If
CRIE0 is 0, CRIS0 will not be set to 1 when the timer logic module of PWM0 captures a rising edge;
thus, the up-counter will not reloaded to 0.
When the timer logic module of PWM0 captures a falling edge, the current value of PCNTR is
locked to CFLR0, and CCR0[CFLF] is set to 1. If CFIE0 is 1, and CFIS0 is set to 1, the PWM0 channel
will send interrupt requests, and the up-counter will be reloaded to 0 and continue to count. If
CFIE0 is 0, CFIS0 will not be set to 1 when the timer logic module of PWM0 captures a falling edge;
thus, the up-counter will not reloaded to 0.

18.7.6
18.7.6.1

Programming Guidelines
Clock Configuration
Step 1

When using PWM, write 1 to PWMx_CLK_GATING in the PCGR; otherwise. Otherwise,
write 0 to mask.

Step 2

Set PWMn_CLK_SRC in the PCCRn to select SYS_CLK24M or APB0 clock.

Step 3

Set PWM01_CLK_DIV_M in the PCCRn to select different frequency division coefficient
(1/2/4/8/16/32/64/128/256).

Step 4

Set PWM_CLK_SRC_BYPASS_TO_PWM in the PCGR to 1, output the PWM clock after the
secondary frequency division to the corresponding PWM output pin.

Step 5

Set PWM_PRESCAL_K in the PCR to select any frequency division coefficient from 1 to
256.
NOTE

The channels in the complementary output and group mode needs the same clock configuration,
simultaneously opened clock gating, PWM parameter configuration, and enabled PWM output at
the same time to ensure the synchronization among channels. Besides, as a PWM pair shares the
same first-level clock division and gating, their two channels cannot be allocated to different
groups in the group mode. If the allocation still exists, the same first-level clock division and the
simultaneously opened gating is required. The total module needs to be reset when the group
mode regroups.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1350

Confidential
18.7.6.2

PWM Configuration
Step 1

To configure PWM mode, set PWM_MODE to select cycle mode or pulse mode; if pulse
mode is to be selected, set PWM_PUL_NUM in the PCR.

Step 2

To configure PWM active level, set PWM_ACT_STA to select a low level or high level in
the PCR.

Step 3

To configure PWM duty-cycle, set PWM_ENTIRE_CYCLE and PWM_ACT_CYCLE after
clock gating is opened in PPR.

Step 4

To configure PWM starting phase, set PWM_COUNTER_START in the PCNTR before the
PWM is enabled. You can verify whether the configuration is successful by reading back
PWM_COUNTER_STATUS in the PCNTR.

Step 5

To enable PWM, select the corresponding PWM enable bit in the PER; pulse mode is to
be selected, set PWM_PUL_NUM in the PCR.

18.7.6.3

18.7.6.4

Deadzone Configuration
Step 1

Set PDZINTVn to 1 to configure deadzone interval value in the PDZCRn.

Step 2

Set PWMn_DZ_CN to 1 to enable PWM01 deadzone in the PDZCRn.

Capture Input Configuration
Step 1

Set CAPn_EN to 1 to enable the capture functions of corresponding channels in the CER.
In addition, set CFIEn or CRIEn to 1 in the CIER to generate the capture channel pending.

Step 2

To configure the capture method, confirm whether to capture in the rising edge or
falling edge through CRLF and CFLF in the CCR. Confirm whether to invert the input
signal through CAPINV in the CCR.

18.7.6.5

Number of Captured Input Signals
Enable Input Counting and Input Capture Simultaneously
To enable input counting and input capture simultaneously, follow the steps as below.
Step 1

To configure the capture method, confirm whether to capture in the rising edge or
falling edge through CRLF and CFLF in the CCR. Confirm whether to invert the input
signal through CAPINV in the CCR.

Step 2

Set the CCSR to 1 in the CCR.

Step 3

Confirm whether to count in the falling edge or rising edge through CCCRFR in the CCCR.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1351

Confidential
Step 4

Confirm whether to stop or restart counting when reaching the count value through
CCCSRR in the CCCR.

Step 5

Set the number of CCCNR and enable the corresponding channels of CCCIER. When the
input signal reach the set value of CCCNR, an interrupt will be generated.

Step 6

Set CFIEn or CRIEn to 1 in the CIER to generate the capture channel pending.

Step 7

Set CAPn_EN to 1 in the CER to enable corresponding capture functions.

Enable Input Counting Separately
To enable input counting separately, follow the steps as below.
Step 1

Confirm whether to invert the input signal through CAPINV in CCR.

Step 2

Set CCSR to 0 in CCR.

Step 3

Confirm whether to count in the falling edge or rising edge through CCCRFR in the CCCR.

Step 4

Confirm whether to stop or restart counting when reaching the count value through
CCCSRR in the CCCR.

Step 5

Set the number of CCCNR and enable the corresponding channels of CCCIER. When the
input signal reach the set value of CCCNR, an interrupt will be generated.

Step 6

18.7.7

Set CAP_CNTn_EN to 1 to enable the counting of corresponding channels of CCCER.

18.8

SPI

18.8.1

Overview
The Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) is a full-duplex, synchronous, four-wire serial
communication interface between a CPU and SPI-compliant external devices. It can work in
master mode and slave mode.
The SPI has the following features:




Four SPI interfaces:
-

SPI0, SPI2, and SPI3 in CPUX Domain

-

S_SPI0 in CPUS Domain

Supports multiple SPI mode
-

Master mode and Slave mode Standard SPI (4-wire)

-

Master mode Dual-Output/Dual-Input SPI/ Dual I/O SPI

-

Master mode Quad-Output/Quad-Input SPI

-

Master mode 3-wire SPI, with programmable serial data frame length: 1bit to 32bits



Supports the Maximum clock frequency: 100MHz



Supports TX/RX DMA Slave interface



Transmits data FIFO with 8-bit wide and 64-entry



Receives data FIFO with 8-bit wide and 64-entry



Transmits data buffer with 8-bit wide and 4-entry



Receives data buffer with 8-bit wide and 128-entry



Supports Data Sample Mode
-



Mode0, Mode1, Mode2 and Mode3

Supports Control signal config
-

Up to four chip selects to support multiple peripherals

-

Polarity and phase of the Chip Select (SPI_CS) and SPI Clock (SPI_CLK) are configurable
NOTE

This chapter only describes SPI0, SPI2, SPI3, and S_SPI0. For the detailed information of SPI1
with SPI mode and DBI mode, please refer to section 18.9 SPI_DBI.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Functional Description
SPI Master and Slave Mode
The SPI controller can be configured to a master or slave device. The master mode is selected by
setting the MODE bit (SPI_GCR[1]); the slave mode is selected by clearing the MODE bit.
In master mode, the SPI_CLK is generated and transmitted to the external device, and the data
from the TX FIFO is transmitted on the MOSI pin, the data from the slave is received on the MISO
pin and sent to RX FIFO. The Chip Select (SPI_CS) is an active low signal, and it must be set low
before the data are transmitted or received. The SPI_CS can be selected the auto control mode
or the software manual control mode. When using auto control, the SS_OWNER (SPI_TCR[6])
must be cleared (default value is 0); when using manual control, the SS_OWNER must be set. And
the level of SPI_CS is controlled by SS_LEVEL (SPI_TCR[7]).
In slave mode, after the software selects the MODE bit (SPI_GCR [1]) to '0', it waits for master to
initiate a transaction. When the master asserts SPI_CS, and SPI_CLK is transmitted to the slave,
the slave data is transmitted from TX FIFO on the MISO pin, and the data from the MOSI pin is
received in RX FIFO.
If using the Master and Slave function of the SPIC, conform to the circuit connection between the
Master and Slave as shown below.
Figure 18-20 Circuit Connection between the Master and Slave

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

18.8.5.2

SPI Transmit Format
The SPI supports 4 different formats for data transfer. The software can select one of the four
modes in which the SPI works by setting the bit1 (Polarity) and bit0 (Phase) of SPI_TCR (Offset:
0x0008). The SPI controller master uses the SPI_CLK signal to transfer data in and out of the shift
register. Data is clocked using any one of four programmable clock phase and polarity
combinations.
The CPOL (SPI_TCR [1]) defines the polarity of the clock signal (SPI_CLK). The SPI_CLK is a high
level when CPOL is ‘1’ and it is a low level when CPOL is ‘0’. The CPHA (SPI_TCR [0])
decides whether the leading edge of SPI_CLK is used to setup or sample data. The leading edge
is used to setup data when CPHA is ‘1’, and sample data when CPHA is ‘0’. The following
table lists the four modes.
Table 18-9 SPI Transmit Format

SPI Dual Mode
The dual read mode (SPI x2) is selected when the DRM is set in SPI_BCC (Offset: 0x0038) [28].
Using the dual mode allows data to be transferred to or from the device at double the rate of
standard single mode, the data can be read at fast speed using two data bits (MOSI and MISO) at
a time. The following figure describes the dual-input/dual-output SPI and the dual I/O SPI.

18.8.5.6

SPI Error Conditions
If any error conditions occur, the hardware will set the corresponding status bits in the SPI
Interrupt Status Register (Offset: 0x0014) and stop the transfer. For the SPI controller, the
following error scenarios can happen.


TX_FIFO Underrun

The TX_FIFO underrun happens when the CPU/DMA reads data from the empty TX FIFO. In the
case, the SPI controller will end the transaction and flag the error bit along with the TF_UDF bit
in the SPI Interrupt Status Register (Offset: 0x0014). The SPI controller will generate an interrupt
if interrupts are enabled. The software has to clear the error bit and the TF_UDF bit. To start a
new transaction, the software has to reset the FIFO by writing to the SRST (soft reset) bit in the
SPI Global Control Register (Offset: 0x0004).


TX_FIFO Overflow

The TX_FIFO overflow happens when the CPU/DMA writes data into the full TX FIFO. In the case,
the SPI controller will end the transaction and flag the error bit along with the TF_OVF bit in the
SPI Interrupt Status Register (Offset: 0x0014). The SPI controller will generate an interrupt if
interrupts are enabled. The software has to clear the error bit and the TF_OVF bit. To start a new
transaction, the software has to reset the FIFO by writing to the SRST (soft reset) bit in the SPI
Global Control Register (Offset: 0x0004).

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1400

Confidential


RX_FIFO Underrun

The RX_FIFO underrun happens when the CPU/DMA reads data from RX FIFO when it is empty. In
the case, the SPI controller will end the transaction and flag the error bit along with the RF_UDF
bit in the SPI Interrupt Status Register (Offset: 0x0014). The SPI controller will generate an
interrupt if interrupts are enabled. The software has to clear the error bit and the RF_UDF bit. To
start a new transaction, the software has to reset the FIFO by writing to the SRST (soft reset) bit
in the SPI Global Control Register (Offset: 0x0004).


RX_FIFO Overflow

The RX_FIFO overflow happens when the CPU/DMA writes data into the RX FIFO when it is full. In
the case, the SPI controller will end the transaction and flag the error bit along with the RF_OVF
bit in the SPI Interrupt Status Register (Offset: 0x0014). The SPI controller will generate an
interrupt if interrupts are enabled. The software has to clear the error bit and the RF_OVF bit. To
start a new transaction, the software has to reset the FIFO by writing to the SRST (soft reset) bit
in the SPI Global Control Register (Offset: 0x0004).

frequency A MHz. 2 stage division coefficient N & M should be set.

Programming Guidelines
CPU or DMA Transfer
The SPI transfers serial data between the processor and peripheral devices. The CPU mode and
DMA mode are the two main operational modes for SPI. For each SPI, the data is simultaneously
transmitted (shifted out serially) and received (shifted in serially). The SPI has 2 channels,
including the TX channel and RX channel. The TX channel has the path from TX FIFO to peripheral
devices. The RX channel has the path from peripheral devices to RX FIFO.
Write Data: The CPU or DMA must write data on the SPI_TXD (Offset: 0x0200), the data on the
register are automatically moved to TX FIFO.
Read Data: To read data from RX FIFO, the CPU or DMA must access the SPI_RXD (Offset: 0x0300)
and the data are automatically sent to the SPI_RXD (Offset: 0x0300).
In CPU or DMA mode, the SPI sends a completed interrupt (SPI_ISR[TC]) to the processor after
each transmission is complete.

18.8.6.2

Master Transmit and Receive Burst
In the SPI Master mode, the transmit and receive bursts (byte in unit) are configured before the
SPI transfers serial data between the processor and external device. The transmit burst write in
MWTC (bit[23:0]) of SPI Master Transmit Counter Register. The transmit burst in single mode
before automatically sending dummy burst write in STC (bit[23:0]) of SPI Master Burst Control
Counter Register. For dummy data, SPI controller can automatically sent before receive by
writing DBC (bit[27:24]) in SPI Master Burst Control Counter Register. If users don't use SPI
controller to send dummy data automatically, then the dummy bursts are used as the transmit
counters to write together in MWTC (bit[23:0]) of SPI Master Transmit Counter Register. In Master
mode, the total burst numbers write in MBC (bit[23:0]) of SPI Master Burst Counter Register.
When all transmit burst and receive burst are transferred, SPI controller will send a completed
interrupt, at the same time, SPI controller will clear DBC, MWTC and MBC.

18.8.6.3

SPI Run Clock and Sample Mode
The SPI Controller runs at 24KHz~100MHz at its interface to external SPI devices. The internal SPI
Clock should run at the same frequency as the outgoing clock in master mode. The SPI Clock is
selected different clock sources, and SPI must configure different work mode. There are three
work mode: normal sample mode, delay half cycle sample mode, delay one cycle sample mode.
Delay half cycle sample mode is the default mode of SPI controller. When SPI runs at 48MHz or
below 48MHz, SPI can work at normal sample mode or delay half cycle sample mode. When SPI
runs over 48MHz, set SDC in SPI Transfer Control Register to ‘1’ to make the internal read
sample point with a delay of half cycle of SPI_CLK, which is used in high-speed read operation to
reduce the error caused by the time delay of SPI_CLK propagating between master and slave
device. The different configuration of new/old SPI sample mode shows in the following tables.
Table 18-10 SPI Old Sample Mode
SPI Sample Mode

SDM(bit13)

SDC(bit11)

1

0

<=24MHz

0

0

<=40MHz

0

>=80MHz

delay half cycle
sample
delay one cycle
sample

NOTE
The remaining frequencies are not recommended. When the SPI Flash output delay time is the
same as the half-cycle time of the SPI working clock, it will cause the device output data edge to
along with the controller clock sampling edge. Therefore, setting a delay of one cycle sampling
may lead to instabilities.

18.9

SPI_DBI

18.9.1

Overview
The SoC provides a 3/4 line SPI display bus interface (SPI_DBI) for video data transmission. It
supports DBI mode or SPI mode. The DBI mode can be configured with 3-wire/4-wire
transmission and compatible with multiple video data formats at the same time. The integrated
SPI mode is used for low-cost display schemes.
The SPI mode has the following features:


Supports multiple SPI mode
-

Master mode and Slave mode Standard SPI (4wire)

-

Master mode Dual-Output/Dual-Input SPI/ Dual I/O SPI

-

Master mode Quad-Output/Quad-Input SPI

-

Master mode 3wire SPI, with programmable serial data frame length: 1bit to 32bits



Supports the Maximum clock frequency: 100MHz



Supports TX/RX DMA Slave interface



Transmits data FIFO with 8-bit wide and 64-entry



Receives data FIFO with 8-bit wide and 64-entry



Transmits data buffer with 8-bit wide and 4-entry



Receives data buffer with 8-bit wide and 128-entry



Supports Data Sample Mode: Mode0, Mode1, Mode2 and Mode3



Supports Control signal config
-

Two chip selects to support multiple peripherals

-

Polarity and phase of the Chip Select (SPI_CS) and SPI Clock (SPI_CLK) are configurable

The DBI mode has the following features:


Supports DBI Type C 3 Line/4 Line Interface Mode



Supports 2 Data Lane Interface Mode



Supports RGB111/444/565/666/888 video format



Supports maximum resolution of RGB666 240 x 320@30Hz with single data lane



Supports maximum resolution of RGB888 240 x 320@60Hz or 320 x 480@30Hz with dual data
lane



Supports tearing effect



Supports software flexible control video frame rate

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1424

Confidential

NOTE
This chapter only describes SPI1 (with SPI mode and DBI mode). For detailed information of SPI0,
SPI2, SPI3, and S_SPI0, please refer to the section SPI.

18.9.5.2

DBI 3-Line Interface Write and Read Timing
DBI 3-Line Interface Write Timing
The 3-line DBI Interface I contains CSX, SDA, and SCL, where SDA shares this port for bidirectional
port data input and output.
The 3-line DBI Interface II contains CSX, SDA, SCL, and SDI; Data input and output ports are
independent of each other.
As there is no Data/Command data line in the 3-line display bus mode, whether Data or
Command is currently being transmitted cannot be confirmed. Thus, an extra bit is added to the
data-stream before MSB to indicate whether Data or Command is currently being transmitted. (0:
Command, 1: Data)

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

DBI 4-Line Interface Write and Read Timing
DBI 4-Line Interface Write Timing
The 4-line DBI Interface I contains CSX, D/CX, SDA, and SCL, where SDA shares this port for
bidirectional port data input and output.
The 4-line DBI Interface II contains CSX, D/CX, SDA, SCL, and SDI; Data input and output ports are
independent of each other.
Since the 4-line display bus mode has a Data/Command data line indicating whether Data or
Command is currently being transmitted (0: Command, 1: Data). So there is no need to add an
extra bit to data-stream before MSB like the 3-line DBI.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

There is a Data/Command data line in the 4-line display bus mode to indicate whether Data or
Command is currently being transmitted. (0: Command, 1: Data) Thus, no extra bit is needed.

18.9.5.7

SPI_DBI Clock Frequency
The equation of SPI_DBI clock frequency is
fSPI_CLK = frame_rate * one_pixel_clock_cycle * one_frame_pixel_value
The meaning of each sub-item is as follows:


frame_rate: The frame rate at the unit of Hz.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1439

Confidential


one_pixel_clock_cycle: The clock period cycle of transferring a pixel. The period cycle differs
from different transferring format.



-

2-data lane-RGB444: 9 cycles

-

2-data lane-RGB565: 9 cycles

-

2-data lane-RGB666-Format0: 10 cycles

-

2-data lane-RGB888: 13 cycles

one_frame_pixel_value: The number of pixel in one frame.
-

240*320

-

320*480

For example, RGB data is transferred with 2 data line and RGB666 mode, and the resolution and
frame rate of the display are 240*320 and 60Hz, then the SPI clock frequency is
60*10*240*320=46.08MHz.
The following tables show the SCLK frequency in different RGB modes.

Programming Guidelines
NOTE
The following are the programming guidelines in DBI mode. For those in SPI mode, see the
section SPI.

18.9.6.1

Write Command Transfer
Step 1

Set the SPI_DBI_MODE_SEL (bit3) of SPI_GCR (0x0004) to 1 to select DBI mode.

Step 2

Set the DBI_EN_MODE_SEL (bit[30:29]) of DBI_CTL_1 (0x0104) to 0 to select the trigger
mode of DBI.

Step 3

Configure the DBI_CTL_0 (0x0100).
a)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Command Type] (bit31) to 0 to configure the writing command.

b)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Write Command Dummy Cycles] (bit[30:20]) to configure the
number of dummy cycles between commands.

c)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Output Data Sequence] (bit19) to select the MSB or LSB.

d)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Transmit Mode] (bit15) to 0 to select the command path.

e)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Output Data Format] (bit[14:12]) to 0 to transmit the command.

f)

Set DBI_CTL_0[DBI interface Select] (bit[10:8]) to select the DBI interface type.

g)

The remaining values of the DBI_CTL_0 register remain the default value.

Step 4

Set DBI_CTL_1[DCX_DATA] (bit22) to 0 to send the command.

Step 5

DMA Path: Configure the SPI_FCR register (0x0018).
a)

Set SPI_FCR[TF_DRQ_EN] (bit24) to 1 to enable TXFIFO DMA.

b)

Set SPI_FCR[TX_TRIG_LEVEL] (bit[23:16]) to 255. It indicates the controller requests
data from DMA if the remaining space of TX FIFO is greater than 255.

CPU Path: Write the command to be sent to the 0x200 address.
Step 6

Set SPI_GCR[DBI_EN] (bit4) to 1 to start transmitting the command.

Step 7

Wait until the TX FIFO underrun interrupt (SPI_ISR[TF_UDF]) is 1. It indicates that the
command written to the TX FIFO is transmitted completely.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1441

Confidential
18.9.6.2

Parameter Transfer
Step 1

Set the SPI_DBI_MODE_SEL (bit3) of SPI_GCR (0x0004) to 1 to select DBI mode.

Step 2

Set the DBI_EN_MODE_SEL (bit[30:29]) of DBI_CTL_1 (0x0104) to 0 to select the trigger
mode of DBI.

Step 3

Configure the DBI_CTL_0 register (0x0100).
a)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Command Type] (bit31) to 0 to configure the writing command.

b)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Write Command Dummy Cycles] (bit[30:20]) to configure the
number of dummy cycles between commands.

c)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Output Data Sequence] (bit19) to select the MSB or LSB.

d)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Transmit Mode] (bit15) to 0 to select the command path.

e)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Output Data Format] (bit[14:12]) to 0 to transmit the command.

f)

Set DBI_CTL_0[DBI interface Select] (bit[10:8]) to select the DBI interface type.

g)

The remaining values of the DBI_CTL_0 register remain the default value.

Step 4

Set DBI_CTL_1[DCX_DATA] (bit22) to 1 to send the parameter.

Step 5

DMA Path: Configure the SPI_FCR register (0x0018).
a)

Set SPI_FCR[TF_DRQ_EN] (bit24) to 1 to enable TXFIFO DMA.

b)

Set SPI_FCR[TX_TRIG_LEVEL] (bit[23:16]) to 255. It indicates the controller requests
data from DMA if the remaining space of TX FIFO is greater than 255.

CPU Path: Write the command to be sent to the 0x200 address.
Step 6

Set SPI_GCR[DBI_EN] (bit4) to 1 to start transmitting the command.

Step 7

Wait until the TX FIFO underrun interrupt (SPI_ISR[TF_UDF]) is 1. It indicates that the
command written to the TX FIFO is transmitted completely.

18.9.6.3

Video Transfer
Before the video transmission configuration, confirm whether the data is from CPU path or DMA
path.
a)

If the data is from the CPU path, the controller writes the command to be sent to the 0x0200
address by the AHB bus.

b)

If the data is from the DMA path, configure DBI_CTL_2[DBI_FIFO_DRQ_EN] (bit15) to 1 and
DBI_CTL_2[TX_TRIG_LEVEL] (bit[14:8]) to 64. The controller will request data from DMA if the
remaining space of TX FIFO is greater than 64. The empty & full interrupts and the status bit
of DBI FIFO can be configured in the DBI_INT and DBI_DEBUG_0.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1442

Confidential
Software Trigger Mode
The software enables DBI_en_trigger when the edge interrupt of TE is detected.
After transmitting a frame of image, the controller automatically clears the line_cnt, pixel_cnt
and stops data transmission.
The operation process is as follows.
Step 1

Set the SPI_DBI_MODE_SEL (bit3) of SPI_GCR (0x0004) to 1 to select DBI mode.

Step 2

Set the DBI EN MODE SEL (bit[30:29]) of DBI_CTL_1 (0x0104) to 01 to select the software
trigger mode.

Step 3

Configure the DBI_CTL_0 register (0x0100).
a)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Command Type] (bit31) to 0 to set the writing command.

b)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Write Command Dummy Cycles] (bit[30:20]) to configure the
number of dummy cycles between commands.

c)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Output Data Sequence] (bit19) to select the MSB or LSB.

d)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Transmit Mode] (bit15) to 1 to select the image path.

e)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Output Data Format] (bit[14:12]) to select RGB111/444/565/666/888.

f)

Set DBI_CTL_0[DBI interface Select] (bit[10:8]) to select the DBI interface type.

g)

The remaining values of the DBI_CTL_0 register remain the default value.

Step 4

Set DBI_CTL_1[DCX_DATA] (bit22) to 0 to send the image data.

Step 5

Configure DBI_Video_Size (0x110) according to the sent image size.

Step 6

Configure DBI_CTL_2 (0x0108) to set the TE-related parameter.

Step 7

Detect the TE interrupt of the DBI_INT (0x0120) register.

Step 8

Configure DBI_CTL_1[DBI_soft_trigger] to 1.

Timer Trigger Mode
The software configures timer_en to enable timer counting, and when the counter reaches the
specified value, the DBI_EN automatically will be enabled to start data transmission.
After transmitting a frame of image, the controller will automatically clear the line_cnt, pixel_cnt,
and stop data transmission.
The timer starts counting again. When the counter reaches the specified value, the controller
automatically enables DBI_EN again until the software turns off the timer_en.
The operation process is as follows.
Step 1

Set the SPI_DBI_MODE_SEL (bit3) of SPI_GCR (0x0004) to 1 to select DBI mode.

Step 2

Set the DBI EN MODE SEL (bit30:29) of DBI_CTL_1 (0x0104) to 10 to select the timer
trigger mode.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1443

Confidential
Step 3

Configure the DBI_CTL_0 register (0x0100).
a)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Command Type] (bit31) to 0 to set the writing command.

b)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Write Command Dummy Cycles] (bit[30:20]) to configure the
number of dummy cycles between commands.

c)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Output Data Sequence] (bit19) to select the MSB or LSB.

d)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Transmit Mode] (bit15) to 1 to select the image path.

e)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Output Data Format] (bit[14:12]) to select RGB111/444/565/666/888.

f)

Set DBI_CTL_0[DBI interface Select] (bit[10:8]) to select the DBI interface type.

g)

The remaining values of the DBI_CTL_0 register remain the default value.

Step 4

Set DBI_CTL_1[DCX_DATA] (bit22) to 0 to send the image data.

Step 5

Configure DBI_Video_Size (0x110) to transmit the image size.

Step 6

Configure the related parameter of DBI_Timer (0x10C).

TE Trigger Mode
When the edge changes of the TE are detected (The rising and falling edges are optional), the
DBI_EN can be automatically enabled to start data transmission.
After transmitting a frame of image, the controller will automatically clear the line_cnt, pixel_cnt,
and stop transmitting data.
When the edge changes of the TE are detected (The rising and falling edges are optional), the
DBI_EN can be automatically enabled to restart data transmission until the software shuts down
TE_EN or the screen no longer sends TE signals.
The operation process is as follows.
Step 1

Set the SPI_DBI_MODE_SEL (bit3) of SPI_GCR (0x0004) to 1 to select DBI mode.

Step 2

Set the DBI EN MODE SEL (bit30:29) of DBI_CTL_1 (0x0104) to 11 to select the TE
Configure the DBI_CTL_0 register (0x0100).

Step 3

Set DBI_CTL_0[Command Type] (bit31) to 0 to set the writing command.
a)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Write Command Dummy Cycles] (bit[30:20]) to configure the
number of dummy cycles between commands.

Step 4

b)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Output Data Sequence] (bit19) to select the MSB or LSB.

c)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Transmit Mode] (bit15) to 1 to select the image path.

d)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Output Data Format] (bit[14:12]) to select RGB111/444/565/666/888.

e)

Set DBI_CTL_0[DBI interface Select] (bit[10:8]) to select the DBI interface type.

f)

The remaining values of the DBI_CTL_0 register remain the default value.

Configure DBI_CTL_1[DCX_DATA] (bit22) to 0 to send the image data.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1444

Confidential

18.9.6.4

Step 5

Configure DBI_Video_Size (0x0110) to transmit the image size.

Step 6

Configure DBI_CTL_2 (0x0108) to set the TE-related parameter.

Read Command & Read Data Transfer
Step 1

Set the SPI_DBI_MODE_SEL (bit3) of SPI_GCR (0x0004) to 1 to select DBI mode.

Step 2

Set the DBI EN MODE SEL (bit[30:29]) of DBI_CTL_1 (0x0104) to 0.

Step 3

Configure the DBI_CTL_0 register (0x0100).

Step 4

a)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Command Type] (bit31) to 0 to set the reading command.

b)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Output Data Sequence] (bit19) to select the MSB or LSB.

c)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Transmit Mode] (bit15) to 0 to select the command path.

d)

Set DBI_CTL_0[Output Data Format] (bit[14:12]) to 0.

e)

Set DBI_CTL_0[DBI interface Select] (bit[10:8]) to select the DBI interface type.

f)

The remaining values of the DBI_CTL_0 register remain the default value.

Configure the DBI_CTL_1 register (0x0104).
a)

Configure DBI_CTL_1[DCX_DATA] (bit22) to 0 to send the command.

b)

Configure DBI_CTL_1[Read_MSB_First] (bit20) to select whether the first bit of the
read data is the highest or lowest bit of data.

c)

Configure DBI_CTL_1[Read Data Number of Bytes] to set the byte number to be
read.

d)

Configure DBI_CTL_1[Read Command Dummy Cycles] to set the dummy cycle
between the read command and the read data. When the dummy cycle is complete,
the data starts to be sampled.

Step 5

DMA Path: Configure the SPI_FCR register (0x0018).
a)

Set SPI_FCR[RF_DRQ_EN] (bit8) to 1 to enable RXFIFO DMA.

b)

Set SPI_FCR[RX_TRIG_LEVEL] (bit[7:0]) to 32, which indicates the controller
requests receiving data from DMA if the data of the RX FIFO is greater than 64.

CPU Path: Read data in RX FIFO from the 0x0300 address.

18.9.7

Step 6

Set SPI_GCR[DBI_EN] (bit4) to 1 to start transmitting command.

Step 7

Wait until DBI_INT[RD_DONE_INT] is 1. It indicates that the data is read completely.

18.10 UART
18.10.1 Overview
The universal asynchronous receiver transmitter (UART) provides an asynchronous serial
communication with external devices, modem (data carrier equipment, DCE). It performs
serial-to-parallel conversion on the data received from peripherals and transmits the converted
data to the internal bus. It also performs parallel-to-serial conversion on the data that is
transmitted to peripherals.
The UART has the following features:


Up to 9 UART controllers
-

7 UART controllers in CPUX domain: UART0, UART1, UART2, UART3, UART4, UART5, and
UART6

-

2 UART controllers in CPUS domain: S_UART0 and S_UART1



Compatible with industry-standard 16450/16550 UARTs



Functional Description

18.10.6.1

Serial Data Format

The following figure shows the UART serial data format. The start bit, data bit, parity bit, and stop
bit can be configured.
Figure 18-61 UART Serial Data Format

One Character
One Bit

TX/RX

Start

Data Bits5-8

Parity

Stop

Start bit: It is the start flag of a data frame. In accordance with the UART protocol, the low level of
the TXD signal indicates the start of a data frame. When the UART transmits data, the level needs
to hold high.
Data bit: The data bit width can be configured as 5-bit, 6-bit, 7-bit, and 8-bit based on the
different applications. If the RS-485 mode is enabled, the data bit width is 8-bit.
Parity bit: It is a 1-bit error correction signal. Parity bit includes odd parity, even parity. The UART
can enable and disable the parity bit by setting the UART_LCR register. If RS-485 mode is enabled,
the parity bit must be enabled.
Stop bit: It is the stop bit of a data frame. It can be set to 1-bit, 1.5-bit, and 2-bit by the UART_LCR
register. The high level of the TXD signal indicates the end of a data frame.
18.10.6.2

Baud and Error Rates

The baud rate is calculated as follows: Baud rate = SCLK/(16 * divisor).
The SCLK is usually APB2 or APS2 and can be set in the section CCMU.
The divisor is the frequency divider of UART, which has 16-bit. The low 8-bit is in the UART_DLL
register, and the high 8-bit is in the UART_DLH register.

18.10.6.3

DLAB Definition

The DLAB control bit (UART_LCR[7]) is the access control bit of the divisor Latch low/high
register.
If DLAB is 0, then the 0x00 offset address is the UART_RBR/UART_THR (RX/TX FIFO) register, and
the 0x04 offset address is the UART_IER register.
If DLAB is 1, then the 0x00 offset address is the UART_DLL register, and the 0x04 offset address is
the UART_DLH register.
When the UART initializes, the divisor needs to be set. Write 1 to DLAB to configure UART_DLL
and UART_DLH, and then write 0 to DLAB to configure UART_RBR/UART_THR.
18.10.6.4

CHCFG_AT_BUSY Definition

The function of the CHCFG_AT_BUSY (UART_HALT [1]) and CHANGE_UPDATE (UART_HALT[2])
are as follows.
CHCFG_AT_BUSY: If this bit is enabled and UART is busy, the software can also set the UART
controller, such as the UART_LCR, UART_DLH, UART_DLL register.
CHANGE_UPDATE: If CHCFG_AT_BUSY is enabled, and CHANGE_UPDATE is written to 1, the
configuration of the UART controller can be updated. After the update completes, the bit is
cleared to 0 automatically.
To set the divisor, write 1 to CHCFG_AT_BUSY, and Write 1 to DLAB to configure UART_DLL and
UART_DLH, then Write 1 to CHANGE_UPDATE.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1482

Confidential
18.10.6.5

UART_USR Definition

UART_USR is the BUSY flag, used for indicating the UART controller is busy or not.
When TX is sending data, or RX is receiving data, or TX FIFO/RX FIFO is not null, the UART_USR
will be asserted. It indicates the UART controller is busy.

18.10.7 Programming Guidelines
The following takes the UART module in the CPUX domain as an example.
18.10.7.1

Initialization

Step 1

System Initialization


Configure APB1_CLK_REG in the CCU module to set the APB1 bus clock (The clock is
24MHz by default).



Set UART_BGR_REG[UARTx_GATING] to 1 to enable the module clock, and set
UART_BGR_REG[UARTx_RST] to 1 to de-assert the module.

Step 2

UART Controller Initialization


IO configuration: Configure GPIO multiplex as UART function, and set UART pins to
internal pull-up mode (For detail, see the description in the section GPIO.)



Baud-rate configuration:
-

Set UART baud-rate (refer to the section Baud and Error Rates);

-

Write UART_FCR [FIFOE] to 1 to enable TX/RX FIFO;

-

Write UART_HALT[HALT_TX] to 1 to disable TX transfer;

-

Set UART_LCR[DLAB] to 1, remain default configuration for other bits; set 0x00
offset address to the UART_DLL register, set 0x04 offset address to the
UART_DLH register;

-

Write the high 8-bit of divisor to the UART_DLH register, and write the low 8-bit
of divisor to the UART_DLL register;

-

Set UART_LCR[DLAB] to 0, remain default configuration for other bits; set 0x00
offset address to the UART_RBR/UART_THR register, set 0x04 offset address to
the UART_IER register;

Step 3

Set UART_HALT[HALT_TX] to 0 to enable TX transfer.

Controller Parameter Configuration


Set data width, stop bits, and even/odd parity type by writing the UART_LCR
register.



Reset, enable FIFO and set FIFO trigger condition by writing the UART_FCR register.



Set the flow control parameter by writing the UART_MCR register.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1483

Confidential
Step 4

Interrupt Configuration


Configure UART interrupt vector number to request UART interrupt (Refer to the
section GIC for interrupt vector number).



In DMA mode, write UART_IER to 0 to disable interrupt; write UART_HSK[Handshake
configuration] to 0xE5 to set DMA handshake mode; write UART_FCR[DMAM] to 1 to
set DMA transmission/reception mode; set DMA parameter and request DMA
interrupt according to DMA configuration process.



In Interrupt mode, configure UART_IER to enable the corresponding interrupt
according to requirements: such as transmit (TX) interrupt, receive (RX) interrupt,
receive line status interrupt, RS48 interrupt, etc. (Here TX/RX interrupt is usually
used).

18.10.7.2

Transmission in DMA Mode

Step 1

Initialize UART model. Refer to section 18.10.7.1 Initialization for initialization steps.

Step 2

Configure UART baud rate by setting UART_DLL and UART_DLH.

Step 3

Configure UART data format by setting UART_LCR.

Step 4

Initialize UART FIFO by setting UART_FCR and UART_FCC.

Step 5

Set PTE and DMA_PTE_RX by setting UART_HALT.

Step 6

Configure DMAC for UART.

Step 7

Wait for DMA done by checking DMAC status.

18.10.7.3

Transmission in Interrupt Mode

Step 1

Initialize UART model. Refer to section 18.10.7.1 for initialization steps.

Step 2

Configure UART baud rate by setting UART_DLL and UART_DLH.

Step 3

Configure UART data format by setting UART_LCR.

Step 4

Initialize UART FIFO by setting UART_FCR and UART_FCC.

Step 5

Set DRQ trigger level for DMA by setting UART_TFL and UART_RFL than set PTE and
DMA_PTE_RX in the UART_HALT.

Step 6

Configure UART interrupt by UART_IER and UART_IIR.

Step 7

Wait for UART Interrupt service done.

18.10.7.4

Transmission in RS485 Mode

Step 1

Initialize UART model. Refer to section 18.10.7.1 for initialization steps.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1484

Confidential
Step 2

Configure UART baud rate by setting UART_DLL and UART_DLH.

Step 3

Configure UART data format by setting UART_LCR.

Step 4

Initialize UART FIFO by setting UART_FCR and UART_FCC.

Step 5

Configure UART Mode by setting UART_MCR [7:6].

Step 6

Configure UART RS485 Receive data format by setting UART_485_CTL [1:0].

Step 7

Configure UART RS485 Address Match Register by setting UART_RS485_ADDR_MATCH if
chose AAD Receive data mode.

Step 8

IF DMA mode is selected, perform steps 5-7 for DMA mode. If not, perform steps 5-7 for
CPU mode.

18.10.7.5

FIFO Test Mode

Step 1

Configure FIFO test mode by setting FIFO_TM.

Step 2

Write data to the txfifo by write UART_THR and read data from the txfifo by read
READ_TX_FIFO.

Step 3

Write data to the rxfifo by write WRITE_RX_FIFO and read data from the rxfifo by read
READ_RX_FIFO.

Description
RBR
Receiver Buffer Register
Data byte received on the serial input port (sin) in
UART mode, or the serial infrared input (sir_in) in
infrared mode. The data in this register is valid only
if the Data Ready (DR) bit in the Line Status Register

8:0

R

0x0

(LCR) is set.
If in FIFO mode and FIFOs are enabled (FCR[0] set to
one), this register accesses the head of the receive
FIFO. If the receive FIFO is full and this register is not
read before the next data character arrives, then the
data already in the FIFO is preserved, but any
incoming data are lost and an overrun error occurs.

DLL
Divisor Latch Low
Lower 8 bits of a 16-bit, read/write, Divisor Latch
register that contains the baud rate divisor for the
UART. This register may only be accessed when the

7:0

R/W

0x0

(sclk) frequency divided by sixteen times the value

serial communications occur. Also, once the DLL is
set, at least 8 clock cycles of the slowest UART clock
should be allowed to pass before transmitting or
receiving data.

In this mode, when PTE is high and TX FIFO is enable,

Confidential
Offset: 0x0014
Bit

Read/Write

Register Name: UART_LSR
Default/Hex

Description
THRE
TX Holding Register Empty
If the FIFOs are disabled, this bit is set to "1"
whenever the TX Holding Register is empty and

5

R

0x1

ready to accept new data and it is cleared when the
CPU writes to the TX Holding Register.
If the FIFOs are enabled, this bit is set to "1"

when at least one byte is written to the TX FIFO.
BI
Break Interrupt
This is used to indicate the detection of a break
sequence on the serial input data.
If in UART mode (SIR_MODE == Disabled), it is set
whenever the serial input, sir_in, is held in a logic '0'
state for longer than the sum of start time + data bits
+ parity + stop bits.
If in infrared mode (SIR_MODE == Enabled), it is set
whenever the serial input, sir_in, is continuously

4

R

0x0

pulsed to logic '0' for longer than the sum of start

time + data bits + parity + stop bits. A break
condition on serial input causes one and only one
character, consisting of all zeros, to be received by
the UART.
In the FIFO mode, the character associated with the
break condition is carried through the FIFO and is
revealed when the character is at the top of the FIFO.
Reading the LSR clears the BI bit. In the non-FIFO
mode, the BI indication occurs immediately and
persists until the LSR is read.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1499

Confidential
Offset: 0x0014
Bit

Read/Write

Register Name: UART_LSR
Default/Hex

Description
FE
Framing Error
This is used to indicate the occurrence of a framing
error in the receiver. A framing error occurs when the
receiver does not detect a valid
STOP bit in the received data.
In the FIFO mode, since the framing error is
associated with a character received, it is revealed
when the character with the framing error is at the

3

RC

0x0

top of the FIFO. When a framing error occurs, the
UART tries to resynchronize. It does this by assuming
that the error was due to the start bit of the next
character and then continues receiving the other bit
i.e. data, and/or parity and stop. It should be noted
that the Framing Error (FE) bit (LSR[3]) is set if a
break interrupt has occurred, as indicated by Break
Interrupt (BI) bit (LSR[4]).
0: No framing error
1: Framing error
Reading the LSR clears the FE bit.
PE
Parity Error
This is used to indicate the occurrence of a parity
error in the receiver if the Parity Enable (PEN) bit
(LCR[3]) is set. In the FIFO mode, since the parity
error is associated with a character received, it is

2

RC

0x0

revealed when the character with the parity error
arrives at the top of the FIFO. It should be noted that
the Parity Error (PE) bit (LSR[2]) is set if a break
interrupt has occurred, as indicated by Break
Interrupt (BI) bit (LSR[4]).
0: No parity error
1: Parity error
Reading the LSR clears the PE bit.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Description
OE
Overrun Error
This occurs if a new data character was received
before the previous data was read. In the non-FIFO
mode, the OE bit is set when a new character arrives
in the receiver before the previous character was
read from the RBR. When this happens, the data in

1

RC

0x0

the RBR is overwritten. In the FIFO mode, an overrun
error occurs when the FIFO is full and a new
character arrives at the receiver. The data in the FIFO
is retained and the data in the receive shift register is
lost.
0: No overrun error
1: Overrun error
Reading the LSR clears the OE bit.

0

0x0

1: Data ready
This bit is cleared when the RBR is read in non-FIFO
mode, or when the receiver FIFO is empty, in FIFO

18.11 Two Wire Interface (TWI)
18.11.1 Overview
This Two Wire Interface (TWI) Controller is used to connect SoC on the 2-wire bus. It supports all
the standard 2-wire bus transfer. Master mode and Slave mode are all supported. The TWI has
the following features:


Up to 16 TWI controllers
-

13 TWI controllers in CPUX domain: TWI0-12

-

3 TWI controllers in CPUS domain: S_TWI0-2



Compliant with I2C bus standard



Supports master mode or slave mode



Supports 7-bit standard address and 10-bit extended address.



Supports standard mode (100 Kbit/s) and high-speed mode (400 Kbit/s).



Supports general call and start byte.



Master mode features:



-

Supports the bus arbitration in the case of multiple master devices.

-

Supports clock synchronization and bit and byte waiting.

-

Supports packet transmission and DMA

-

Supports DVFS request adjust voltage

Salve mode features:
-

Interrupt on address detection

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1513

Confidential

in SEND_FIFO

The controller includes TWI engine and TWI driver. Each time the TWI engine sends a START
signal, a STOP signal, or a BYTE data, or a corresponding ACK, the TWI engine will generate an
interrupt, and wait for the CPU to process and clear the interrupt before the next START, STOP,
or BYTE, ACK transmission can be performed. Therefore, when a device communication is
completed, many interrupts will be generated, and the CPU needs to wait for the previous
interrupt before it can configure the next one. The TWI driver defines each communication with
the device as a packet transmission. The CPU can directly configure the slave address, register
address and data transmission for one or more package transmissions without waiting for
interruption, then start the TWI driver, and the TWI driver can control the TWI engine to complete
a pre-configured communication, and report an interrupt to the CPU after completion.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

18.11.5 Functional Description
18.11.5.1

TWI Engine Master and Slave Mode in TWI Engine

There are four operation modes on the TWI bus which dictates the communications method.
They are Master Transmit, Master Receive, Slave Transmit and Slave Receive. In general, CPU
host controls TWI Engine by writing commands and data to its registers. TWI Engine transmits an
interrupt to CPU when each time a byte transfer is done or a START/STOP conditions is detected.
The CPU host can also poll the status register for current status if the interrupt mechanism is not
disabled by the CPU host.
When the CPU host wants to start a bus transfer, it initiates a bus START to enter the master
mode by setting IM_STA bit in the 2WIRE_CNTR register to high (before it must be low). The TWI
Engine will assert INT line and INT_FLAG to indicate a completion for the START condition and
each consequent byte transfer. At each interrupt, the micro-processor needs to check the
2WIRE_STAT register for current status. A transfer has to be concluded with STOP condition by
setting M_STP bit high.
In Slave Mode, the TWI Engine also constantly samples the bus and looks for its own slave
address during addressing cycles. Once a match is found, it is addressed and interrupt the CPU
host with the corresponding status. Upon request, the CPU host should read the status,
read/write 2WIRE_DATA data register, and set the 2WIRE_CNTR control register. After each byte
transfers, a slave device always halts the operation of remote master by holding the next low
pulse on SCL line until the microprocessor responds to the status of previous byte transfer or
START condition.

18.11.5.3

TWI DVFS

In the master mode, the TWI supports dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) request for
8 set of peripherals. Each peripheral has independent interface for communication, which is
completed based on the REQ and ACK handshake signals.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1519

Confidential
When the peripheral sends the REQ request (REQ=1), TWI will respond to it and transfer the data
sent by the peripheral to PMU. After a voltage adjustment finishes, an ACK signal (ACK=1) is sent
back. After receiving the high active ACK signal, the peripheral will dis-assert the REQ (REQ=0).
Then a voltage adjustment ends.
The primary arbitration is used for arbitrating the REQs simultaneously initiated by multiple
peripherals, which can be configured as the poll mode or priority mode.
The secondary arbitration is used for arbitrating the CPU and DVFS device control over the TWI
driver, which can be configured as the poll mode.
The read-back function supports configuring whether to read back the transferred data for
double check.
The mask function supports configuring the mask bit transferred to PMU. First, initiate the read
operation to read back the data, and then mask the corresponding data bit. At last, send out the
new data.

18.11.6 Programming Guidelines
The TWI controller operates in an 8-bit data format. The data on the TWI_SDA line is always 8 bits
long. At first, the TWI controller sends a start condition. When in the addressing formats of 7-bit,
the TWI sends out an 8-bit message which includes 7 MSB slave address and 1 LSB read/write
flag. The least significant of the salve address indicates the direction of transmission. When the
TWI works in 10-bit slave address mode, the operation will be divided into two steps, for details
on the operation, refer to TWI_ADDR and TWI_XADDR.
The following takes the TWI module in the CPUX domain as an example.
18.11.6.1

TWI Engine Initialization

Follow the steps below to initialize the TWI engine.
Step 1

Configure the corresponding GPIO multiplex function as TWI mode.

Step 2

For TWIn, set TWI_BGR_REG [TWIn_GATING] in CCU module to 0 to close TWIn clock.

Step 3

For TWIn, set TWI_BGR_REG [TWIn_RST] in CCU module to 0, then set to 1 to reset TWIn.

Step 4

For TWIn, set TWI_BGR_REG [TWIn_GATING] in CCU module to 1 to open TWIn clock.

Step 5

Configure TWI_CCR[CLK_M] and TWI_CCR[CLK_N] to get the needed rate (The clock
source of TWI is from APB1).

Step 6

Configure TWI_CNTR [BUS_EN] and TWI_CNTR [A_ACK]. When using interrupt mode, set
TWI_CNTR [INT_EN] to 1, and register the system interrupt through GIC module. In slave
mode, configure TWI_ADDR and TWI_XADDR registers to finish TWI initialization
configuration.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1520

Confidential
18.11.6.2

Writing Data Operation in TWI Engine

Follow the steps below to write data to the device.
Step 1

Clear TWI_EFR register, and configure TWI_CNTR [M_STA] to 1 to transmit the START
signal.

Step 2

After the START signal is transmitted, the first interrupt is triggered, then write device ID
to TWI_DATA (For a 10-bit device ID, firstly write the first byte ID, secondly write the
second byte ID in the next interrupt).

Step 3

The Interrupt is triggered again after device ID transmission completes, write device
data address to be read to TWI_DATA (For a 16-bit address, firstly write the first-byte
address, secondly write the second-byte address).

Step 4

Interrupt is triggered after data address transmission completes, write data to be
transmitted to TWI_DATA (For consecutive write data operation, every byte
transmission completion triggers interrupt, during interrupt write the next byte data to
TWI_DATA).

Step 5

After transmission completes, write TWI_CNTR [M_STP] to 1 to transmit the STOP signal
and end this write-operation.

18.11.6.3

Reading Data Operation in TWI Engine

Follow the steps below to read data from the device.
Step 1

Clear TWI_EFR register, and set TWI_CNTR [A_ACK] to 1, and configure TWI_CNTR
[M_STA] to 1 to transmit the START signal.

Step 2

After the START signal is transmitted, the first interrupt is triggered, then write device ID
to TWI_DATA (For a 10-bit device ID, firstly write the first-byte ID, secondly write the
second-byte ID in the next interrupt).

Step 3

The Interrupt is triggered again after device ID transmission completes, write device
data address to be read to TWI_DATA (For a 16-bit address, firstly write the first-byte
address, secondly write the second-byte address).

Step 4

The Interrupt is triggered after data address transmission completes, write TWI_CNTR
[M_STA] to 1 to transmit new START signal, and after interrupt triggers, write device ID
to TWI_DATA to start read-operation.

Step 5

After device address transmission completes, each receive completion will trigger an
interrupt, in turn, read TWI_DATA to get data. When receiving the previous interrupt of
the last byte data, clear [A_ACK] to stop acknowledge signal of the last byte.

Step 6

Write TWI_CNTR [M_STP] to 1 to transmit the STOP signal and end this read-operation.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1521

Confidential
18.11.6.4

TWI Driver Initialization

Follow the steps below to initialize the TWI driver.
Step 1

Configure corresponding GPIO multiplex function as TWI mode.

Step 2

For TWIn, set TWI_BGR_REG [TWIn_GATING] in CCU module to 0 to close TWIn clock.

Step 3

For TWIn, set TWI_BGR_REG [TWIn_RST] in CCU module to 0, then set to 1 to reset TWIn.

Step 4

For TWIn, set TWI_BGR_REG [TWIn_GATING] in CCU module to 1 to open TWIn clock.

Step 5

Set TWI_DRV_CTRL [TWI_DRV_EN] to 1 to enable the TWI driver.

Step 6

Configure TWI_DRV_BUS_CTRL [CLK_M] and TWI_DRV_BUS_CTRL [CLK_N] to get the
needed rate (The clock source of TWI is from APB1).

Step 7

Set TWI_DRV_CTRL [RESTART_MODE] to 0 and [READ_TRAN_MODE] to 1, and set
TWI_DRV_INT_CTRL [TRAN_COM_INT_EN] to 1.

Step 8

When using DMA for data transmission, set TWI_DRV_DMA_CFG [DMA_RX_EN] and
TWI_DRV_DMA_CFG [DMA_TX_EN] to 1, and configure TWI_DRV_DMA_CFG [RX_TRIG]
and TWI_DRV_DMA_CFG [TX_TRIG] to set the thresholds of RXFIFO and TXFIFO.

To use the DVFS functions, follow the steps below.
Step 1

Configure ADDR_PMU, MASK_EN, and MASK (if needed) of each DVFS device in the
TWI_PMU_Dn_CONFIG.

Step 2

Configure the request priority of each DVFS device in the TWI_PMU_ARBITER.

Step 3

Configure the PKT_INTERVAL_PMU, channel enable, readback enable (if needed) in the
TWI_PMU_CTL.

Step 4
18.11.6.5

Set 1 to RR8_Un_ENABLE enable RR8_Un in the TWI_RR8_CTL.

Writing Packet Transmission for TWI Driver

Follow the steps below to write package to the device.
Step 1

Configure TWI_DRV_SLV [SLV_ID] to set the device ID, and configure TWI_DRV_SLV [CMD]
to 0 to set the write operation.

Step 2

Configure TWI_DRV_FMT [ADDR_BYTE] according to the address width of the device
register, and TWI_DRV_FMT [DATA_BYTE] according to the written data count in a
packet.

Step 3

Configure TWI_DRV_CFG [PACKET_CNT] to set the written packet number.

Step 4

Configure DMA channel, including TWI TXFIFO, device register address, and the written
data.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1522

Confidential
Step 5

Set [START_TRAN] to 1 to start TWI Driver transmission.

Step 6

When TWI driver transmission completes, the interrupt is triggered, it indicates that the
write packet transmission ends.

18.11.6.6

Reading Packet Transmission for TWI Driver

Step 1

To read package from the device, perform the following steps:

Step 2

Configure TWI_DRV_SLV [SLV_ID] to set the device ID, and configure TWI_DRV_SLV [CMD]
to 1 to set the read operation.

Step 3

Configure TWI_DRV_FMT [ADDR_BYTE] according to the address width of the device
register, and TWI_DRV_FMT [DATA_BYTE] according to the read data count in a packet.

Step 4

Configure TWI_DRV_CFG [PACKET_CNT] to set the read packet number.

Step 5

Configure DMA channel, including TWI TXFIFO, TWI RXFIFO, device register address and
the read data.

Step 6

Set [START_TRAN] to 1 to start TWI Driver transmission.

Step 7

When TWI driver transmission completes, the interrupt is triggered, it indicates that the
read packet transmission ends.

18.11.6.7

Slave Mode Configuration

Step 1

Enable A_ACK, BUS_EN, and INT_EN in the TWI_CNTR.

Step 2

Set the TWI_ADDR and TWI_XADDR based on the device address bit width.

0x0000 TWI0 Slave Address Register (Default Value: 0x0000_0000)

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1525

Confidential
For 7-bit addressing:
SLA6 – SLA0 is the 7-bit address of the TWI when is in slave mode. When the TWI receives this
address after a START condition, it will generate an interrupt and enter slave mode. (SLA6
corresponds to the first bit received from the TWI bus.) If GCE is set to ‘1’, the TWI will also
recognize the general call address (00h).
For 10-bit addressing:
When the address received starts with 11110b, the TWI recognizes this as the first part of a 10-bit
address and if the next two bits match ADDR[2:1] (i.e. SLAX9 and SLAX8 of the device’s extended
address), it sends an ACK. (The device does not generate an interrupt at this point.) If the next
byte of the address matches the XADDR register (SLAX7 – SLAX0), the TWI generates an interrupt
and goes into slave mode.

Bit

Register Name: TWI_CNTR
Default/Hex

Description
BUS_EN
TWI Bus Enable
0: The TWI bus inputs ISDA/ISCL are ignored and the
TWI Controller will not respond to any address on the

6

R/W

0x0

bus.
1: The TWI will respond to calls to its slave address ‒
and to the general call address if the GCE bit in the
ADDR register is set.
Notes: In master operation mode, this bit should be
set to ‘1’.
M_STA
Master Mode Start
When M_STA is set to ‘1’, TWI Controller will enter
master mode and transmit a START condition on the
bus when the bus is free. If the M_STA bit is set to
‘1’ when the TWI Controller is already in master
mode and one or more bytes have been transmitted,

5

R/WAC

0x0

then a repeated START condition will be sent. If the
M_STA bit is set to ‘1’ when the TWI is being
accessed in slave mode, the TWI will complete the
data transfer in slave mode then enter master mode
when the bus has been released.
The M_STA bit is cleared automatically after a START
condition has been sent: writing ‘0’ to this bit has
no effect.
M_STP
Master Mode Stop
If M_STP is set to ‘1’ in master mode, a STOP
condition is transmitted on the TWI bus. If the M_STP
bit is set to ‘1’ in slave mode, the TWI will behave

4

R/WAC

0x0

as if a STOP condition has been received, but no
STOP condition will be transmitted on the TWI bus. If
both M_STA and M_STP bits are set, the TWI will first
transmit the STOP condition (if in master mode) then
transmit the START condition.
The M_STP bit is cleared automatically: writing a
‘0’ to this bit has no effect.

Interrupt Flag
INT_FLAG is automatically set to ‘1’ when any of 28

3

INT_FLAG is state F8h. If the INT_EN bit is set, the

the TWI is operating in slave mode, data transfer is
suspended when INT_FLAG is set and the low period
of the TWI bus clock line (SCL) is stretched until ‘1’

released and the interrupt line goes low.
A_ACK
Assert Acknowledge
When A_ACK is set to ‘1’, an Acknowledge (low
level on SDA) will be sent during the acknowledge
clock pulse on the TWI bus if:
1. Either the whole of a matching 7-bit slave address
or the first or the second byte of a matching 10-bit
slave address has been received.
2. The general call address has been received and the
GCE bit in the ADDR register is set to ‘1’.

0x0

mode.
When A_ACK is ‘0’, a Not Acknowledge (high level
on SDA) will be sent when a data byte is received in
master or slave mode.
If A_ACK is cleared to ‘0’ in slave transmitter mode,
the byte in the DATA register is assumed to be the
‘last byte’. After this byte has been transmitted,
the TWI will enter state C8h then return to the idle
state (status code F8h) when INT_FLAG is cleared.
The TWI will not respond as a slave unless A_ACK is
set.

18.11.10 S_TWI0 Register Description
18.11.10.1

0x0000 S_TWI0 Slave Address Register (Default Value: 0x0000_0000)

Offset: 0x0000

Register Name: TWI_ADDR

Bit

Read/Write

Default/Hex

Description

31:8

/

/

/
SLA
Slave address
7-bit addressing

7:1

R/W

0x0

SLA6, SLA5, SLA4, SLA3, SLA2, SLA1, SLA0
10-bit addressing
1, 1, 1, 1, 0, SLAX[9:8]
GCE

0

R/W

0x0

General call address enable
0: Disable
1: Enable

Notes:
For 7-bit addressing:
SLA6 – SLA0 is the 7-bit address of the TWI when in slave mode. When the TWI receives this
address after a START condition, it will generate an interrupt and enter slave mode. (SLA6
corresponds to the first bit received from the TWI bus.) If GCE is set to ‘1’, the TWI will also
recognize the general call address (00h).
For 10-bit addressing:
When the address received starts with 11110b, the TWI recognizes this as the first part of a 10-bit
address and if the next two bits match ADDR[2:1] (i.e. SLAX9 and SLAX8 of the device’s extended
address), it sends an ACK. (The device does not generate an interrupt at this point.) If the next
byte of the address matches the XADDR register (SLAX7 – SLAX0), the TWI generates an interrupt
and goes into slave mode.
