1540

Confidential
Offset: 0x000C
Bit

Read/Write

Register Name: TWI_CNTR
Default/Hex

Description
M_STA
Master Mode Start
When M_STA is set to ‘1’, TWI Controller enters
master mode and will transmit a START condition on
the bus when the bus is free. If the M_STA bit is set to
‘1’ when the TWI Controller is already in master
mode and one or more bytes have been transmitted,

5

R/WAC

0x0

then a repeated START condition will be sent. If the
M_STA bit is set to ‘1’ when the TWI is being
accessed in slave mode, the TWI will complete the
data transfer in slave mode then enter master mode
when the bus has been released.
The M_STA bit is cleared automatically after a START
condition has been sent: writing a ‘0’ to this bit has
no effect.
M_STP
Master Mode Stop
If M_STP is set to ‘1’ in master mode, a STOP
condition is transmitted on the TWI bus. If the M_STP
bit is set to ‘1’ in slave mode, the TWI will behave
as if a STOP condition has been received, but no

4

R/WAC

0x0

STOP condition will be transmitted on the TWI bus. If
both M_STA and M_STP bits are set, the TWI will first
transmit the STOP condition (if in master mode) then
transmit the START condition.
The M_STP bit is cleared automatically: writing a
‘0’ to this bit has no effect.
INT_FLAG
Interrupt Flag
INT_FLAG is automatically set to ‘1’ when any of 28
(out of the possible 29) states is entered (see ‘STAT
Register’ below). The only state that does not set

3

R/W1C

0x0

INT_FLAG is state F8h. If the INT_EN bit is set, the
interrupt line goes high when IFLG is set to ‘1’. If
the TWI is operating in slave mode, data transfer is
suspended when INT_FLAG is set and the low period
of the TWI bus clock line (SCL) is stretched until ‘1’
is written to INT_FLAG. The TWI clock line is then
released and the interrupt line goes low.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1541

Confidential
Offset: 0x000C
Bit

Read/Write

Register Name: TWI_CNTR
Default/Hex

Description
A_ACK
Assert Acknowledge
When A_ACK is set to ‘1’, an Acknowledge (low
level on SDA) will be sent during the acknowledge
clock pulse on the TWI bus if:
1. Either the whole of a matching 7-bit slave address
or the first or the second byte of a matching 10-bit
slave address has been received.
2. The general call address has been received and the
GCE bit in the ADDR register is set to ‘1’.

2

R/W

0x0

3. A data byte has been received in master or slave
mode.
When A_ACK is ‘0’, a Not Acknowledge (high level
on SDA) will be sent when a data byte is received in
master or slave mode.
If A_ACK is cleared to ‘0’ in slave transmitter mode,
the byte in the DATA register is assumed to be the
‘last byte’. After this byte has been transmitted,
the TWI will enter state C8h then return to the idle
state (status code F8h) when INT_FLAG is cleared.
The TWI will not respond as a slave unless A_ACK is
set.

1

1: scl clock high period count on iscl

Description
CLK_N
Clock N setting
The TWI bus is sampled by the TWI at the frequency
defined by F0:
Fsamp = F 0 = Fin / 2^CLK_N
The TWI OSCL output frequency, in master mode, is
F1 / 10:
F1 = F0 / (CLK_M + 1)
Foscl = F1 / 10 = Fin / (2^CLK_N * (CLK_M + 1)*10)

2:0

R/W

0x0

CLK_DUTY=40% due to the delay of SCL sample
debounce.
For Example:
Fin = 24Mhz (APB clock input)

F0 = 24M/2^1=12Mhz, F1= F0/(10*(2+1)) = 0.4Mhz
For 100Khz standard speed 2Wire, CLK_N=1,
CLK_M=11
F0=24M/2^1=12Mhz, F1=F0/(10*(11+1)) = 0.1Mhz

18.12 General Purpose ADC (GPADC)
18.12.1 Overview
The General Purpose ADC (GPADC) can convert the external signal into a certain proportion of
digital value, to realize the measurement of analog signal, which can be applied to power
detection and key detection.
The GPADC has the following features:


12-bit successive-approximation register ADC (SAR ADC) with 7 pads
-

4 for boot detection

-

3for analog voltage input detection



64 FIFO depth of data register



12-bit sampling resolution



Up to 1 MHz sampling frequency



Input voltage: 0 V to 1.8 V



Three operation modes: single conversion mode, continuous conversion mode, and burst
conversion mode

18.12.5 Functional Description
18.12.5.1


Operation Mode
Single conversion mode

The GPADC samples and converts once in a specified channel, and then the converted data is
updated at the data registers of the corresponding channels.


Continuous conversion mode

The GPADC keeps sampling and converting in a specified channel until the ADC is disabled, and
then the converted data is updated at the data registers of the corresponding channels.


Burst conversion mode

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1565

Confidential
The GPADC keeps sampling and converting in a specified channel until the ADC is disabled, and
then the converted data is sequentially stored at the FIFO.
18.12.5.2

Clock and Timing Requirements

CLK_IN = 24 MHz
CONV_TIME (Conversion Time) = 1/(24MHz/13Cycles) =0.542 (us)
TACQ (ADC acquiring time) > 10RC (R is output resistor of ADC sample circuit, C = 6.4 pF)
ADC Sample Frequency > TACQ+CONV_TIME+3
Figure 18-70 GPADC Timing Requirement
TACQ

CONV_TIME

ADC Sample Rate

18.12.6 Programming Guidelines
18.12.6.1

Initialization

The GPADC initial process is as follows.
Figure 18-71 GPADC Initial Process
Start

Set GPADC GATING,RESET(in CCU)

Set TACQ,FS_DIV,Work Mode,
Compare Data,Interrupt Enable

Enable GPADC

Query Mode
Take channel0 for example:
Step 1

Write 0x1 to the bit [16] of GPADC0_BGR_REG to de-assert reset.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1566

Confidential
Step 2

Write 0x1 to the bit [0] of GPADC0_BGR_REG to enable the GPADC clock.

Step 3

Write 0x2F to the bit [15:0] of GP_SR_CON to set the acquiring time of ADC.

Step 4

Write 0x1DF to the bit [31:16] of GP_SR_CON to set the ADC sample frequency divider.

Step 5

Write 0x2 to the bit [19:18] of GP_CTRL to set the continuous conversion mode.

Step 6

(Optional) If you need to configure the sampling frequency for each channel, follow
these steps:
a)

Configure GP_SMP_TMS (offset: 0x00C0) register to set GP_SMP_TMS value. The
initial sampling frequency set in step4 is multiplied by this value to get the actual
sampling frequency. For detailed configuration information, please refer to the
section Sampling Frequency.

b)

Configure the GP_CH_SMP_BYP bit (bit {0}) of GP_SMP_BYP (offset: 0x00D0) register
as 0.

Step 7

Write 0x1 to the bit [0] of GP_CS_EN to enable the analog input channel.

Step 8

Write 0x1 to the bit [16] of GP_CTRL to enable the ADC function.

Step 9

Read the bit [0] of GP_DATA_INTS. If the bit is 1, then data conversion is complete.

Step 10 Read the bit [11:0] of GP_CH0_DATA, and calculate voltage value based on GPADC
formula.
Interrupt Mode
Take channel0 for example:
Step 1

Write 0x1 to the bit [16] of GPADC0_BGR_REG to de-assert reset.

Step 2

Write 0x1 to the bit [0] of GPADC0_BGR_REG to enable the GPADC clock.

Step 3

Write 0x2F to the bit [15:0] of GP_SR_CON to set the acquiring time of ADC.

Step 4

Write 0x1DF to the bit [31:16] of GP_SR_CON to set the ADC sample frequency divider.

Step 5

Write 0x2 to the bit [19:18] of GP_CTRL to set the continuous conversion mode.

Step 6

(Optional) If you need to configure the sampling frequency for each channel, follow
these steps:
a)

Configure GP_SMP_TMS (offset: 0x00C0) register to set GP_SMP_TMS value. The
initial sampling frequency set in step4 is multiplied by this value to get the actual
sampling frequency. For detailed configuration information, please refer to section
Sampling Frequency.

b)

Configure the GP_CH_SMP_BYP bit (bit {0}) of GP_SMP_BYP (offset: 0x00D0) register
as 0. Write 0x1 to the bit [0] of GP_CS_EN to enable the analog input channel.

Step 7

Write 0x1 to the bit [0] of GP_DATA_INTC to enable the GPADC data interrupt.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1567

Confidential
Step 8

Set the GIC module based on the IRQ 93.

Step 9

Put interrupt handler address into interrupt vector table based on the IRQ 93.

Step 10 Write 0x1 to the bit16 of GP_CTRL to enable the ADC function.
Step 11 Read the bit [11:0] of GP_CH0_DATA from the interrupt handler, calculate voltage value
based on GPADC formula.
18.12.6.2

Sampling Frequency Configuration

The sampling frequency is only configurable in continue conversion mode. The sampling
frequency for each channel can be configured as a multiple of 32 kHz and the total sampling
frequency of all channels should be less than or equal to 1 MHz.
The sampling frequency configuration steps are as follows.
Step 1

After setting GP_SMP_TMS0/1/2/3 and GP_SMP_BYP as 0, configure the ADC_EN bit (bit
[16]) of GP_CTRL (offset: 0x0004) register to disable ADC function.

Step 2

Configure the FS_DIV bit (bit [31:16]) of GP_SR_CON (offset: 0x0000) register to set the
initial sampling frequency of each channel.

Step 3

Configure GP_SMP_TMS (offset: 0x00C0) register to set GP_SMP_TMS value. The initial
sampling frequency is multiplied by this value to get the actual sampling frequency.
NOTE

All GPADC channels should be configured simultaneously.
The following are the all available sampling frequencies for each channel and corresponding
GP_SMP_TMS values.

18.13 Low Rate ADC (LRADC)
18.13.1 Overview
The low rate analog-to-digital converter (LRADC) can convert the external signal into a certain
proportion of digital value, to realize the measurement of analog signal, which can be applied to
power detection and key detection.
The LRADC has the following features:


6-bit sampling resolution



Up to 2 KHz sampling frequency



Input voltage: 0 V to 1.35 V; power supply voltage:1.8V



Supports hold key and general key



Supports interrupt control



Three operation modes: single mode, continuous mode, and normal mode

18.13.2 Block Diagram
The following figure shows the block diagram of the LRADC.
Figure 18-72 LRADC Block Diagram

Table 18-29 LRADC External Signals

18.13.5 Functional Description
18.13.5.1


Operation Mode
Normal Mode

The LRADC gathers and averages 8 samples to obtain a data, then updates it to the data register
and asserts a data interrupt flag. Sampling is repeated in this manner until the LRADC is disabled.


Continuous Mode

The LRADC gathers and averages 8 samples every 8*(N+1) sample cycle, then updates it to the
data register and asserts a data interrupt flag. (N is defined in the bit [19:16] of LRADC_CTRL).


Single Mode

The LRADC gathers and averages 8 samples to obtain a data, then updates it to the data register
and asserts a data interrupt flag. Then, the LRADC stops sampling.
18.13.5.2

Interrupt Control

Each LRADC channel has five interrupt sources and five interrupt enable controls.
Figure 18-73 LRADC Interrupt
DATA_IRQ_EN
DATA_IRQ
KEYDOWN_IRQ_EN
KEYDOWN_IRQ
KEYUP_IRQ_EN
KEYUP_IRQ

LRADC_IRQ

HOLDKEY_IRQ_EN
HOLDKEY_IRQ
ALREADYHOLDKEY_IRQ_EN
ALREADYHOLDKEY_IRQ

When the input voltage is between LEVEL A (1.35 V) and LEVEL B (control by the bit [5:4] of
LRADC_CTRL), the IRQ1 will be generated. When the input voltage is lower than LEVEL B, the
IRQ2 will be generated.
If the controller receives IRQ1 but does not receive IRQ2 in a certain time, the controller will
generate Hold Key Pending, or Data IRQ Pending.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1592

Confidential
The Hold KEY is usually used for the self-locking key. When the self-locking key stays in the
locked status, the controller receives the IRQ2, then the controller will generate Already Hold
Pending.

18.13.6 Programming Guidelines
18.13.6.1

Initialization
Start

Set sample rate, channel, LEVELB,
LEVELA_B_CNT, and work mo de, and
enable interrupts

Enable LRADC

18.13.6.2

Normal Mode

Perform the following steps for normal mode:
Step 1

Configure LRADC_BGR_REG [LRADC_GATING] to 0 to disable the clock of LRADC.

Step 2

Configure LRADC_BGR_REG [LRADC_RST] to 1 to de-assert the reset of LRADC.

Step 3

Configure LRADC_BGR_REG [LRADC_GATING] to 1 to enable the clock of LRADC.

Step 4

Configure LRADC_CTRL[LRADC_SAMPLE_RATE] to set the appropriate sampling
frequency.

Step 5

Configure LRADC_CTRL[LEVELB_VOL] to set the appropriate voltage threshold.

Step 6

Configure LRADC_CTRL[FIRST_CONVER_DLY] and LRADC_CTRL[LEVELA_B_CNT] to set
the appropriate debounce value.

Step 7

Configure LRADC_CTRL[LRADC_HOLD_KEY_EN] to 1.

Step 8

Configure LRADC_CTRL[KEY_MODE_SELECT] to 0 to set the normal mode.

Step 9

Configure LRADC_INTC to enable the corresponding interrupt.

Step 10 Configure LRADC_CTRL[LRADC_HOLD_KEY_EN] to 1.
Step 11 Read the corresponding key voltage value from LRADC_DATA when the CPU receives the
LRADC interrupt.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1593

Confidential
18.13.6.3

Single Mode

Perform the following steps for the single mode:
Step 1

ConfigureLRADC_BGR_REG [LRADC_GATING] to 0 to disable the clock of LRADC.

Step 2

ConfigureLRADC_BGR_REG [LRADC_RST] to 1 to de-assert the reset of LRADC.

Step 3

ConfigureLRADC_BGR_REG [LRADC_GATING] to 1 to enable the clock of LRADC.

Step 4

Configure LRADC_CTRL[LRADC_SAMPLE_RATE] to set the appropriate sampling
frequency.

Step 5

Configure LRADC_CTRL[LEVELB_VOL] to set the appropriate voltage threshold.

Step 6

Configure LRADC_CTRL[FIRST_CONVER_DLY] and LRADC_CTRL[LEVELA_B_CNT] to set
the appropriate debounce value.

Step 7

Configure LRADC_CTRL[LRADC_HOLD_KEY_EN] to 1.

Step 8

Configure LRADC_CTRL[KEY_MODE_SELECT] to 1 to set the single mode.

Step 9

Configure LRADC_INTC to enable the corresponding interrupt.

Step 10 Configure LRADC_CTRL[LRADC_HOLD_KEY_EN] to 1.
Step 11 Read the corresponding key voltage value from LRADC_DATA when the CPU receives the
LRADC interrupt.
18.13.6.4

Continuous Mode

Perform the following steps for continuous mode:
Step 1

Configure LRADC_BGR_REG [LRADC_GATING] to 0 to disable the clock of LRADC.

Step 2

ConfigureLRADC_BGR_REG [LRADC_RST] to 1 to de-assert the reset of LRADC.

Step 3

Configure LRADC_BGR_REG [LRADC_GATING] to 1 to enable the clock of LRADC.

Step 4

Configure LRADC_CTRL[LRADC_SAMPLE_RATE] to set the appropriate sampling
frequency.

Step 5

Configure LRADC_CTRL[LEVELB_VOL] to set the appropriate voltage threshold.

Step 6

Configure LRADC_CTRL[FIRST_CONVER_DLY] and LRADC_CTRL[LEVELA_B_CNT] to set
the appropriate debounce value.

Step 7

Configure LRADC_CTRL[LRADC_HOLD_KEY_EN] to 1.

Step 8

Configure LRADC_CTRL[KEY_MODE_SELECT] to 2 to set the continuous mode, and
configure LRADC_CTRL[CONTINUE_TIME_SELECT] to set a sampling interval.

Step 9

Configure LRADC_INTC to enable the corresponding interrupt.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

1594

Confidential
Step 10 Configure LRADC_CTRL[LRADC_HOLD_KEY_EN] to 1.
Step 11 Read the corresponding key voltage value from LRADC_DATA when the CPU receives the
LRADC interrupt.
18.13.6.5

Calculation Formula

Calculation formula: LRADC_DATA = Vin/VREF*63, VREF=1.35 V

18.14 GPIO
18.14.1 Overview
The general purpose input/output (GPIO) is one of the blocks controlling the chip multiplexing
pins. Each pin can be configured as input or output and these pins are used to generate input
signals or output signals for special purposes.
The GPIO has the following features:


11 groups of ports (PB, PC, PD, PE, PF, PG, PH, PJ, PK, PL, PM)



Software control for each signal pin



Each GPIO peripheral can produce an interrupt



Pull-up/Pull-down/no-Pull register control



Control the direction of every signal



4 drive strengths in each operating mode



Up to 159 interrupts



Configurable interrupt edges

The following figure shows the block diagram of the GPIO.

The overall I/O ports consists of the digital part (GPIO, peripheral interfaces) and IO analog part
(output buffer, pull up/down, pad). The output of digital part can be selected by MUX, and the
analog part can be used to configure pull-up/pull-down registers, driving strengths and so on.

When in the read operation, read the current pin level to the APB bus. When not in the read
operation, the external pins aren’t connected to the APB bus, which is called the
high-impedance state.

Table 18-41 Port Function

18.14.3.3

Pull-up, Pull-down, and High-impedance Input

Each IO can be configured as the internal pull-up, pull-down, or high-impedance input mode.
Figure 18-75 Pull-up, Pull-down, and High-impedance Input Mode
VCC

Rpu
PAD

Rpd

GND

High-impedance: The output port is in the floating status. All the drives are turned off, and their
levels are depended by the external levels.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential
Pull-up: The uncertain signals are pulled high by resistors, which performs the current-limiting
function. In pull-up status, the IO is pulled up to VCC by Rpu.
Pull-down: The uncertain signals are pulled low by resistors. In pull-down status, the IO is pulled
down to GND by Rpd.

NOTE
The pull-up/down resistor value of each IO is around 100K.
Whether pull-down, pull-up or high-impedance input is decided by the external circuit.

18.14.3.4

Output Driving Strength

Each IO can be set as different output driving strength. The IO driving strength diagram is as
follows.
Figure 18-76 IO Buffer Strength Diagram
VCC

P0

P1

P2

P3

ro ro ro ro

ro ro ro ro
n0 n1 n2 n3
GND

High Level Output
In the process of high level output, the n0, n1, n2, n3 of NMOS is off, and the p0, p1, p2, p3 of
PMOS is on.
When the driving strength is set to 0, only the p0 is turned on, during which the output
impedance is maximum, that is, the driving capability is the weakest. The output impedance is
the turned-on r0.
When the driving strength is set to 1, only the p0 and p1 are turned on. The output impedance is
r0/2, equivalent to the parallel-connected two r0.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential
When the driving strength is set to 2, three MOS of p0-p3 are turned on. The output impedance is
r0/3, equivalent to the parallel-connected three p0.
When the driving strength is set to 3, p0-p3 are turned on. The output impedance is r0/4,
equivalent to the parallel-connected four p0.

Low Level Output
In the process of low level output, the p0, p1, p2, p3 of PMOS is off, and the n0, n1, n2, n3 of
NMOS is on.
When the driving strength is set to 0, only the n0 is turned on, during which the output
impedance is maximum, that is, the driving capability is the weakest. The output impedance is
the turned-on r0.
When the driving strength is set to 1, only the n0 and n1 are turned on. The output impedance is
r0/2, equivalent to the parallel-connected two r0.
When the driving strength is set to 2, three MOS of n0-n3 are turned on. The output impedance is
r0/3, equivalent to the parallel-connected three r0.
When the driving strength is set to 3, n0-n3 are turned on. The output impedance is r0/4,
equivalent to the parallel-connected four r0.

NOTE
a)

No matter what kind of driver strength it is, r0 typical value is 200Ω when voltage is 3.3V and
it is 100Ω when voltage is 1.8V.

b)

When GPIO is configured as input or interrupt functions, the output driver circuit is
unconnected to port. Then, driver configuration is invalid.

18.14.3.5

Interrupts

There is an interrupt number for each group of IO, in which all IOs share one interrupt number.
When an IO generates interrupts, the collector will send interrupt request to GIC. The user can
query which IO generates interrupt in the external interrupt status registers. The following
interrupt diagram takes PB as an example.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential
Figure 18-77 GPIOB Interrupt Diagram
PB0 interrups

Interrupt Trigger

PB1 interrupts

PB2 interrupts

GIC

GPIOB interrupts

Interrupt Trigger

Interrupt Trigger

PB0

PB1

PB2

Controller

PBn interrputs

Interrupt Trigger

PBn

The interrupt trigger of GPIO supports the following trigger types.


Positive Edge: When a low level changes to a high level, the IO will generate interrupts.



Negative Edge: When a high level changes to a low level, the IO will generate interrupts.



High Level: The IO will generate interrupts in the high level.



Low Level: The IO will generate interrupts in the low level.



Double Edge: The IO will generate interrupts both in the positive edge and negative edge.

The interrupt trigger types can be configured in the external interrupt configure registers.
The GPIO interrupts support hardware debounce function configuration in the external interrupt
debounce Registers. In this way, the trigger signal will be sampled with a lower-frequency
sample clock. As the dither frequency of signals is higher than their sample frequency, the
debounce effect is reached.
The sample clock source can be set in the GPIO_INT_CLK_SELECT, and the prescale factor can be
set in DEB_CLK_PRE_SCALE.
18.14.3.6

GPIO Group Withstand Voltage

Before using GPIO, you need to read the voltage in the GPIO Group Power Value Register. If it is 1,
the power supply is 3.3V; in this condition, no voltage setting is needed. If it is 0, the power
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential
supply is 1.8V; in this condition, the withstand voltage needs to be set in the GPIO Group Power
Voltage Select Control Register.
If it is 0 in the GPIO Group Power Voltage Select Control Register, the GPIO group power supply
will be set as 1.8V.
If it is 1 in the GPIO Group Power Voltage Select Control Register, the GPIO group power supply
will be set as 3.3V.
If it is 2 in the GPIO Group Power Voltage Select Control Register, the GPIO group enters the
adaptive mode. Their withstand voltage will be auto adjusted based on the detected GPIO
voltage.

18.14.4 Programming Guidelines
18.14.4.1

Disabling I/O Pins

To disable I/O pins, follow the steps as below.
Step 1

Write 1111 to the Px_SELECT of the Px_CFG register to disable the I/O pins.

Step 2

If needed, set the pull-up/pull-down status of the I/O pins by setting the Px_PULL
register. In the pull-up status, the pin level is 1 by default; in the pull-down status, the
pin level is 0 by default.

18.14.4.2

Input Configuration

To configure I/O pins as the general input pins, follow the steps as below.
Step 1

Write 0 to the Px_SELECT of the Px_CFG register to enable input function.

Step 2

If needed, set the pull-up/pull-down status of the I/O pins by setting the Px_PULL
register. When the I/O pins are externally driven, the external input value can be read;
When the I/O pins are not externally driven, the pin statuses are 1 (pull-up) or 0
(pull-down).

Step 3
18.14.4.3

Read the pin status in the Px_DAT register.

Output Configuration

To configure I/O pins as the general output pins, follow the steps as below.
Step 1

Write 1 to the Px_SELECT of the Px_CFG register to enable output function.

Step 2

If needed, configure the Px_DRV register to set the output driving strength. When it is set
as 11, the driving strength is maximum; when it is set as 0, the driving strength is
minimum. It is set as 1 by default.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential
Step 3

If needed, configure the Px_PULL register to set the pull-up and pull-down status. When
the output function is enabled, the I/O pin status are the same as the output signals;
when the output function is disabled, the pin statuses are 1 (pull-up) or 0 (pull-down).

Step 4

Write to Px_DAT register or output 1 or 0 to I/O pins through atomic operation.

Step 5

During the atomic operation, write 1 to the corresponding bits in Px_DAT_SET. Writing 1
to corresponding bits in Px_DAT_CLR will clear them.

18.14.4.4

Interrupt Configuration

To configure I/O pins as the interrupt pins, follow the steps as below.
Step 1

Write 1110 to the Px_SELECT of the Px_CFG register to enable the interrupt function.

Step 2

If needed, set the pull-up/pull-down status of the I/O pins by setting the Px_PULL
register. In the pull-up status, the interrupt input level is 1 by default in case of no
driving strength. In the pull-down status, the interrupt input level is 0 by default in case
of no driving strength.

Step 3

Set the interrupt trigger types in the Px_INT_CFG register.

Step 4

Set the debounce clock in the Px_INT_CFG register.

Step 5

Clear the IRQ pending status in the Px_INT_STA register.

Step 6

Enable external interrupts in the Px_INT_CTL register.

Step 7

After receiving interrupts, CPU will handle them. After that, the pending status of
interrupts can be cleared in the Px_INT_STA register.

Step 8

Disable external interrupts in the Px_INT_CTL register in case no interrupts are needed.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential

NOTE
a) It is not recommended to switch functions through PX_CFG in the interrupt mode. As the pins
are in the input state, their input levels can be read in the PX_DAT.
b) Disable the interrupts in the PX_INT_CTL before configuring new functions during the function
switches. Before switching back to the interrupt functions, clear the pending states in the
PX_INT_STA.
c) If the interrupts aren’t disabled in the course of function switches, an interrupt will be
mistakenly triggered.
18.14.4.5

Multi-Function Configuration

To configure I/O pins as the multiplexing function pins, follow the steps as below.
Step 1

Set the pin as the needed function through the Px_SELECT bit of the Px_CFG register.

Step 2

Set the driving strength in the Px_DRV register according to the selected function.

Step 3

Set the pull-up/down status in the Px_PLL register according to the selected function.
When the I/O pins are driven, the I/O pin status are the same as the output signals; when
the output function are not driven, the pin statuses are 1 (pull-up) or 0 (pull-down).

18.14.4.6

Power Configuration

Configuring Group Power Voltage
The SoC only supports setting group power voltage in PF ports, which is able to be set as 3.3 V or
1.8V by configuring GPIO_POW_VAL_SET_CTL. The group power voltage in other ports is
unconfigurable and depended on peripheral circuits.
Configuring Group Withstand Voltage
Configuring group withstand voltage intends to ensure that the internal withstand circuit voltage
is consistent with group voltage. There are two modes, adaptive mode and manual mode, for
users. In the SoC, the GPIO groups are configured as adaptive mode by default. When the
power-up completes, the groups can be re-configured.
The following steps describe how to configure group withstand voltage.


Adaptive Mode

In adaptive mode, each bit is set as 10 in GPIO_POW_MOD_SEL. The internal withstand circuit
will adjust group withstand mode automatically depending on the detected GPIO voltage.


Manual Mode

Step 4

Read the GPIO_POW_VAL to obtain the voltage statuses of GPIO group.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential
Step 5

Configure the GPIO_POW_MOD_SEL to keep the voltage statuses of corresponding bits
consistent with the those of GPIO groups. Specifically, when the voltage value of GPIO
group is 1.8V, configure the corresponding bit as 0; when the voltage value of GPIO
group is 3.3V, configure the corresponding bit as 1.

PD_DAT
PD Data.
If the port is configured as input, the
corresponding bit is the pin state. If the port

23:0

R/W

0

is configured as output, the pin state is the

value is the value setup by software. If the
port is configured as functional pin, the
undefined value will be read.

PE Data.

15:0

is configured as output, the pin state is the

18.15 LEDC
18.15.1 Overview
The LEDC is used to control the external LED lamp.
The LEDC has the following features:


Configurable LED output high-/low-level width



Configurable LED reset time



LEDC data supports DMA configuration mode and CPU configuration mode



Maximum 1024 LEDs serial connect



LED data transfer rate up to 800 kbit/s



Configurable RGB display mode

18.15.2 Block Diagram
The following figure shows a block diagram of the LEDC.
Figure 18-78 LEDC Block Diagram

Table 18-42 LEDC Sub-blocks

Data_trans

The input data is transferred to 0 and 1.

LEDC Data Transfer

The LEDC supports DMA data transfer mode and CPU data transfer mode through APB bus.


Data transfer in DMA mode

When the valid space of internal FIFO is greater than the setting FIFO space threshold, the LEDC
will send the DMA_REQ to require DMA to transfer data from DRAM to LEDC. The maximum data

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential
transfer size in DMA mode is 16 words. (The internal FIFO level is 32.) The DMA data transfer
mode is set by LEDC_DMA_EN.


Data transfer in CPU mode

When the valid space of internal FIFO is greater than the setting FIFO space threshold, the LEDC
will send LEDC_CPUREQ_INT to require CPU to transfer data to LEDC. The transfer data size in
CPU mode is controlled by software. The internal FIFO destination address is 0x06700014. The
data width is 32-bit. (The lower 24-bit is valid.)
18.15.5.5

LEDC Interrupt

Interrupt Name

Description
FIFO overflow interrupt.
The amount of written data exceeds the maximum storage
space of LED FIFO. The LEDC is in the data loss state. At this
time, the anomaly should be handled by software as follows.

FIFO_OVERFLOW_INT

a)

Query the LED_FIFO_DATA_REG to determine which

data has been stored in the internal FIFO of LEDC. Resend
the overflow data to LEDC.
b)

Soft_reset the LEDC to refresh all the data.

Wait Data Timeout Interrupt
When internal FIFO of LEDC cannot get data resulting from
some anomaly, the timeout interrupt will be enabled after
the led_wait_data_time. At this time, the LEDC is in
WAIT_DATA state, and the LEDC will output the level
WAITDATA_TIMEOUT_INT

configured by the LED_PAUSE_LEVEL. During the wait_data,
the LEDC will continue to transfer data. In this condition, if
LEDC waiting time exceeds the LED reset time, it is as if the
LEDC has sent a reset operation. The LED will enter
refreshing state by mistake, and the data hasn’t been
completely sent.
FIFO Request CPU Data Interrupt

FIFO_CPUREQ_INT

When FIFO data amount is less than the threshold, the
interrupt will be reported to the CPU.
Data Transfer Finish Interrupt

LEDC_TRANS_FINISH_INT

It indicates that the configured data of total_data_length
finishes transfer.

LEDC interrupt usage scenario:


CPU mode

The software can enable GLOBAL_INT_EN, FIFO_CPUREQ_INT_EN, WAITDATA_TIMEOUT_INT_EN,
FIFO_OVERFLOW_INT_EN, and LED_TRANS_FINISH_INT_EN in the LEDC_INTERRUPT_CTRL_REG,
and cooperate with LEDC_FIFO_TRIG_LEVEL in the LEDC_DMA_CTRL_REG to use. When

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential
FIFO_CPUREQ_INT is set to 1, the software can configure data of LEDC_FIFO_TRIG_LEVEL to
LEDC.


DMA mode

The

software

can

enable

FIFO_OVERFLOW_INT_EN,

and

LEDC_INTERRUPT_CTRL_REG,

and

GLOBAL_INT_EN,

WAITDATA_TIMEOUT_INT_EN,

LEDC_TRANS_FINISH_INT_EN
cooperate

with

in

LEDC_FIFO_TRIG_LEVEL

the
in

the

LEDC_DMA_CTRL_REG to use. After receiving LEDC DMA_REQ, DMA can transfer data of
LEDC_FIFO_TRIG_LEVEL to LEDC.

18.15.6 Programming Guidelines
18.15.6.1

Normal Configuration

Step 1

Configure LEDC_CLK and bus pclk as described in the section CCU.

Step 2

Configure the LEDC data to be written.

Step 3

Configure 0-code, 1-code, reset time, LEDC wait time, and the number of connected LED
and the threshold of DMA transferred data by setting LED_T01_TIMING_CTRL_REG,
LEDC_DATA_FINISH_CNT_REG,

LED_RESET_TIMING_CTRL_REG,

LEDC_WAIT_TIME0_CTRL_REG, LEDC_DMA_CTRL_REG, LEDC_INTERRUPT_CTRL_REG.
Step 4

Enable LEDC_EN through LEDC_CTRL_REG. The LEDC will start outputting data.

Step 5

When the LED_TRANS_FINISH_INT_EN in LEDC_INTERRUPT_CTRL_REG is enabled, it
indicates the configured data has been transferred. Then, LED_EN will be set to 0, and
the read/write point of LEDC FIFO is cleared.

Step 6

Repeat the first four steps to start a new round of configuration, and enable LEDC_EN.
The LEDC will restart data transfer.

18.15.6.2

Abnormal Processing

WAITDATA_TIMEOUT
Step 1

When a WAITDATA_TIMEOUT_INT occurs, it indicates the internal FIFO data request of
LEDC doesn’t obtain a response. In this condition, if the default output level is low, the
external LED device will mistakenly believe it is a reset operation, resulting in refreshing
LED data by mistake.

Step 2

Write 1 to LEDC_SOFT_RESET in the LEDC_CTRL_REG to reset the LEDC by software.
Afterwards, LEDC_EN will be automatically disabled. All the status registers will go back
to the idle status. LEDC FIFO read &write point are cleared to 0. LEDC The interrupts are
cleared.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential
Step 3

Write 1 to RESET_LED_EN in the LEDC_CTRL_REG. The LEDC will send the reset order to
ensure the external LED lights stay in the right status.

Step 4

Read the RESET_LED_EN in the LEDC_CTRL_REG. 1 indicates that LEDC hasn’t sent the
reset order. 0 indicates that LEDC has sent the reset order.

Step 5

When the LEDC reset operation finishes, the LEDC will restart the configuration of data
and registers. The data transfer starts again.

18.16 CIR Receiver (IR_RX)
18.16.1 Overview
The Consumer Infrared (CIR) receiver captures pulse from the IR Receiver module and uses the
Run-Length Code (RLC) to encode the pulse.
The CIR receiver has the following features:


One IR_RX interface in CPUX domain and one IR_RX interface in CPUS domain



Supports CIR for remote control



64x8 bits FIFO for data buffer



Sample clock up to 1 MHz

18.16.2 Block Diagram
Figure 18-88 CIR Receiver Block Diagram
IRQ

APB

REG

FIFO

CIR_RX LOGIC

CIR_RX

SCLK

The CIR receiver samples the input signal on the programmable frequency and records these
samples into RX FIFO when one CIR signal is found on the air. The CIR receiver uses Run-Length
Code (RLC) to encode pulse width. The encoded data is buffered in 64 levels and 8-bit width RX
FIFO; the MSB bit is used to record the polarity of the receiving CIR signal, the rest 7 bits are used
for the length of RLC. The maximum length of the RLC is 128. If the duration of one level (high or
low level) is more than 128, another byte is used.

NEC mode
Figure 18-89 A typical Pulse Train of the NEC

MSB

The CIR receiver module is a timer with a capture function.
When CIR_RX signals satisfy the Active Threshold (ATHR), the CIR receiver starts capturing. The
signals whose pulse width less than Noise Threshold (NTHR) will be ignored. When the signals
satisfy Idle Threshold (ITHR), the capture process will be stopped and the Receiver Packet End
interrupt will be generated, then the Receiver Packet End Flag will be asserted.
In a capture process, every effective pulse is buffered to FIFO in bytes according to the form of
the Run-Length Code. The MSB bit of a byte indicates the polarity of pulse, and the rest 7 bits
indicate the pulse width by taking Sample Clock as a basic unit. This is the code form of the
RLC-Byte. When the level changes or the pulse width counter overflows, the RLC-Byte is buffered
to FIFO. Afterwards, the CIR_RX module receives the infrared signals transmitted by the infrared
remote control, the software decodes the signals.
Sample Clock
Figure 18-90 Logical 0 and Logical 1 of NEC Protocol
560us

560us

560us
Logical 0

1690us
Logical 1

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential
For NEC protocol, a logical "1" takes 2.25 ms (560 us+1680 us) to transmit, while a logical "0" only
takes 1.12 ms (560 us+560 us) to transmit.
For example, if the sample clock frequency is 31.25 kHz, and a sample cycle is 32 us, then 18
sample cycles are 560 us. So the RLC of 560 us low level is 0x12 (b’00010010), the RLC of 560 us
high level is 0x92 (b’10010010). For instance, a logical “1” will samples 0x12 (b’00010010)
and 0xb5 (b’10110101), of which bit 7 indicates level, and bit 6 indicates sampling cycles.
Therefore, 00010010（0x12）indicates 18 sampling cycles of low level (approximately 560 us).
Active Threshold (ATHR)
When the CIR receiver is in the idle state, if the electrical level of the IR_RX signal changes
(positive jump or negative jump), and the duration reaches this threshold, then the CIR receiver
takes the starting of the signal as a lead code. It turns into an active state and starts to capture
IR_RX signals.

18.17 CIR Transmitter (IR_TX)
18.17.1 Overview
The CIR transmitter (IR_TX) transfer arbitrary waves which can be modulated with configurable
carrier waves such as 38 kHz. IR_TX only uses lower 8 bits of the 32-bit registers, and stores a
16-bit number in 2 registers, where one register contains the higher 8 bits while the other
contains the lower 8 bits.
The IR_TX has the following features:


One IR_TX interface in CPUX domain



Supports industry-standard AMBA Peripheral Bus (APB) and it is fully compliant with the
AMBA Specification, Revision 2.0



Full physical layer implementation



Arbitrary wave generator



Configurable carrier frequency



Handshake mode and waiting mode of DMA



128 bytes FIFO for data buffer



Supports Interrupts and DMA

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential

18.17.5 Functional Description
The IR_TX is used to generate a waveform of arbitrary length, arbitrary shape, and no high-speed
requirement, and it can change the data into the high-/low-level sequence of a certain length.
Every data is transmitted in bytes, the Bit[7] of a byte means whether the level of a transmitting
wave is high or low, the Bit[6:0] is the length of this wave. If the current transmitting
frequency-division is 1, 0x88 is a high level of 8 cycles, 0x08 is a low level of 8 cycles. If the current
transmitting frequency-division is 4, 0x88 is a high level of 32 cycles, 0x08 is a low level of 32
cycles.
The IR_TX has two transmission modes: non-cycle transmission and cycle transmission.
The non-cycle transmission is to transmit all the data in TX_FIFO until the FIFO is empty.
The cycle transmission is to transmit all the data in TX_FIFO; after the transmission completion,
wait for a certain time to recover the data in TX_FIFO and then send it until a stop signal is
detected. The data recovery in FIFO is implemented by clearing the read pointer.
Timing Diagram
The IR remote control contains many protocols designed by different manufacturers. Here take
NEC protocol as an example, the IR_TX module uses a variable pulse-width modulation
technique to encompass the various formats of infrared encoding for remote-control
applications. A message is started by a 9 ms AGC burst, which is used to set the gain of the earlier
CIR receivers. This AGC burst is then followed by a 4.5 ms space, which is then followed by the
address and command.
Bit definition: the logical “1” takes 2.25 ms to transmit, while a logical “0” is only 1.12 ms.
Figure 18-96 Definitions of Logical “1” and Logical “0”

19 Security
19.1

Crypto Engine (CE)

19.1.1

Overview
The Crypto Engine (CE) module is one encryption/decryption algorithms accelerator. It supports
kinds of symmetric, asymmetric, HASH, and RBG algorithms. There are two software interfaces
for secure and non-secure world each. Algorithm control information is written in memory by
task descriptor, then CE automatically reads it when executing request. It supports parallel
requests from 4 channels each world and 4 different types of algorithms simultaneously. This
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential
module also has an internal DMA controller to transfer data between CE and memory. It supports
parallel running for symmetric, HASH, asymmetric algorithms.
The CE has the following features:


Symmetrical algorithm:
-

-





AES symmetrical algorithm


Key size: 128/192/256 bits (not XTS), 256/512 bits (XTS)



CFB mode includes: CFB1, CFB8, CFB64, and CFB128



CTR mode includes: CTR16, CTR32, CTR64, and CTR128



Supports ECB, CBC, CTS, OFB, CBC-MAC, GCM, and XTS modes

DES symmetrical algorithm


CTR mode, includes: CTR16, CTR32, and CTR64



Supports ECB, CBC, and CBC-MAC mode

-

Supports 3DES

-

SM4 symmetrical algorithm supports ECB and CBC mode

-

Supports RC4

Hash algorithms
-

Supports MD5, SHA1, SHA224, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512, and SM3

-

Supports HMAC-SHA1, HMAC-SHA256

-

Supports multi-package1 mode for these ones

-

Supports hardware padding

Random bit generator algorithms
-

Supports PRNG, 175 bits seed width, and output with multiple of 5 words

-

Supports TRNG, post-process by hardware with SHA256, output with multiple of 8 words

-

Supports TRNG single/double entropy source mode

-

Supports TRNG healthy test

-

Supports Instantiate/Reseed/Generate/Uninstantiate 4 process

-

Supports prediction resistance requests

-

Supports 8 separate suits of Internal State

-

Maxim 2^32 BYTE length of Entropy input, Nonce, Personalization, Additional input. And
length is multiple of word

Security Strategy and System Feature

Symmetric, asymmetric, HASH/RBG ctrl logics are separate, can handle task

through its own interface, don’t know each other’s existence.

Each world has 4 channels for software request, each channel has an interrupt control
and status bit, and channels are independent with each other.

19.1.4.3

ECB Mode
The ECB mode is a confidentiality mode that features, for a given key, the assignment of a fixed
ciphertext block to each plaintext block, analogous to the assignment of code words in a
codebook.
In ECB mode, encryption and decryption algorithms are directly applied to the block data. The
operation of each block is independent, so the plaintext encryption and ciphertext decryption
can be performed concurrently.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential

19.1.4.4

Key

CBC Mode
The CBC mode is a confidentiality mode whose encryption process features the combining of the
plaintext blocks with the previous ciphertext blocks. The CBC mode requires an initialization
vector (IV) to combine with the first plaintext block. The encryption process of each plaintext
block is related to the block processing result of the previous ciphertext blocks, so encryption
operations cannot be concurrently performed in CBC mode. The decryption operation is
independent of output plain text of the previous block, so decryption operations can be
performed concurrently.

19.1.4.5

CTR Mode
The CTR mode is a confidentiality mode that features the application of the forward cipher to a
set of input blocks, called counters, to produce a sequence of output blocks that are
exclusive-ORed with the plaintext to produce the ciphertext, and vice versa. All of the counters
must be distinct.

19.1.4.6

CFB Mode
The CFB mode is a confidentiality mode that features the feedback of successive ciphertext
segments into the input blocks of the forward cipher to generate output blocks that are
exclusive-ORed with the plaintext to produce the ciphertext, and vice versa. The CFB mode
requires an IV as the initial input block, and the forward cipher operation is applied to the IV to
produce the first output block. The first ciphertext segment is produced by exclusive-ORing the
first plaintext segment with the s most significant bits of the first output block. The value of s is 1
bit, 8 bits, 64 bits, or 128 bits.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

19.1.4.7

OFB Mode
The OFB mode is a confidentiality mode that features the iteration of the forward cipher on an IV
to generate a sequence of output blocks that are exclusive-ORed with the plaintext to produce
the ciphertext, and vice versa. If a same key is used, different IVs must be used to ensure
operation security.

19.1.4.9

HASH Algorithm
The hash algorithms support MD5, SHA1, SHA224, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512, HMAC-SHA1, and
HMAC-SHA256. All algorithms are iterative, one-way hash functions that can process a message
to produce a condensed representation called a message digest. When a message is received,
the message digest can be used to verify whether the data has changed, that is, to verify its
integrity.
The hash algorithm of the CE supports block-aligned total length of the input data (padded by
software), that is, a multiple of 64 bytes. The message length after padding by software is used as
the configured data length for the hash algorithm.

19.1.4.10

RSA Algorithm

The RSA is a public key encryption/decryption algorithm implemented through the modular
exponentiation operation.
The ciphertext is obtained as follows: C = ME mod N. The plaintext is obtained as follows: M = CD
mod N.
M indicates the plaintext, C indicates the ciphertext, (N, E) indicates the public key, and (N, D)
indicates the private key.

Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential
19.1.4.11

Storing Message

In the application, a message may not be stored contiguously in the memory, but divided into
multiple segments. Or a piece of continuously stored messages can be artificially split into
multiple pieces as needs. Then each segment corresponds to a set of the source address and
source length in the descriptor. Multiple segments correspond to groups 0-7 source
address/source length in sequence.
Each task supports up to 8 message segments, and the data volume of each message segment
supports up to 4 GWord (AES-CTS is 1 GByte). The total amount of all segments in a task (that is a
package) supports up to 4 GWord (AES-CTS is 1 GByte). If a message is divided into multiple
packages, all others are required to be whole words; when the last package of AES-CTS is less
than one word, 0 needs to be padded, and those less than one word are counted as one word.
The following figure shows the address order structure.
Figure 19-12 Word Address of Message

filled first. The following figure shows the byte order structure (blue means it is filled by the
message).
Figure 19-13 Byte Order

19.1.4.13

Storing IV

For different algorithms, the length of IV is different. But they are integer multiples of word. To
keep the byte order of IV and HASH digest output consistent, the byte order of IV is different from
that of the message. For the multi-packet operation, the first address of the digest output result
of the previous HASH can be directly configured to the first address of the next IV, and the
software does not need to do any processing on the digest.

Task Descriptor of Hash Algorithms and RBG Algorithms

The task descriptor is data written by software to a continuous space in memory. The data
describes the various properties of a task, such as algorithm type, mode, subcommand, key
address, data source address, the data size read from data source, abstract destination address,
the written destination data size, and the information of other tasks. First, configure the task
descriptor by software; then operate the registers of CE to start this task. After the task starts, CE
will read task descriptor based on the address of the task descriptor configured in register, and
perform the task one time based on the described properties.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential
In applications, the “NEXT SG ADDR” field can be configured as the starting address of the next
SG descriptor to concatenate multi SG descriptors into a SG chain, thereby realizing multiple SG
functions. In addition, the “NEXT TASK ADDR” field can be configured as the starting address of
the next task descriptor to concatenate multi task descriptors into a SG chain, thereby realizing
multiple task functions. Multiple SGs and tasks can be randomly configured. After the first take is
initiated, CE will sequentially execute each SG among the tasks until NEXT SG ADDR”and“NEXT
TASK ADDR”field is invalid.
The HASH/RBG algorithms and Symmetrical/Asymmetrical algorithms use different descriptor
structures, as shown below.
Figure 19-17 Task Chaining of Hash Algorithms and Random Bit Generator Algorithms

next task field should be set to 0 when no next task, else set to next task’s descriptor.
19.1.4.16

PKC Microcode

PKC module supports RSA, ECC, SM2 algorithms in the form of microcode. It implements basic
modular add, minus, multiplication, point add, point double, and logic computing, etc.
Complete RSA/ECC/SM2 encryption, decryption, sign, verify are implemented with these
microcodes.
Asymmetric algorithms RSA/ECC/SM2 are implemented as microcode in PKC module. The
encryption, decryption, sign, verify operations of asymmetric algorithms are composed with
certain fixed microcodes with hardware.
19.1.4.17

PKC Configuration

Before starting PKC, task description must be configured. Parameters to PKC are assigned to
source sg, outcome is put to destination sg.
For RSA, parameters should be at the order of key, modulus, plaintext.
For ECC point add P2 = P0 + P1, parameters should be at the order of p, P0x, P0y, P1x, P1y.
Output is at the order of P2x, P2y.
For ECC point double P2 = 2*P0, parameters should be at the order of p, a, P0x, P0y. Output is at
the order of P2x, P2y.
For ECC point multiplication P2 = k*P0, parameters should be at the order of p, k, a, P0x, P0y.
Output is at the order of P2x, P2y.
Copyright©2025 Allwinner Technology Co.,Ltd. All Rights Reserved.

Confidential
For ECC point verification, parameters should be at the order of p, a, P0x, P0y, b. Output is 1 or 0.
For ECC encryption, parameters should be at the order of random k, p, a, Gx, Gy, Qx, Qy, m.
Output is at the order of Rx, Ry, c.
For ECC decryption, parameters should be at the order of random k, p, a, Rx, Ry, c. Output is m.
For ECC signature, parameters should be at the order of random k, p, a, Gx, Gy, n, d, e. Output is
at the order of r, s.
For ECC signature verification, parameters should be at the order of n, s, e, r, p, a, Gx, Gy, Qx, Qy,
n, r. Output is 1 or 0.
19.1.4.18

Error Check

After CE reads the task descriptor, CE can monitor error during algorithm operation. When the
error is monitored, CE will do the following operations:
The task will pause immediately
Generates interrupt
The corresponding channel of the task status register is Fail
The corresponding channel bit of error status register can be read error number
The error number has the following types.
Code
0x01
0x11
0x21
0x31
